5.10.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
ānarttādhipatirbhūpaścamatkāra iti smṛtaḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare prāptastatra haṃtuṃ vane mṛgān .....
sa dadarśa mṛgīṃ dūrānniścalāṃgīṃ taroradhaḥ ..
stanaṃ sutāya yacchaṃtīṃ viśvastāmakutobhayām .. 2 ..
5.10.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
आनर्त्ताधिपतिर्भूपश्चमत्कार इति स्मृतः ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तस्तत्र हंतुं वने मृगान् .....
स ददर्श मृगीं दूरान्निश्चलांगीं तरोरधः ..
स्तनं सुताय यच्छंतीं विश्वस्तामकुतोभयाम् .. 2 ..
5.10.m:
Sūta said:
A king of Ānarta, known as Camatkāra,
arrived there in the forest at that time to slay deer.
From afar he saw a doe, motionless beneath a tree,
giving her teat to her fawn, trusting and without fear of anything.

5.10.s:
atha tāṃ pārthivastūrṇaṃ śareṇānataparvaṇā ..
jaghānākarṇakṛṣṭena marmasthāne praharṣitaḥ .. 3 ..
5.10.d:
अथ तां पार्थिवस्तूर्णं शरेणानतपर्वणा ..
जघानाकर्णकृष्टेन मर्मस्थाने प्रहर्षितः .. 3 ..
5.10.m:
Then the king swiftly, with a straight-jointed arrow
drawn to his ear, struck her in a vital spot, full of joy.

5.10.s:
sahasā sā hatā tena gārddhrapatreṇa patriṇā ..
diśo vilokayāmāsa samaṃtādvyathayārditā .. 4 ..
5.10.d:
सहसा सा हता तेन गार्द्ध्रपत्रेण पत्रिणा ..
दिशो विलोकयामास समंताद्व्यथयार्दिता .. 4 ..
5.10.m:
Instantly struck by that vulture-feathered arrow,
she looked in every direction all around, tormented by pain.

5.10.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā mahīpālaṃ nātidūre dhanurdharam ..
provācāśrupariklinnavadanā sutavatsalā .. 5 ..
5.10.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा महीपालं नातिदूरे धनुर्धरम् ..
प्रोवाचाश्रुपरिक्लिन्नवदना सुतवत्सला .. 5 ..
5.10.m:
Then, seeing the ruler of the earth nearby bearing a bow,
she spoke, her face drenched with tears, loving her fawn:

5.10.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
ayuktaṃ pṛthivīpāla yattvayaitadanuṣṭhitam ..
hatā'haṃ bālavatsā'dya śareṇānataparvaṇā ..6..
5.10.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
अयुक्तं पृथिवीपाल यत्त्वयैतदनुष्ठितम् ..
हताऽहं बालवत्साऽद्य शरेणानतपर्वणा ..6..
5.10.m:
The doe said:
It was improper, O protector of the earth, what you have done here:
I, whose young fawn is small, have been struck today with a straight-jointed arrow.

5.10.s:
nā'haṃ śocāmi bhūpāla maraṇaṃ svaśarīragam ..
yathemaṃ vālakaṃ dīnaṃ kṣīrāsvādanalaṃpaṭam .. 7 ..
5.10.d:
नाऽहं शोचामि भूपाल मरणं स्वशरीरगम् ..
यथेमं वालकं दीनं क्षीरास्वादनलंपटम् .. 7 ..
5.10.m:
I do not grieve, O king, for the death coming upon my own body,
as much as for this helpless fawn who craves the taste of milk.

5.10.s:
yasmāttvayedṛśaṃ karma nirdayaṃ samanuṣṭhitam ..
kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktastasmātsadyo bhaviṣyasi .. 8 ..
5.10.d:
यस्मात्त्वयेदृशं कर्म निर्दयं समनुष्ठितम् ..
कुष्ठव्याधिसमायुक्तस्तस्मात्सद्यो भविष्यसि .. 8 ..
5.10.m:
Since you have performed such a merciless deed,
you shall therefore immediately be afflicted with the disease of leprosy!

5.10.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
svadharma eṣa bhūpānāṃ kurvaṃti mṛgasaṃkṣayam ..
tasmātsvadharmasaṃyuktaṃ na māṃ tvaṃ śaptumarhasi .. 9 ..
5.10.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
स्वधर्म एष भूपानां कुर्वंति मृगसंक्षयम् ..
तस्मात्स्वधर्मसंयुक्तं न मां त्वं शप्तुमर्हसि .. 9 ..

5.10.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
satyametanmahīpāla yattvayā parikīrtitam ..
kṣattriyāṇāṃ vadhārthāya mṛgāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā .. 6.10.10..
5.10.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
सत्यमेतन्महीपाल यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम् ..
क्षत्त्रियाणां वधार्थाय मृगाः सृष्टाः स्वयंभुवा .. 6.10.10..
5.10.m:
The doe said:
It is true, O king, what you have declared:
deer were created by the self-manifest [Brahmā] for the slaughter of kṣatriyas.

5.10.s:
paraṃ tena vidhisteṣāṃkṛto yastaṃ mahīpate ..
śṛṇuṣvā'vahito bhūtvā vadaṃtyā mama sāṃpratam .. 11 ..
5.10.d:
परं तेन विधिस्तेषांकृतो यस्तं महीपते ..
शृणुष्वाऽवहितो भूत्वा वदंत्या मम सांप्रतम् .. 11 ..
5.10.m:
Yet hear attentively the rule concerning them which was laid down by him,
O king, as I speak it now:

5.10.s:
suptaṃ maithunasaṃyuktaṃ stanapānakriyodyatam ..
hatvā mṛgaṃ jalāsaktaṃ naraḥ pāpena lipyate .. 12 ..
5.10.d:
सुप्तं मैथुनसंयुक्तं स्तनपानक्रियोद्यतम् ..
हत्वा मृगं जलासक्तं नरः पापेन लिप्यते .. 12 ..
5.10.m:
Having slain a deer that is asleep, engaged in mating, devoted to the act of suckling,
or absorbed in drinking water, a man is tainted with sin.

5.10.s:
etasmātkāraṇācchāpastava datto mayā nṛpa ..
na kāmato na mṛtyorvā satyenātmānamālabhe .. 13 ..
5.10.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाच्छापस्तव दत्तो मया नृप ..
न कामतो न मृत्योर्वा सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. 13 ..
5.10.m:
For this reason the curse was pronounced upon you by me, O king;
neither out of passion nor out of fear of death—by the truth I swear upon my soul!

5.10.s:
evamuktvā mṛgī prāṇānsā mumoca vyathānvitā ..
kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktaḥ so'pi rājā babhūva ha .. 14 ..
5.10.d:
एवमुक्त्वा मृगी प्राणान्सा मुमोच व्यथान्विता ..
कुष्ठव्याधिसमायुक्तः सोऽपि राजा बभूव ह .. 14 ..
5.10.m:
Having spoken thus, the doe gave up her vital breaths, filled with pain;
and that king, indeed, became afflicted with the disease of leprosy.

5.10.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā kuṣṭhasaṃyuktaṃ pārthivaḥ svaṃ kalevaram..
tataḥ svānsevakānāha samāhūya suduḥkhitaḥ .. 15 ..
5.10.d:
स दृष्ट्वा कुष्ठसंयुक्तं पार्थिवः स्वं कलेवरम्..
ततः स्वान्सेवकानाह समाहूय सुदुःखितः .. 15 ..
5.10.m:
The king, seeing his own body covered with leprosy,
then summoned his servants and said, deeply sorrowful:

5.10.s:
ahaṃ tapaścariṣyāmi pūjayiṣyāmi śaṃkaram ..
tāvadyāvatpraṇāśo me kuṣṭhavyādherbhaviṣyati .. 16 ..
5.10.d:
अहं तपश्चरिष्यामि पूजयिष्यामि शंकरम् ..
तावद्यावत्प्रणाशो मे कुष्ठव्याधेर्भविष्यति .. 16 ..
5.10.m:
“I will perform austerity; I will worship Śaṃkara
until the destruction of my leprosy disease shall come to pass.

5.10.s:
yatkiṃcittriṣu lokeṣu prārthayaṃti narāḥ sukham ..
tatsarvaṃ tapasā sādhyaṃ tasmātkāryaṃ mayā tapaḥ .. 17 ..
adhunaiko'hamaikāhamekaikasminvanaspatau ..
caranbhaikṣaṃ tu niyamaiścariṣyāmi dharātale...8..
pāṃsunā samavacchanne śūnyāgāre pratiśrayaḥ ..
vṛkṣamūlanikete vā muktasarvapriyāpriyaḥ ...9..
5.10.d:
यत्किंचित्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयंति नराः सुखम् ..
तत्सर्वं तपसा साध्यं तस्मात्कार्यं मया तपः .. 17 ..
अधुनैकोऽहमैकाहमेकैकस्मिन्वनस्पतौ ..
चरन्भैक्षं तु नियमैश्चरिष्यामि धरातले...8..
पांसुना समवच्छन्ने शून्यागारे प्रतिश्रयः ..
वृक्षमूलनिकेते वा मुक्तसर्वप्रियाप्रियः ...9..
5.10.m:
Whatever happiness men pray for in the three worlds,
all that is to be attained by austerity; therefore austerity must be performed by me.
Now, alone, I shall wander on the earth under one tree each day,
living on begged food according to vows,
having my shelter in a deserted house covered over with dust
or at the root of a tree, freed from all likes and dislikes,

5.10.s:
samaḥ śatruṣu mitreṣu samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanaḥ ..
bhūtvā kālaṃ nayiṣyāmi yāvatkālasya saṃsthitiḥ ..6.10.20...
5.10.d:
समः शत्रुषु मित्रेषु समलोष्टाश्मकांचनः ..
भूत्वा कालं नयिष्यामि यावत्कालस्य संस्थितिः ..6.10.20...
5.10.m:
impartial toward enemies and friends, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal;
becoming such, I will spend my time for as long as life remains.”

5.10.s:
evaṃ tānsevakānbhūpaḥ so'bhidhāya visṛjya ca ..
tīrthayātrā paro bhūtvā babhrāma vasudhātale..21...
5.10.d:
एवं तान्सेवकान्भूपः सोऽभिधाय विसृज्य च ..
तीर्थयात्रा परो भूत्वा बभ्राम वसुधातले..21...
5.10.m:
Having thus spoken to those servants and dismissed them, the king,
dedicated to pilgrimage to sacred fords, wandered over the surface of the earth.

5.10.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā prāpya viprasamudbhavam ..
upadeśaṃ nṛpaḥ prāptaḥ śaṃkhatīrthaṃ mahodayam..22..
5.10.d:
ततः कालेन महता प्राप्य विप्रसमुद्भवम् ..
उपदेशं नृपः प्राप्तः शंखतीर्थं महोदयम्..22..
5.10.m:
Then, after a long time, having received instruction
originating from a brahmin, the king reached the magnificent Śaṅkhatīrtha,

5.10.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvavyādhivināśakam ..
vikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu pūritaṃ svacchavāriṇā .. 23 ..
5.10.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे सर्वव्याधिविनाशकम् ..
विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु पूरितं स्वच्छवारिणा .. 23 ..
5.10.m:
in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, the destroyer of all diseases,
renowned throughout the three worlds, filled with clear water.

5.10.s:
tatrā'sau snānamātreṇa tatkṣaṇātpārthivotamaḥ ..
kuṣṭhavyādhivi nirmuktaḥ saṃjātaḥ sumahādyutiḥ .. 24 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śaṃkhatīrthamāhātmye camatkāranṛpatikuṣṭhanivṛttivṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāma daśamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 10 .. .. cha ..
5.10.d:
तत्राऽसौ स्नानमात्रेण तत्क्षणात्पार्थिवोतमः ..
कुष्ठव्याधिवि निर्मुक्तः संजातः सुमहाद्युतिः .. 24 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शंखतीर्थमाहात्म्ये चमत्कारनृपतिकुष्ठनिवृत्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनाम दशमोऽध्यायः .. 10 .. .. छ ..
5.10.m:
There, by mere ritual ablution, at that very moment that best of kings
was completely freed from the disease of leprosy and became possessed of great splendor.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled “Description of the Story of the Relief of King Camatkāra's Leprosy in the Māhātmya of Śaṅkhatīrtha,” in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.11.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
camatkāraḥ kathaṃ rājā muktaḥ kuṣṭhena sūtaja ..
kathaṃ tena tapastaptaṃ kiyatkālaṃ ca bhūbhujā .. 1 ..
5.11.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
चमत्कारः कथं राजा मुक्तः कुष्ठेन सूतज ..
कथं तेन तपस्तप्तं कियत्कालं च भूभुजा .. 1 ..
5.11.m:
The seers said:
How was King Camatkāra freed from leprosy, O Sūta's son?
How was austerity performed by him, and for how long a time by that ruler of the earth?

5.11.s:
katame brāhmaṇāste vai śaṃkhatīrthaṃ pradarśitam ..
yaistasya rogamuktyarthaṃ duḥkhitasya mahātmanaḥ .. 2 ..
5.11.d:
कतमे ब्राह्मणास्ते वै शंखतीर्थं प्रदर्शितम् ..
यैस्तस्य रोगमुक्त्यर्थं दुःखितस्य महात्मनः .. 2 ..
5.11.m:
Which brahmins indeed were those by whom Śaṅkhatīrtha was pointed out
for the release from disease of that noble-minded, suffering one?

5.11.s:
katamaṃ śaṃkhatīrthaṃ tatkasminsthāne vyavasthitam ..
kiṃprabhāvaṃ ca niḥśeṣaṃ sarvaṃ vistarato vada .. 3 ..
5.11.d:
कतमं शंखतीर्थं तत्कस्मिन्स्थाने व्यवस्थितम् ..
किंप्रभावं च निःशेषं सर्वं विस्तरतो वद .. 3 ..
5.11.m:
Which one is that Śaṅkhatīrtha? In what place is it situated?
And what is its power? Relate it all in detail without omission.

5.11.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ manoharām ..
sarvapāpaharāṃ viprāścamatkāranṛpodbhavām .. 4 ..
5.11.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अहं वः कीर्तयिष्यामि कथामेतां मनोहराम् ..
सर्वपापहरां विप्राश्चमत्कारनृपोद्भवाम् .. 4 ..
5.11.m:
Sūta said:
I will tell you this captivating tale
that takes away all sins, O brahmins, concerning King Camatkāra.

5.11.s:
sa bhrāṃtaḥ sarvatīrthāni prabhāsādyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
tapasvī niyatāhāro bhikṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ ..5..
5.11.d:
स भ्रांतः सर्वतीर्थानि प्रभासाद्यानि कृत्स्नशः ..
तपस्वी नियताहारो भिक्षान्नकृतभोजनः ..5..
5.11.m:
He wandered to all the sacred fords, Prabhāsa and the rest, in their entirety,
an ascetic of restricted diet, taking his meals from begged food,

5.11.s:
pṛcchamāno bhiṣagmukhyānauṣadhāni muhurmuhuḥ ..
maṃtrānmaṃtravidaścaiva roganāśāya nityataḥ .. .. 6 ..
5.11.d:
पृच्छमानो भिषग्मुख्यानौषधानि मुहुर्मुहुः ..
मंत्रान्मंत्रविदश्चैव रोगनाशाय नित्यतः .. .. 6 ..
5.11.m:
continually questioning eminent physicians about remedies,
and also knowers of mantras about mantras, constantly for the destruction of the disease.

5.11.s:
na lebhe kiṃcidiṣṭaṃ vā sa maṃtraṃ bheṣajaṃ ca vā ..
tīrthaṃ vā nṛpaśārdūlo yena syādvyādhisaṃkṣayaḥ .. 7 ..
5.11.d:
न लेभे किंचिदिष्टं वा स मंत्रं भेषजं च वा ..
तीर्थं वा नृपशार्दूलो येन स्याद्व्याधिसंक्षयः .. 7 ..
5.11.m:
That tiger among kings obtained no desired mantra, nor medicine,
nor sacred ford by which the destruction of the disease might come about.

5.11.s:
tataśca pārthivaśreṣṭho vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ ..
ekākī yatacittātmā sarvasattvavirājite .. 97 ..
nivāsamakarottasminkṣetre puṇyatame ciram ..
śīrṇaparṇaphalāhāro bhūmau śete sadā niśi ..
anya syā'nyasya vṛkṣasya madāhaṃkāravarjitaḥ .. 9 ..
tataḥ katipayāhasya bhramamāṇo mahīpatiḥ ..
so'paśyadbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāṃstīrthayātrāśrayānbahūn .. 6.11.10 ..
tataḥ praṇamya tānviprānupaviṣṭāndharātale ..
viśvāmitrāśramasyāṃte provāca vinayānvitaḥ ......
.. rājovāca .. ..
ahaṃ nāmnā camatkāraḥ pārthivaḥ sūryavaṃśajaḥ ..
ānarttādhipatirvyāptaḥ kuṣṭhena dvijasattamāḥ ...2..
asti kaścidupāyo'tra daivo vā mānuṣo'pi vā ..
bheṣajaṃ vā'tha maṃtro vā yena kuṣṭhaṃ praśāmyati .. 13 ..
mamopari dayāṃ kṛtvā vadadhvaṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
kuṣṭhagrastaśarīraṃ ca paraṃ kṛcchramupāgatam ...4..
5.11.d:
ततश्च पार्थिवश्रेष्ठो वैराग्यं परमं गतः ..
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा सर्वसत्त्वविराजिते .. 97 ..
निवासमकरोत्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे पुण्यतमे चिरम् ..
शीर्णपर्णफलाहारो भूमौ शेते सदा निशि ..
अन्य स्याऽन्यस्य वृक्षस्य मदाहंकारवर्जितः .. 9 ..
ततः कतिपयाहस्य भ्रममाणो महीपतिः ..
सोऽपश्यद्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठांस्तीर्थयात्राश्रयान्बहून् .. 6.11.10 ..
ततः प्रणम्य तान्विप्रानुपविष्टान्धरातले ..

5.11.m:
And then that best of kings attained supreme detachment;
alone, with mind and self restrained, in that most holy sacred field,
splendid with all creatures, he made his dwelling for a long time,
eating withered leaves and fruits, always sleeping at night upon the ground
beneath one tree after another, free from pride and egoism.
Then, after a few days, as he was wandering, the ruler of the earth
saw many excellent brahmins engaged in pilgrimage to sacred fords.
Then, having bowed to those brahmins seated on the ground
adjacent to the hermitage of Viśvāmitra, he spoke full of humility:
The king said:
“By name I am Camatkāra, a king born of the solar dynasty,
the ruler of Ānarta, afflicted with leprosy, O best of the twice-born!
Is there any means here, whether divine or human,
or medicine, or mantra, by which leprosy is alleviated?
Taking pity upon me, speak, O best of the twice-born,
to one whose body is seized by leprosy and who has fallen into extreme distress.

Or if you do not know, I will abandon my body here,
having entered fire or water, or having consumed poison!”
Hearing those words of his, all those best of the twice-born,
filled with compassion, then spoke to that lord of the earth:
“O tiger among kings, not far from this place there is
[a sacred ford] known as Śaṅkhatīrtha, bringing about the destruction of all diseases.”
Men afflicted with disease, one-eyed, blind, and dumb, / deformed in limb, having extra limbs, ugly, and with distorted faces—
even they, having bathed there while fasting, at the beginning of the dark [fortnight] of Caitra, / when the moon is in Citrā, become instantly free of disease.
We have seen by the hundreds [those] with the radiance of twelve suns, / shaped like Kāmadeva, endowed with splendor and strength.
The king said: / How should I know Śaṅkhatīrtha, O best of brahmins? / And how did it arise? Tell me in detail.

5.11.m:
The brahmins said: / Long ago, on the surface of the earth, there was a foremost sage named Likhita, / the son of the sage Śāṇḍilya, endowed with austerity and strength.
Then his younger brother was born, named Śaṅkha, a knower of the law-books, / who lived on tubers, roots, and fruits, always established in austerity.
Once upon a time, Śaṅkha went to Likhita's hermitage / in search of sweet fruits, tormented by intense hunger.
Finding the hermitage of the great-souled Likhita empty, / he then took fruits, thinking them to be his own.
He ate many ripe and sweet [fruits]. / In the meantime, Likhita arrived accompanied by his disciples.
Seeing Śaṅkha holding the fruit, he said in anger:
O sinner, you have taken fruits not given by me! / Why, in the manner of a thief, did you not consider the consequences?

5.11.m:
Śaṅkha said: / What you have declared is true, O best of the twice-born. / The fruits were taken here in your lonely hermitage.
Therefore, mete out to me the proper punishment born of theft, / so that this world and the next may bring happiness to me.
Then, seized by anger, taking Śaṅkha’s hand in his hand, / he instantly cut it off, even though restrained by the ascetics.
Though his hand was severed, Śaṅkha performed exceedingly severe austerity; / having returned particularly to his own hermitage, he [did so] once again.
Then, after some time, Mahādeva, being pleased with him, / appeared and addressed that lord of sages, Śaṅkha.
Maheśvara said: / O sage, O great-hearted one, you have performed what is difficult to do! / Choose from me a boon desired in your heart.
Śaṅkha said: / If you are pleased with me, O God, and if you grant a boon, O Lord, / let both my hands become as they were again, O best of gods!

5.11.m:
Likewise, let this sacred ford bear my name, O best of gods, / renowned in all the worlds, removing all sins of men.
Whether one is deformed in limb or with extra limbs, or even afflicted with disease, / if he takes a ritual ablution here, may he quickly become completely renewed!
The Lord said: / This sacred ford will indeed be known by your name, / destroying the sins of embodied beings from this day forth, O chief of brahmins.
Whoever, whether deformed in limb or with extra limbs, shall take a ritual ablution here / without food in the bright [fortnight] of Caitra, when the moon is in Citrā, / will undoubtedly become golden-limbed and radiant.
If he has desires, O chief of brahmins, meditating on beauty of form, [he will attain it]; / or if free from desire, he will go to the supreme realm, which is identical to Śiva.
When a śrāddha is performed here on the fourteenth day when the moon is in Citrā, / the ancestors will attain supreme satisfaction, O holy one.
This very day, O tiger among brahmins, is the auspicious end of the bright fortnight of Caitra; / in the afternoon, the moon will enter its conjunction with Citrā.

5.11.m:
For one who is fasting there and has properly bathed, instantly / both hands will become beautiful, just as they were before.
Having spoken thus, the Lord then vanished from sight. / Śaṅkha, too, at the kutapa hour, then performed his ritual ablution there.
And then, at that very moment, his hands became as before: / resembling red lotuses, lovely, and marked with the sign of a fish.
The brahmins said: / In this way that sacred ford arose on the surface of the earth, O best of kings, / auspicious by the power of the god of gods who bears the crescent moon.
Therefore, O king of kings, you too perform a ritual ablution there / on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, when the moon is in Citrā.
There is no doubt you will become freed from all diseases. / We shall show it to you when the stated time arrives.
Sūta said: / Then, after a few days, the beginning of the dark fortnight of Caitra arrived, / and the fourteenth day occurred when the moon was in Citrā.

5.11.m:
Then those brahmins, taking the king along immediately, / wishing for his welfare, went toward Śaṅkhatīrtha.
Then, meditating in his mind on the destruction of the disease of leprosy, / he performed his ritual ablution according to rule, endowed with supreme faith.
Then, freed from leprosy, shining with the brilliance of twelve suns, / he emerged from that water filled with great joy.
Then, having bowed to all those brahmins who had mastered the Vedas, / with folded hands, he spoke these words:
Indeed, by your grace, O best of brahmins, I am freed / from the disease of leprosy, for which I was reviled by living beings for a great length of time.
Therefore I will not rule the kingdom, O best of brahmins; / at this very sacred ford I will now constantly perform great austerity.
This kingdom and country, and elephants, horses, and whatever else / belongs to me—let the best of the twice-born take that!

5.11.m:
Showing the greatest compassion for my grace alone, / [pity] me, a miserable, devoted, and especially detached person.
The brahmins said: / We are not able to protect a kingdom, O best of kings. / Then what is the use of taking that which would lead to the ruin of the kingdom?
Long ago, Rāma, son of Jamadagni, gave the earth to us, / after ridding it of Kṣatriyas thrice-seven times, O best of kings.
Yet it was snatched away from us again by mightier kṣatriyas, / insulting all the twice-born with ease again and again.
The king said: / "I shall provide you protection, O best of brahmins; / even while engaged in austerity in this matter, you must have no fear whatsoever."
The brahmins said: / "If you indeed have faith born of charitable donation, / then build an excellent city right here in this most holy sacred field and give it [to us]

Sūta said: / Hearing that, the ruler of the earth, saying 'So be it,' was overjoyed, / and founded a great city in that place,
with a very high rampart and moats all around, / one krośa in length and width, delightful to the mind,
clean at the junctions of three roads and crossroads, adorned all around with flags, / with lofty, beautiful mansions covered everywhere in white plaster,
furnished with turrets and having many storeys, / filled with persons of true desire and praised by virtuous people.
Then, having filled all the houses, that ruler of the earth, / with gold, gems, pearls, and other objects,
to brahmins of noble birth, especially to knowers of the Vedas, / learned in scripture and self-controlled, endowed with faith,

5.12.m:
Having thus spoken to all of them, that ruler of the earth remained in austerity. / They too did everything just as they were instructed by him.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Instruction Given to His Own Sons and Others for the Preservation of the City by King Camatkāra' in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya of the sixth [book], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.13.s:
.. ..sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ nivedya putrāṇāṃ sa rājyaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
puraṃ ca taddvijātibhyaḥ pradāya svayameva hi .. 1 ..
5.13.d:
.. ..सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं निवेद्य पुत्राणां स राज्यं पृथिवीपतिः ..
पुरं च तद्द्विजातिभ्यः प्रदाय स्वयमेव हि .. 1 ..
5.13.m: Sūta said: / Having thus entrusted the kingdom to his sons / and personally given that city to the twice-born,

5.13.s:
tata ārādhayāmāsa devadevaṃ maheśvaram ..
kṛtvā tadā''śramaṃ tatra śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ .. 2 ..
5.13.d:
तत आराधयामास देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ..
कृत्वा तदा'ऽश्रमं तत्र श्रद्धया परया युतः .. 2 ..
5.13.m: the lord of the earth then worshipped Maheśvara, the god of gods, / having built a hermitage there, endowed with supreme faith.

5.13.s:
sa babhūva phalāhāro yāvadvarṣaśataṃ nṛpaḥ ..
śīrṇaparṇāśanaḥ paścāttāvatkālaṃ samāhitaḥ .. 3 ..
5.13.d:
स बभूव फलाहारो यावद्वर्षशतं नृपः ..
शीर्णपर्णाशनः पश्चात्तावत्कालं समाहितः .. 3 ..
5.13.m: That king subsisted on fruit for a hundred years; / afterwards, concentrated in mind, he ate fallen leaves for the same length of time.

5.13.s:
tataḥ paraṃ jalāhāro jāto varṣaśataṃ hi saḥ ..
vāyubhakṣastato'bhūtsa yāvadvarṣaśataṃ param.. 4 ..
5.13.d:
ततः परं जलाहारो जातो वर्षशतं हि सः ..
वायुभक्षस्ततोऽभूत्स यावद्वर्षशतं परम्.. 4 ..
5.13.m: Thereafter, he subsisted on water for a hundred years, / and then he became an eater of air for a further hundred years.

5.13.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevastasya varṣaśate gate ..
caturthe vāyubhakṣasya darśane samupasthitaḥ .. 5 ..
5.13.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवस्तस्य वर्षशते गते ..
चतुर्थे वायुभक्षस्य दर्शने समुपस्थितः .. 5 ..
5.13.m: Then, when his fourth hundred years of eating air had passed, / Mahādeva, pleased, appeared before his sight.

5.13.s:
provāca parituṣṭo'smi mattaḥ prārthaya vāṃchitam ..
ahaṃ te saṃpradāsyāmi durlabhaṃ tridaśairapi .. 6 ..
5.13.d:
प्रोवाच परितुष्टोऽस्मि मत्तः प्रार्थय वांछितम् ..
अहं ते संप्रदास्यामि दुर्लभं त्रिदशैरपि .. 6 ..
5.13.m: He said: "I am well pleased; ask a wish of me. / I shall bestow on you what is difficult to obtain even by the gods."

5.13.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
etatpuṇyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ nānātīrthasamāśrayam ..
hāṭakeśvaramāhātmyātsarvapāpakṣayāpaham .. 7 ..
5.13.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
एतत्पुण्यतमं क्षेत्रं नानातीर्थसमाश्रयम् ..
हाटकेश्वरमाहात्म्यात्सर्वपापक्षयापहम् .. 7 ..
5.13.m: The king said: / "This most holy sacred field is the refuge of various sacred fords; / because of the greatness of Hāṭakeśvara, it removes all sins.

5.13.s:
tasmāttava nivāsena bhūyānmedhyatamaṃ punaḥ ..
etanme vāṃchitaṃ deva dehi tuṣṭiṃ gato yadi .. 8 ..
5.13.d:
तस्मात्तव निवासेन भूयान्मेध्यतमं पुनः ..
एतन्मे वांछितं देव देहि तुष्टिं गतो यदि .. 8 ..
5.13.m: Therefore, by your residence, may it become most pure once again. / Grant this desire of mine, O Lord, if you are pleased.

5.13.s:
mayaitadagryaṃ nirmāya brāhmaṇebhyo niveditam ..
puraṃ śarvā'marādhīśa śraddhāpūtena cetasā .. 9 ..
5.13.d:
मयैतदग्र्यं निर्माय ब्राह्मणेभ्यो निवेदितम् ..
पुरं शर्वाऽमराधीश श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा .. 9 ..
5.13.m: Having constructed this foremost city, O Śarva, lord of the immortals, / I have offered it to the brahmins with a mind purified by faith.

5.13.s:
tasmiṃstvayā sadā vāsaḥ kartavyo mama vākyataḥ ..
niścalatvena yena syādgaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitam .. 6.13.10 ..
5.13.d:
तस्मिंस्त्वया सदा वासः कर्तव्यो मम वाक्यतः ..
निश्चलत्वेन येन स्याद्गणैः सर्वैः समन्वितम् .. 6.13.10 ..
5.13.m: At my word, you should constantly dwell in it / with steadfastness, so that it may be accompanied by all the gaṇas."

5.13.s:
.. bhagavānuvāca .. ..
acalo'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi sthāne'tra tava bhūmipa ..
acaleśvara ityeva nāmnā khyāto jagattraye .. 11 ..
5.13.d:
.. भगवानुवाच .. ..
अचलोऽहं भविष्यामि स्थानेऽत्र तव भूमिप ..
अचलेश्वर इत्येव नाम्ना ख्यातो जगत्त्रये .. 11 ..
5.13.m: The Blessed One said: / "I shall be immovable in this place for you, O king, / renowned in the three worlds by the very name Acaleśvara.

5.13.s:
yo māmatra sthitaṃ martyo vīkṣayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ ..
bhaviṣyaṃtyacalāstasya sarvadaiva vibhūtayaḥ ..12..
5.13.d:
यो मामत्र स्थितं मर्त्यो वीक्षयिष्यति भक्तितः ..
भविष्यंत्यचलास्तस्य सर्वदैव विभूतयः ..12..
5.13.m: The mortal who shall behold me stationed here with devotion, / his prosperities shall indeed forever be immovable.

5.13.s:
māghaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ mama liṃgasya yo naraḥ ..
śraddhayā parayā yuktaḥ kartā yo ghṛtakaṃbalam ..13..
5.13.d:
माघशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां मम लिंगस्य यो नरः ..
श्रद्धया परया युक्तः कर्ता यो घृतकंबलम् ..13..
5.13.m: On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, whatever man, / endowed with supreme faith, makes a covering of ghee for my liṅga,

5.13.s:
bālye vayasi yatpāpaṃ vārdhake yauvane'pi vā ..
tadyāsyati kṣayaṃ tasya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā .. 14 ..
5.13.d:
बाल्ये वयसि यत्पापं वार्धके यौवनेऽपि वा ..
तद्यास्यति क्षयं तस्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा .. 14 ..
5.13.m: whatever sin was committed in his childhood, in old age, or even in youth, / that shall vanish, just as darkness does at sunrise.

5.13.s:
tasmātsthāpaya me liṃgaṃ tvamatraiva mahīpate ..
ahaṃ yena karomyeva tatra vāsaṃ sadācalaḥ .. 15 ..
5.13.d:
तस्मात्स्थापय मे लिंगं त्वमत्रैव महीपते ..
अहं येन करोम्येव तत्र वासं सदाचलः .. 15 ..
5.13.m: Therefore, O king, install my liṅga right here, / so that I may dwell there, always immovable.

5.13.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā sa deveśastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
so'pi rājā cakārāśu prāsādaṃ sumanoharam .. 16 ..
tatra saṃsthāpayāmāsa liṃgaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ ..
śraddhayā parayā yuktaḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam ...7..
yasmindṛṣṭe'thavā spṛṣṭe dhyāte vā pūjite'pi vā ..
naro vimucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇāṃtikāt ...8..
5.13.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा स देवेशस्ततश्चादर्शनं गतः ..
सोऽपि राजा चकाराशु प्रासादं सुमनोहरम् .. 16 ..
तत्र संस्थापयामास लिंगं देवस्य शूलिनः ..
श्रद्धया परया युक्तः सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् ...7..
यस्मिन्दृष्टेऽथवा स्पृष्टे ध्याते वा पूजितेऽपि वा ..
नरो विमुच्यते पापादाजन्ममरणांतिकात् ...8..
5.13.m:
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the Lord of gods then vanished from sight. / That king too quickly built a very charming temple.
Endowed with supreme faith, he installed there the liṅga / of the trident-bearing god, marked by all auspicious characteristics.
When it is seen, touched, meditated upon, or even worshipped, / a person is freed from sins extending from birth to death.

5.13.s:
tataḥ saṃciṃtayāmāsa bhūpālaḥ kiṃ maheśvaraḥ ..
sāṃnidhyaṃ niścalo bhūtvā liṃge'traiva kariṣyati .. 19 ..
5.13.d:
ततः संचिंतयामास भूपालः किं महेश्वरः ..
सांनिध्यं निश्चलो भूत्वा लिंगेऽत्रैव करिष्यति .. 19 ..
5.13.m: Then the king pondered: "Will Maheśvara, / having become immovable, manifest his presence right here in this liṅga?"

5.13.s:
etasminnaṃtare jātā vāṇī gaganagocarā ..
harṣayantī mahīpālaṃ camatkāraṃ sunisvanā .. 6.13.20 ..
5.13.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे जाता वाणी गगनगोचरा ..
हर्षयन्ती महीपालं चमत्कारं सुनिस्वना .. 6.13.20 ..
5.13.m: In the meantime, a sweet-sounding celestial voice arose, / gladdening the king, [producing] astonishment:

5.13.s:
mā tvaṃ bhūmipaśārdūla kāryacintāṃ kariṣyasi ..
asminvāsaṃ sadātraiva liṃge kartāsmi nityaśaḥ .. 21 ..
5.13.d:
मा त्वं भूमिपशार्दूल कार्यचिन्तां करिष्यसि ..
अस्मिन्वासं सदात्रैव लिंगे कर्तास्मि नित्यशः .. 21 ..
5.13.m: "Do not worry about this matter, O tiger among kings! / I will always and continuously dwell right here in this liṅga.

5.13.s:
tathānyadapi te vacmi pratyayārthaṃ vaco nṛpa ..
tacchrutvā nirvṛtiṃ gaccha vīkṣasvaiva ca yatnataḥ .. 22 ...
5.13.d:
तथान्यदपि ते वच्मि प्रत्ययार्थं वचो नृप ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा निर्वृतिं गच्छ वीक्षस्वैव च यत्नतः .. 22 ...
5.13.m: Moreover, O king, I tell you another word to inspire confidence; / hearing it, attain peace of mind and observe it carefully.

5.13.s:
sadā me niścalā chāyā liṃgasyāsya bhaviṣyati ..
ekaiva pṛṣṭhadeśasthā na diksaṃsthā bhaviṣyati .. 23 ..
5.13.d:
सदा मे निश्चला छाया लिंगस्यास्य भविष्यति ..
एकैव पृष्ठदेशस्था न दिक्संस्था भविष्यति .. 23 ..
5.13.m: The shadow of this liṅga of mine shall always be motionless; / it shall remain solely at its back, and shall not shift with the directions."

5.13.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tataḥ sa vīkṣayāmāsa tāṃ chāyāṃ liṃgasaṃbhavām ..
tadrūpāṃ niścalāṃ nityaṃ taddiksaṃsthe divākare .. 24 ..
5.13.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततः स वीक्षयामास तां छायां लिंगसंभवाम् ..
तद्रूपां निश्चलां नित्यं तद्दिक्संस्थे दिवाकरे .. 24 ..
5.13.m: Sūta said: / Then he observed that shadow cast by the liṅga, / constant in form, ever motionless even as the sun moved through its directions.

5.13.s:
tato harṣaṃ paraṃ gatvā praṇipatya ca taṃ bhuvi ..
kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ sa mene pārthivottamaḥ .. 25 ..
5.13.d:
ततो हर्षं परं गत्वा प्रणिपत्य च तं भुवि ..
कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानं स मेने पार्थिवोत्तमः .. 25 ..
5.13.m: Attaining supreme joy and bowing down to it on the ground, / that best of kings considered himself to have achieved his purpose.

5.13.s:
adyāpi dṛśyate chāyā tādṛgrūpā sadā hi sā ..
tasya liṃgasya viprendrā jātā vismayakāriṇī .. 26 ..
5.13.d:
अद्यापि दृश्यते छाया तादृग्रूपा सदा हि सा ..
तस्य लिंगस्य विप्रेन्द्रा जाता विस्मयकारिणी .. 26 ..
5.13.m: Even today, that very shadow is always seen in that form; / O best of brahmins, it has become a wonder of that liṅga.

5.13.s:
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuryasya syādbhuvi bho dvijāḥ ..
na sa paśyati tāṃ chāyāmeṣo'nyaḥ pratyayaḥ paraḥ .. 27 ..
5.13.d:
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे मृत्युर्यस्य स्याद्भुवि भो द्विजाः ..
न स पश्यति तां छायामेषोऽन्यः प्रत्ययः परः .. 27 ..
5.13.m: If a person on earth is to die within six months, O twice-born, / he does not see that shadow; this is another great proof.

5.13.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstatra sarvadaiva vyavasthitaḥ ..
acaleśvararūpeṇa camatkārapurāṃtike .. 28 ..
5.13.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं स भगवांस्तत्र सर्वदैव व्यवस्थितः ..
अचलेश्वररूपेण चमत्कारपुरांतिके .. 28 ..
5.13.m: Sūta said: / Thus the Blessed Lord has always remained stationed there / in the form of Acaleśvara, near Camatkārapura.

5.13.s:
niścalatvena deveśohyaṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu madhyamaḥ ..
kṣetrāṇāṃ vasate tatra tasya vākyānmaheśvaraḥ .. 29 ..
5.13.d:
निश्चलत्वेन देवेशोह्यष्टषष्टिषु मध्यमः ..
क्षेत्राणां वसते तत्र तस्य वाक्यान्महेश्वरः .. 29 ..
5.13.m: Due to his word, Maheśvara, the Lord of gods, the central one / among the sixty-eight sacred fields, dwells there with immobility.

5.13.s:
tena tatpāvanaṃ kṣetraṃ sarveṣāmiha kīrtitam ..
kāmadaṃ muktidaṃ caiva jāyate sarvadehinām .. 6.13.30 ..
5.13.d:
तेन तत्पावनं क्षेत्रं सर्वेषामिह कीर्तितम् ..
कामदं मुक्तिदं चैव जायते सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 6.13.30 ..
5.13.m: Therefore, that sacred field is proclaimed here as purifying for all; / it grants the desires and liberation of all embodied beings.

5.13.s:
tathānyadapi yadvṛttaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ tatprabhāvajam ..
tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 31 ..
5.13.d:
तथान्यदपि यद्वृत्तं वृत्तांतं तत्प्रभावजम् ..
तदहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां द्विजसत्तमाः .. 31 ..
5.13.m: Likewise, another incident that occurred, arising from its power, / I shall proclaim; let it be heard, O best of brahmins!

5.13.s:
acaleśvaramāhātmyāttasminkṣetre narā drutam..
vāṃchitaṃ manasaḥ sarve labhaṃte sakalaṃ phalam .. 32 ..
5.13.d:
अचलेश्वरमाहात्म्यात्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे नरा द्रुतम्..
वांछितं मनसः सर्वे लभंते सकलं फलम् .. 32 ..
5.13.m: By virtue of the māhātmya of Acaleśvara, in that sacred field men swiftly / obtain their every heart's desire, the entire fruit:

5.13.s:
svargameke pare mokṣaṃ dhanadhānyasutāṃstathā ..
yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya pūjayedacaleśvaram..
taṃtaṃ sa labhate martyaḥ svalpāyāsena ca drutam .. 33 ..
5.13.d:
स्वर्गमेके परे मोक्षं धनधान्यसुतांस्तथा ..
यो यं काममभिध्याय पूजयेदचलेश्वरम्..
तंतं स लभते मर्त्यः स्वल्पायासेन च द्रुतम् .. 33 ..
5.13.m: some obtain heaven, others liberation, as well as wealth, grain, and sons; / whatever desire a mortal contemplates while worshipping Acaleśvara, / he attains that very thing swiftly and with little effort.

5.13.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaḥ sarve pāpanarā bhuvi ..
svargaṃ yāṃti tathā mokṣaṃ prāpnuvanti ca sammukham .. 34 ..
5.13.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षः सर्वे पापनरा भुवि ..
स्वर्गं यांति तथा मोक्षं प्राप्नुवन्ति च सम्मुखम् .. 34 ..
5.13.m: Then the thousand-eyed [Indra], seeing that all sinful men on earth / go to heaven and directly attain liberation,

5.13.s:
tataḥ krodhaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca lobhaṃ dveṣaṃ bhayaṃ ratim ..
mohaṃ ca vyasanaṃ durgaṃ matsaraṃ rāgameva ca .. 35 ..
5.13.d:
ततः क्रोधं च कामं च लोभं द्वेषं भयं रतिम् ..
मोहं च व्यसनं दुर्गं मत्सरं रागमेव च .. 35 ..
5.13.m: summoned all [the passions] in bodily form—anger, desire, / greed, hatred, fear, pleasure, delusion, vice, distress, envy, and passion—

5.13.s:
sarvānmūrtānsamāhūya tataḥ provāca sādaram..
svayameva sahasrākṣo rahasye dvijasattamāḥ .. 36 .
5.13.d:
सर्वान्मूर्तान्समाहूय ततः प्रोवाच सादरम्..
स्वयमेव सहस्राक्षो रहस्ये द्विजसत्तमाः .. 36 .
5.13.m: and then the thousand-eyed one himself spoke respectfully / in secret, O best of brahmins:

5.13.s:
naro vā yadi vā nārī camatkārapuraṃ prati ..
yo gacchati dharāpṛṣṭhe yuṣmābhirvārya eva saḥ .. 37 ..
5.13.d:
नरो वा यदि वा नारी चमत्कारपुरं प्रति ..
यो गच्छति धरापृष्ठे युष्माभिर्वार्य एव सः .. 37 ..
5.13.m: "Whatever man or woman on the surface of the earth / goes toward Camatkārapura must be turned back by you.

5.13.s:
tatraiva vasamāno'pi yo gacchedacaleśvaram ..
madvākyātsa viśeṣeṇa sarvairvāryaḥ prayatnataḥ .. 38 ..
5.13.d:
तत्रैव वसमानोऽपि यो गच्छेदचलेश्वरम् ..
मद्वाक्यात्स विशेषेण सर्वैर्वार्यः प्रयत्नतः .. 38 ..
5.13.m: Even one who resides right there, should he go to Acaleśvara, / by my command he especially must be turned back with effort by all [of you]."

5.13.s:
te tatheti pratijñāya gatvā śakrasya śāsanāt ..
cakrustataḥ samucchinnaṃ tanmāhātmyaṃ gataṃ bhuvi .. 39 ..
5.13.d:
ते तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय गत्वा शक्रस्य शासनात् ..
चक्रुस्ततः समुच्छिन्नं तन्माहात्म्यं गतं भुवि .. 39 ..
5.13.m: Promising, "So be it," and setting out by Indra's command, / they completely destroyed that māhātmya that had spread on earth.

5.13.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātamākhyānaṃ pāpanāśanam ..
acaleśvaradevasya tasminkṣetre nivāsinaḥ .. 6.13.40 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'caleśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trayodaśodhyāyaḥ .. .. 13 .. .. ..
5.13.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातमाख्यानं पापनाशनम् ..
अचलेश्वरदेवस्य तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे निवासिनः .. 6.13.40 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽचलेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रयोदशोध्यायः .. .. 13 .. .. ..
5.13.m:
This entire sin-destroying narrative has been related to you / concerning the god Acaleśvara, who dwells in that sacred field.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named "Description of the Māhātmya of Acaleśvara," in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.14.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
yadanyattatra sañjātamāścaryaṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi rahasyaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam .. 1 ..
5.14.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
यदन्यत्तत्र सञ्जातमाश्चर्यं द्विजसत्तमाः ..
तदहं कीर्तयिष्यामि रहस्यं हृदि संस्थितम् .. 1 ..
5.14.m: Sūta said: / What other marvel occurred there, O best of brahmins, / that secret held in my heart I shall proclaim.

5.14.s:
camatkārapure kaścidvaiśyajātisamudbhavaḥ ..
babhūva puruṣo mūko daridreṇa samanvitaḥ .. 2 ..
5.14.d:
चमत्कारपुरे कश्चिद्वैश्यजातिसमुद्भवः ..
बभूव पुरुषो मूको दरिद्रेण समन्वितः .. 2 ..
5.14.m: In Camatkārapura there was a certain man born of the vaiśya caste; / he was mute and afflicted with poverty.

5.14.s:
yo dauḥsthyātsarvalokānāṃ karoti paśurakṣaṇam ..
kuṭumbabharaṇārthāya saṃtuṣṭo yenakenacit .. 3 ..
5.14.d:
यो दौःस्थ्यात्सर्वलोकानां करोति पशुरक्षणम् ..
कुटुम्बभरणार्थाय संतुष्टो येनकेनचित् .. 3 ..
5.14.m: Due to distress, he tended cattle for everyone / to support his family, satisfied with whatever little [he received].

5.14.s:
kadācidrakṣatastasya paśūṃstānvanabhūmiṣu ..
paśureko viniṣkrāṃtaḥ svayūthāttṛṇalobhataḥ ..4...
5.14.d:
कदाचिद्रक्षतस्तस्य पशूंस्तान्वनभूमिषु ..
पशुरेको विनिष्क्रांतः स्वयूथात्तृणलोभतः ..4...
5.14.m: Once, while he was tending those animals in the forest lands, / one animal strayed from its herd out of greed for grass.

5.14.s:
kṛṣṇa pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ caitramāse dvijottamāḥ ..
na tadā lakṣitastena gacchamāno yadṛcchayā .. 5 ..
5.14.d:
कृष्ण पक्षे चतुर्दश्यां चैत्रमासे द्विजोत्तमाः ..
न तदा लक्षितस्तेन गच्छमानो यदृच्छया .. 5 ..
5.14.m: On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Caitra, O best of the twice-born, / it was not noticed by him as it wandered off at will.

5.14.s:
atha yāvadgṛhaṃ prāptaḥ sa mūkaḥ paśupālakaḥ ..
tāvattasya ca goḥ svāmī bhartsayansamupāgataḥ .. 6 ..
5.14.d:
अथ यावद्गृहं प्राप्तः स मूकः पशुपालकः ..
तावत्तस्य च गोः स्वामी भर्त्सयन्समुपागतः .. 6 ..
5.14.m: Now, as soon as the mute cowherd reached home, / the owner of that cow arrived, scolding him:

5.14.s:
kiṃ pāpa na samāyātaḥ paśureko'dya no yathā ..
nūnaṃ tvayā hataḥ so'pi vikrīto'pihito'thavā ..
tasmā dānaya me kṣipraṃ nirāhāro'pi gāṃ tvarāt .. 7 ..
5.14.d:
किं पाप न समायातः पशुरेकोऽद्य नो यथा ..
नूनं त्वया हतः सोऽपि विक्रीतोऽपिहितोऽथवा ..
तस्मा दानय मे क्षिप्रं निराहारोऽपि गां त्वरात् .. 7 ..
5.14.m: "Why, you sinner, has one of our cattle not returned today? / Surely it was killed by you, or sold, or concealed! / Therefore, bring me that cow quickly, even without eating!"

5.14.s:
tacchrutvā bhayasaṃtrastaḥ sa mūkaḥ paśupālakaḥ ..
niṣkrāṃto yaṣṭimādāya nirāhāro'pi mandirāt .. .. 8 ..
5.14.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भयसंत्रस्तः स मूकः पशुपालकः ..
निष्क्रांतो यष्टिमादाय निराहारोऽपि मन्दिरात् .. .. 8 ..
5.14.m: Hearing that, the mute cowherd, terrified with fear, / took a stick and set out from the house, without even taking food.

5.14.s:
tato'raṇyaṃ samāsādya vīkṣāṃcakre samaṃtataḥ ..
sūkṣmadṛṣṭyā sa durgāṇi gahanāni vanāni ca . 9 ..
5.14.d:
ततोऽरण्यं समासाद्य वीक्षांचक्रे समंततः ..
सूक्ष्मदृष्ट्या स दुर्गाणि गहनानि वनानि च . 9 ..
5.14.m: Then, having reached the wilderness, he looked all around / with a sharp gaze into the difficult places and dense forests.

5.14.s:
atha tena kvaciddṛṣṭaṃ padaṃ tasya paśoḥ sphuṭam ..
aṭavyāṃ bhramamāṇena parijñātaṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 6.14.10 ..
5.14.d:
अथ तेन क्वचिद्दृष्टं पदं तस्य पशोः स्फुटम् ..
अटव्यां भ्रममाणेन परिज्ञातं च कृत्स्नशः .. 6.14.10 ..
5.14.m: Then somewhere, as he was wandering in the forest, / the clear footprint of that animal was seen and fully recognized by him.

5.14.s:
tataśca tatpadānveṣī sa jagāma vanādvanam ..
camatkārapurasyāsya samaṃtāddvijasatta māḥ .. 11 ..
5.14.d:
ततश्च तत्पदान्वेषी स जगाम वनाद्वनम् ..
चमत्कारपुरस्यास्य समंताद्द्विजसत्त माः .. 11 ..
5.14.m: Then, following those footprints, he went from forest to forest / all around this Camatkārapura, O best of brahmins.

5.14.s:
evaṃ pradakṣiṇā tasya jātā paśudidṛkṣayā ..
sthānasya caiva nirveśe paśoścāpidvijottamāḥ .. 12 ..
5.14.d:
एवं प्रदक्षिणा तस्य जाता पशुदिदृक्षया ..
स्थानस्य चैव निर्वेशे पशोश्चापिद्विजोत्तमाः .. 12 ..
5.14.m: Thus a circumambulation of the place and also of the animal / was performed by him in his desire to find the animal, O best of the twice-born.

5.14.s:
pradakṣiṇāvasāne ca paśurlabdho hi tena saḥ ..
niśāṃte'tha gṛhaṃ nītvā svāmine viniveditaḥ .. 13 ..
5.14.d:
प्रदक्षिणावसाने च पशुर्लब्धो हि तेन सः ..
निशांतेऽथ गृहं नीत्वा स्वामिने विनिवेदितः .. 13 ..
5.14.m: And at the end of the circumambulation, the beast was indeed found by him. / Then, at the end of the night, having led [it] home, it was presented to its owner.

5.14.s:
caitre puṇyatame māsi kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm ..
kṣetre puṇyatame devāstīrthānyā yāṃti sarvaśaḥ .. 14 ..
5.14.d:
चैत्रे पुण्यतमे मासि कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् ..
क्षेत्रे पुण्यतमे देवास्तीर्थान्या यांति सर्वशः .. 14 ..
5.14.m: On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the most holy month of Caitra, / the gods and the sacred fords arrive from all around at the most sacred field.

5.14.s:
evamajñānabhāvena kṛtā tābhyāṃ pradakṣiṇā ..
paśupālapaśubhyāṃ vai supuṇye tatra vāsare .. 15 ..
5.14.d:
एवमज्ञानभावेन कृता ताभ्यां प्रदक्षिणा ..
पशुपालपशुभ्यां वै सुपुण्ये तत्र वासरे .. 15 ..
5.14.m: Thus, circumambulation was performed unconsciously by both of them, / indeed by the herdsman and the beast, on that most holy day.

5.14.s: nirāhārasya mūkasya sāhārasya paśostathā .. 16 ..
5.14.d: निराहारस्य मूकस्य साहारस्य पशोस्तथा .. 16 ..
5.14.m: [It was performed] by the speechless one who was without food, and likewise by the beast that had food,

5.14.s:
vinā snānena bhakṣācca daivāddvijavarottamāḥ ..
tataḥ kāle vyatikrāṃte kiyanmātre svakarmataḥ ..
ubhau paṃcatvamāpannau pṛthaktvenāyuṣaḥ kṣaye .. 17 ..
5.14.d:
विना स्नानेन भक्षाच्च दैवाद्द्विजवरोत्तमाः ..
ततः काले व्यतिक्रांते कियन्मात्रे स्वकर्मतः ..
उभौ पंचत्वमापन्नौ पृथक्त्वेनायुषः क्षये .. 17 ..
5.14.m: without bathing or eating, by fate, O best of excellent brahmins. / Then, after a certain amount of time had passed in accordance with their own karma, / both met their death separately at the expiration of their life span.

5.14.s:
tataśca paśupālastu daśārṇādhipateḥ sutaḥ ..
saṃjātastatprabhāvena pūrvajātimanusmaran .. 18 ..
so'pi jajñe paśustasya sacivo dvijasattamāḥ .
jātismaro yathā rājā sarvadā nṛpasaṃmataḥ...9..
5.14.d:
ततश्च पशुपालस्तु दशार्णाधिपतेः सुतः ..
संजातस्तत्प्रभावेन पूर्वजातिमनुस्मरन् .. 18 ..
सोऽपि जज्ञे पशुस्तस्य सचिवो द्विजसत्तमाः .
जातिस्मरो यथा राजा सर्वदा नृपसंमतः...9..
5.14.m:
And then the herdsman was born as the son of the ruler of Daśārṇa / through the power of that [merit], remembering his previous birth.
The beast also was born as his minister, O best of brahmins, / remembering his past birth just like the king, and always esteemed by the king.

5.14.s:
athāgatya sa rājeṃdrastenaiva saha maṃtriṇā ..
kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ purastasyāḥ pradakṣiṇām .. 6.14.20 ..
5.14.d:
अथागत्य स राजेंद्रस्तेनैव सह मंत्रिणा ..
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां पुरस्तस्याः प्रदक्षिणाम् .. 6.14.20 ..
5.14.m: Then, having arrived on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, that lord of kings together with that very minister / [performed] circumambulation around that city

5.14.s:
cakre saṃvatsarasyāṃte śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ ..
nirāhāraśca maunena padātirdvijasattamāḥ .. 21 ..
5.14.d:
चक्रे संवत्सरस्यांते श्रद्धया परया युतः ..
निराहारश्च मौनेन पदातिर्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 21 ..
5.14.m: at the end of the year, endowed with supreme faith, / fasting, in silence, and on foot, O best of brahmins.

5.14.s:
ekadā tatra cā''yātā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ ..
tīrthe pāpahare puṇye viśvāmitrasamudbhave .. 22 ..
5.14.d:
एकदा तत्र चा'ऽयाता मुनयः शंसितव्रताः ..
तीर्थे पापहरे पुण्ये विश्वामित्रसमुद्भवे .. 22 ..
5.14.m: Once, sages of celebrated vows arrived there, / at the holy sacred ford that removes sin, born of Viśvāmitra:

5.14.s:
yājñavalkyo bharadvājaḥ śunaḥśepo'tha gālavaḥ ..
devalo bhāgurirdhaumyaḥ kaśya paścyavano bhṛguḥ .. 23 ..
5.14.d:
याज्ञवल्क्यो भरद्वाजः शुनःशेपोऽथ गालवः ..
देवलो भागुरिर्धौम्यः कश्य पश्च्यवनो भृगुः .. 23 ..
5.14.m: Yājñavalkya, Bharadvāja, Śunaḥśepa, and then Gālava, / Devala, Bhāguri, Dhaumya, Kaśyapa, Cyavana, and Bhṛgu,

5.14.s:
tathānye śaṃsitā''tmāno brahmacaryaparāyaṇāḥ ..
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena tasminkṣetre samāgatāḥ .. 24 ..
5.14.d:
तथान्ये शंसिता'ऽत्मानो ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणाः ..
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे समागताः .. 24 ..
5.14.m: as well as other praised souls dedicated to celibacy; / on the occasion of a pilgrimage to sacred fords, they arrived at that sacred field.

5.14.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā sa mahīpālaḥ praṇipatya kṛtāṃjaliḥ ..
yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathāśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ .. 25 ..
5.14.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा स महीपालः प्रणिपत्य कृतांजलिः ..
यथाज्येष्ठं यथाश्रेष्ठं पूजयामास भक्तितः .. 25 ..
5.14.m: Seeing them, the protector of the earth bowed down with folded hands, / and worshipped them with devotion according to age and according to excellence.

5.14.s:
tatasteṣāṃ sa madhye ca saṃniviṣṭo mahīpatiḥ ..
tathāgataḥ sa bhūpālaḥ sarvai staiścābhinaṃditaḥ .. 26 ..
5.14.d:
ततस्तेषां स मध्ये च संनिविष्टो महीपतिः ..
तथागतः स भूपालः सर्वै स्तैश्चाभिनंदितः .. 26 ..
5.14.m: Then the lord of the earth sat down in their midst; / the ruler of the earth, having approached thus, was welcomed by all of them.

5.14.s:
tataścakruḥ kathā divyā munayaste mahīpateḥ .
purato munimukhyānāṃ caritāni mahātmanām .. 27 ..
5.14.d:
ततश्चक्रुः कथा दिव्या मुनयस्ते महीपतेः .
पुरतो मुनिमुख्यानां चरितानि महात्मनाम् .. 27 ..
5.14.m: Then those sages related divine stories before the king, / [narrating] the deeds of great-souled foremost sages

5.14.s:
rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ dharmaśāstrasamudbhavāḥ ..
ānaṃdaṃ tasya rājarṣerjanayaṃto dvijottamāḥ .. 28 ..
5.14.d:
राजर्षीणां पुराणानां धर्मशास्त्रसमुद्भवाः ..
आनंदं तस्य राजर्षेर्जनयंतो द्विजोत्तमाः .. 28 ..
5.14.m: and of royal sages, derived from the Purāṇas and the scriptures of Dharma, / generating joy for that royal sage, O best of brahmins.

5.14.s:
atha kvā'pi kathāṃte sa pārthivastairmaharṣibhiḥ ..
pṛṣṭaḥ kautūhalāviṣṭairdattvā śrautīstadāśiṣaḥ .. 29 ..
5.14.d:
अथ क्वाऽपि कथांते स पार्थिवस्तैर्महर्षिभिः ..
पृष्टः कौतूहलाविष्टैर्दत्त्वा श्रौतीस्तदाशिषः .. 29 ..
5.14.m: Then, at the end of a certain story, after bestowing Vedic blessings, / the earthly ruler was asked by those great seers filled with curiosity:

5.14.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
varṣevarṣe mahīpāla tvamatrā''gatya yatnataḥ ..
karoṣi maṃtriṇā sārdhaṃ purasyā'sya pradakṣiṇām .. .. 6.14.30 ..
5.14.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
वर्षेवर्षे महीपाल त्वमत्रा'ऽगत्य यत्नतः ..
करोषि मंत्रिणा सार्धं पुरस्याऽस्य प्रदक्षिणाम् .. .. 6.14.30 ..
5.14.m: The seers said: / "Year after year, O protector of the earth, coming here with effort / along with your minister, you perform the circumambulation of this city.

5.14.s:
asminkṣetre sutīrthāni saṃti pārthivasattama ..
tathā'nyāni prasiddhāni devatāyatanāni ca . 31 ..
5.14.d:
अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे सुतीर्थानि संति पार्थिवसत्तम ..
तथाऽन्यानि प्रसिद्धानि देवतायतनानि च . 31 ..
5.14.m: In this sacred field there are excellent sacred fords, O best of earthly rulers, / and likewise other renowned shrines of deities.

5.14.s:
ādarasteṣu vai rājannāsti svalpo 'pi karhicit ..
etannaḥ kautukaṃ jātaṃ na cedguhyaṃ prakīrtaya .. 32 ..
5.14.d:
आदरस्तेषु वै राजन्नास्ति स्वल्पो ऽपि कर्हिचित् ..
एतन्नः कौतुकं जातं न चेद्गुह्यं प्रकीर्तय .. 32 ..
5.14.m: Yet toward them, O king, there is not the slightest regard from you at any time. / This curiosity has arisen in us; if it is not a secret, explain [it]."

5.14.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vinayā'vanataḥ sthitaḥ ..
sa provāca vaco bhūpaḥ kiṃcidvrīḍāsamanvitaḥ..33..
5.14.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विनयाऽवनतः स्थितः ..

5.14.m:
That king and the minister also became gods riding aerial chariots; / even today the two are seen in the form of stars in the vault of heaven.
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, named 'The Description of the Greatness of the Circumambulation of Camatkārapura', in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.15.m: Chapter Fifteen. / Nārada said: / Then the god Nārāyaṇa, wearing matted hair and bark garments, / and his companion as a second, holding fruit in his hand, arrived. / Seeing the two, that doe-eyed messenger of love lamented. / Hearing her speech, both of them said to her: / "Do not fear, auspicious lady! We two have come to protect you. / How have you entered this dreadful forest frequented by wicked beings?"

5.15.m: Having thus comforted that slender lady, Mādhava said to the rākṣasa: / "Release this sweet-smiling lady of delicate limbs, you of vile conduct! / Ah, you fool of evil conduct, what have you set out to do, / preparing to make food out of the treasure of the eyes of all people? / This lady is the ornament of the earth through the power of world-merit; you are killing her! / By killing this celestial nymph in the forest, you will now render the world lightless / and love deprived of pride; / therefore quickly release her, the goddess of the palace of happiness!"

5.15.m: Hearing these words of Hari, the enraged rākṣasa said: / "If you are capable, then release [her] right now from my hands!" / The moment that speech was uttered, looked upon in wrath by Mādhava, / he abandoned Vṛndā far away and fell, reduced to ashes. / Then, utterly bewildered by the illusion of the Lord of the Universe, she said: / "Who are you, ocean of compassion, by whom I have been protected here? / O treasure of austerities, bodily and mental distress accompanied by torment / has been removed by you with sweet speech, through the destruction of the rākṣasa."

5.15.m: I will perform austerity in your hermitage, gentle one, rich in austerity.” / The ascetic said: / “I am the son of Bharadvāja, renowned as Devaśarman; / abandoning all pleasures, I have come to this dreadful forest. / Together with this novice boy, my disciple, who travels at will; / and many other disciples of mine also travel at will and assume forms at will. / If, auspicious lady, you wish to perform austerity staying in my hermitage, / come, queen, let us go to another forest, because it lies far off.”

5.15.m: Having spoken thus to that king’s wife, Hari went towards the eastern direction, / to a forest filled with pretas and piśācas, walking with slow steps, O ruler of men. / Vṛndārikā, her eyes filled with tears, followed closely behind him, / and Smaradūtī followed behind her, saying, “Wait for me!” / In the meantime, an evil-doer of sinful appearance in the forest / spread out a net; when it was filled with living creatures, / then that master of sin drew the net tight; / and then, taking up the living creatures caught in the net, he released them.

5.15.m: And seeing the two women, that hunter—Smaradūtī spoke to her: / “O queen, he is coming to devour me! Let my friend take me by the hand!” / Hearing what she said, Vṛndā looked at that man of deformed face; / beholding him, shaken by the wind of fear, the beloved of the Ocean’s son / ran away in distress, the fair lady, together with Smaradūtī in the forest; / fleeing along with her friend, she reached the ascetic's hermitage. / In that ascetic forest she beheld something exceedingly wondrous: / birds with golden bodies, chirping with diverse songs.

सुखस्पर्शं भुजाभ्यां सा शोकवल्लीव लिंगिता
तवालिंगनभावेन पुनरेव भविष्यति 31
5.15.m: She said to him: “O lord, protect me! Protect me from the sinful hunter! / What use is austerity, what use is dharma, what use is silence and muttered prayer? / There is no merit higher than protecting the frightened, O you rich in austerity!” / Having spoken thus to the ascetic, terrified, her limbs languid, / meanwhile that wicked-souled hunter, the captor of all living beings, arrived; / Queen Vṛndā, terrified with fear, embraced Hari’s neck. / With her two arms she clung to his pleasant touch like a creeper of sorrow; / “By the power of your embrace, it will come to be again:

5.15.s:

5.15.s:

शृणु देवि यथा युद्धं वृत्तं शंभोर्मया सह 37
प्रिये रुद्रेण रौद्रेण छिन्नं चक्रेण मे शिरः

5.15.m: Then, seeing her beloved with his full body, she said: / “I shall do what pleases you, my master; tell me also about your battle.” / Hearing Vṛndā’s words, he who was born from the ocean of illusion said: / “Listen, queen, to how the battle took place between Śambhu and me. / My dear, my head was cut off with a discus by fierce Rudra; / then, by the power of your ascetic attainment and through my soul directed toward you, / it was severed and brought here, and restored to life through contact with your limbs! / My dear, innocent girl, you became sorrowful through separation from me;

5.15.s:
kṣaṃtavyaṃ vipriyaṃ mahyaṃ yattvāṃ tyaktvā raṇaṃ gataḥ
ityādi vacanaistena vṛṃdā saṃsmāritā tadā 40
tāṃbūlaiśca vinodaiśca vastrālaṃkaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ

mokṣādapyadhikaṃ saukhyaṃ vṛṃdā mohanasaṃbhavam 42
mene nārāyaṇo devo lakṣmīpremarasādhikam

क्षंतव्यं विप्रियं मह्यं यत्त्वां त्यक्त्वा रणं गतः

वृंदां वियोगजं दुःखं विनोदयति माधवे 43
5.15.m: forgive me that displeasure, in that I abandoned you and went to battle.” / With these and other words Vṛndā was then reassured by him, / and with betel rolls, amusements, and beautiful clothes and ornaments. / Then the goddess Vṛndārikā, endowed with all pleasures, / embracing her beloved tightly, kissed him, eager for lovemaking. / Lord Nārāyaṇa deemed that happiness arising from Vṛndā’s infatuation / to be greater even than liberation, surpassing the nectar of Lakṣmī’s love. / While Mādhava was dispelling Vṛndā’s sorrow born of separation,

tatkrīḍācāruvilasadvāpikā rājahaṃsake

तद्रूपभावात्कृष्णोऽसौ पद्मायां विगतस्पृहः 44

दिनानि कतिचिन्मेने शिवकार्यं जगत्पतिः 46

5.15.m: in a stepped well shining beautifully with royal swans for their sport, / through the sentiment of her form, that Kṛṣṇa lost his desire for Padmā. / In that forest of Vṛndā, she who bore the form of the Tulasī plant / arose exceedingly holy upon the earth from the sweat of Vṛndā’s body. / Experiencing this pleasure born from contact with Vṛndā’s body, / Hari, the Lord of the universe, considered the business of Śiva for several days. / Once, at the end of lovemaking, she saw the ascetic / clinging to her neck—the two-armed Supreme Person.

5.15.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha sā kaṃṭhādvimucya bhujabaṃdhanam

5.15.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा प्राह सा कंठाद्विमुच्य भुजबंधनम्
कथं तापसरूपेण त्वं मां मोहितुमागतः 48
निशम्य वचनं तस्याः सांत्वयन्प्राह तां हरिः
शृणु वृंदारिके त्वं मां विद्धि लक्ष्मीमनोहरम् 49

अहं शिवः शिवश्चाहं पृथक्त्वे न व्यवस्थितौ 6.15.50

नारद उवाच-
5.15.m: Seeing him, she released the embrace of her arms from his neck and said: / “Why have you come in the form of an ascetic to deceive me?” / Hearing her words, Hari spoke to comfort her: / “Listen, Vṛndārikā, know me to be the charmer of Lakṣmī. / Your husband went to conquer Hara and bring back Gaurī; / I am Śiva and Śiva is I, we do not exist separately. / Jālandhara has been killed in battle; worship me now, blameless lady!” / Nārada said:

5.15.s:
iti viṣṇorvacaḥ śrutvā viṣaṇṇavadanābhavat
tato vṛṃdārikā rājankupitā pratyuvāca ha 51
raṇe baddho'si yena tvaṃ jīvanmuktaḥ piturgirā
vividhaiḥ satkṛto ratnairyuktaṃ tasya hṛtā vadhūḥ 52
patirdharmasya yo nityaṃ paradārarataḥ katham
īśvaro'pi kṛtaṃ bhuṃkte karmetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ 53
ahaṃ mohaṃ yathānītā tvayā māyā tapasvinā
tathā tava vadhūṃ māyā tapasvīko'pi neṣyati 54
5.15.d:
इति विष्णोर्वचः श्रुत्वा विषण्णवदनाभवत्
ततो वृंदारिका राजन्कुपिता प्रत्युवाच ह 51
रणे बद्धोऽसि येन त्वं जीवन्मुक्तः पितुर्गिरा
विविधैः सत्कृतो रत्नैर्युक्तं तस्य हृता वधूः 52
पतिर्धर्मस्य यो नित्यं परदाररतः कथम्
ईश्वरोऽपि कृतं भुंक्ते कर्मेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः 53
अहं मोहं यथानीता त्वया माया तपस्विना
तथा तव वधूं माया तपस्वीकोऽपि नेष्यति 54
5.15.m: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, her face became dejected; / then, O king, Vṛndārikā, enraged, answered: / “By whom you were bound in battle, and who released you alive at his father’s word / and honoured you with various jewels—is it right that his wife was abducted? / How can he who is the eternal master of dharma be attached to another’s wife? / Wise men say that even the Lord experiences the fruit of the deeds he has done. / Just as I was brought to delusion by you, a false ascetic, / so too will some false ascetic carry off your wife!”

5.15.s:
iti śaptastathā viṣṇurjagāmādṛśyatāṃ kṣaṇāt

prāha niḥśvasya caivoṣṇaṃ rājñī vṛṃdātiduḥkhitā 58
5.15.d:
इति शप्तस्तथा विष्णुर्जगामादृश्यतां क्षणात्
सा चित्रशालापर्यंकः स च तेऽथप्लवंगमाः 55
नष्टं सर्वं हरौ याते वनं शून्यं विलोक्य सा
वृंदा प्राह सखीं प्राप्य जिह्मं तद्विष्णुना कृतम् 56
त्यक्तं पुरं गतं राज्यं कांतः संदेहतां गतः
अहं वने विदित्वैतत्क्व यामि विधिनिर्मिता 57
मनोरथानां विषयमभून्मे प्रियदर्शनम्
प्राह निःश्वस्य चैवोष्णं राज्ञी वृंदातिदुःखिता 58
5.15.m: Cursed thus, Viṣṇu vanished in an instant; / that painted chamber, the couch, and those monkeys— / all disappeared when Hari went away. Seeing the forest empty, / Vṛndā reached her female friend and said, “A crooked deed was done by that Viṣṇu! / The city is abandoned, the kingdom gone, my beloved is uncertain; / having found this out in the forest, where shall I go, fashioned by destiny? / The sight of my beloved has become only an object of my daydreams!” / So spoke Queen Vṛndā, sighing hotly, intensely sorrowful.

5.15.s:
mama prāptaṃ hi maraṇaṃ tvayā hi smaradūtike

tapaścacārasātyugraṃ nirāhārā sakhīsamam 62
5.15.d:
मम प्राप्तं हि मरणं त्वया हि स्मरदूतिके
इत्युक्ता सा तया प्राह मम त्वं प्राणरूपिणी 59
तस्यास्तथोक्तमाकर्ण्य इतिकर्त्तव्यतां ततः
वने निश्चित्य सा वृंदा गत्वा तत्र महत्सरः 60
विहाय दुःखमकरोद्गात्रक्षालनमंबुना
तीरे पद्मासनं बद्ध्वा कृत्वा निर्विषयं मनः 61
शोषयामास देहं स्वं विष्णुसंगेन दूषितम्
तपश्चचारसात्युग्रं निराहारा सखीसमम् 62
5.15.m:
"Indeed, my death has arrived through you, messenger of Love!"
Addressed thus by her, she replied, "You are my very life."
Having heard what she said, and then having determined in the forest
what must be done, that Vṛndā went there to a great lake.
Casting off her sorrow, she washed her limbs with water.
Assuming the lotus posture on the shore and making her mind free of sense-objects,
she dried up her own body which had been defiled by union with Viṣṇu.
Deprived of food, she performed exceedingly severe austerity along with her companion.

5.15.s:

गंधर्वलोकतो वृंदामथागत्याप्सरोगणः
प्राह याहीति कल्याणि स्वर्गं मा त्यज विग्रहम् 63

नीतो येनेह वृंदे त्यजसि कथमिदं तद्वपुः प्राप्तकामम्
कांतं ते विद्धि शूलिप्रवरशरहतं पुण्यलाभस्य भूषास्वर्गस्य त्वं
भवाद्य द्रुतममरवनं चंडिभद्रे भज त्वम् 64
श्रुत्वा शास्त्रं वधूनां जलधिजदयिता वाक्यमाह प्रहस्य
स्वर्गादाहृत्य मुक्तात्रिदशपति वधूश्चातिवीरेण पत्या
5.15.m:
Then a host of apsarases, having arrived at Vṛndā from the world of the gandharvas,
said: "O auspicious woman, go to heaven; do not abandon your body!
This Gandharva weapon conquers the three worlds, by which the Lord of Śrī was brought here to supreme satisfaction;
why do you abandon this body, O Vṛndā, that has attained [all] desire?
Know that your beloved has been slain by the excellent arrow of the bearer of the trident. You are an ornament yielding merit;
become one belonging to heaven today, quickly, O fierce and auspicious lady, and resort to the grove of the immortals!"
Having heard the instruction of the wives, the beloved of the ocean-born one, laughing, spoke this word:
"Having been carried away from heaven, the wives of the lord of the gods were released by my exceedingly heroic husband.

5.15.s:
ādau pātraṃ sukhānāmahamamarajitā preyasā tadviyuktānirduṣṭā tadya

viṣayebhyaḥ samāhṛtya manaḥ prāpa tataḥ param 67

tuṣṭuvurnabhasastuṣṭā vavṛṣuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭibhiḥ 68

तिष्ये प्रियममृतगतं प्राप्नुयां येन चैव 65

तत्प्रीतिपाशबद्धास्ता नित्यमायांति यांति च 66

विषयेभ्यः समाहृत्य मनः प्राप ततः परम् 67
दृष्ट्वा वृंदारिकां तत्र महांतश्चाप्सरोगणाः
तुष्टुवुर्नभसस्तुष्टा ववृषुः पुष्पवृष्टिभिः 68
5.15.m:
At first I was the vessel of joys with my beloved who conquered the immortals; now separated from him,
blameless, I will strive so that I may indeed reach my beloved who has attained immortality."
Having spoken thus, Vṛndā, together with her companion, dismissed the hosts of apsarases;
bound by the bonds of love for her, they constantly came and went.
Then Vṛndā, having burned away the qualities with the fire of knowledge through the practice of yoga,
and having withdrawn her mind from the sense-objects, attained the Supreme beyond them.
Seeing Vṛndārikā there, the great hosts of apsarases
were pleased and praised [her] from the sky and rained down showers of flowers.

5.15.s:
śuṣkakāṣṭhacayaṃ kṛtvā tatra vṛṃdākalevaram
nidhāyāgniṃ ca prajvālya smaradūtī viveśa tam 69
dagdhaṃ vṛṃdāṃgarajasāṃ biṃbaṃ tadgolakātmakam
kṛtvā tadbhasmanaḥ śeṣaṃ maṃdākinyāṃ vicikṣipuḥ 70
yatra vṛṃdā parityajya dehaṃ brahmapathaṃ gatā
āsīdvṛṃdāvanaṃ tatra govarddhanasamīpataḥ 71
devyo'tha svargametya tridaśapativadhūsattvasaṃpattimāhurdevībhyastanniśamya pramuditamanaso nirjarādyāśca sarve
śatrordaityasya hitvā prabalatarabhayaṃ bhīmabheryo nijaghnuḥ śrutvā tatrāsanasthaḥ
5.15.d:
शुष्ककाष्ठचयं कृत्वा तत्र वृंदाकलेवरम्
निधायाग्निं च प्रज्वाल्य स्मरदूती विवेश तम् 69
दग्धं वृंदांगरजसां बिंबं तद्गोलकात्मकम्
कृत्वा तद्भस्मनः शेषं मंदाकिन्यां विचिक्षिपुः 70
यत्र वृंदा परित्यज्य देहं ब्रह्मपथं गता
आसीद्वृंदावनं तत्र गोवर्द्धनसमीपतः 71
देव्योऽथ स्वर्गमेत्य त्रिदशपतिवधूसत्त्वसंपत्तिमाहुर्देवीभ्यस्तन्निशम्य प्रमुदितमनसो निर्जराद्याश्च सर्वे
शत्रोर्दैत्यस्य हित्वा प्रबलतरभयं भीमभेर्यो निजघ्नुः श्रुत्वा तत्रासनस्थः
5.15.m:
Having made a pile of dry wood and placed Vṛndā's corpse there,
and having ignited the fire, the messenger of Love entered it.
Having made a spherical globe from the burnt remnants of the dust of Vṛndā's body,
they cast the rest of the ashes into the Mandākinī.
Where Vṛndā abandoned her body and went along the path of Brahman,
there, near Govardhana, was Vṛndāvana.
Then the divine women, having reached heaven, reported the abundance of virtue of the wife of the lord of gods [and Jalandhara]; having heard that from the goddesses, the gods and all were joyful at heart.
Casting off the exceedingly strong fear of the enemy demon, they beat fierce kettledrums; having heard [this], seated on their seats there,
the throng of attendants attained the splendor of good fortune.

5.15.s:
parijananivahovāpaśobhāṃ śubhasya 72
iti śrīpādme mahāpurāṇe uttarakhaṃḍe paṃcapaṃcāśatasahasrasaṃhitāyāṃ jālaṃdharopākhyāne vṛṃdāyā brahmapadaprāptirnāma paṃcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ 15
5.15.d:
परिजननिवहोवापशोभां शुभस्य 72
इति श्रीपाद्मे महापुराणे उत्तरखंडे पंचपंचाशतसहस्रसंहितायां जालंधरोपाख्याने वृंदाया ब्रह्मपदप्राप्तिर्नाम पंचदशोऽध्यायः 15
5.15.m: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named "Attainment of the Abode of Brahman by Vṛndā," in the story of Jalandhara, in the fifty-five-thousand verse compilation of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Mahāpurāṇa of Padma.

5.16.s:
.. .. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tyaktvā'nyā nikhilāḥ kriyāḥ ..
raktaśṛṃgasya sāṃnidhyaṃ sevanīyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 1 ..
5.16.d:
.. .. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन त्यक्त्वाऽन्या निखिलाः क्रियाः ..
रक्तशृंगस्य सांनिध्यं सेवनीयं विचक्षणैः .. 1 ..
5.16.m:
Sūta said:
Therefore, with every effort, abandoning all other rites,
the wise should resort to the presence of Raktaśṛṅga. 1

5.16.s:
kiṃ dānaiḥ kiṃ kriyākāṃḍaiḥ kiṃ yajñaiḥ kiṃ vratairapi ..
tatkṣetraṃ sevayedbhaktyā hāṭakeśvarasaṃbhavam ..2..
5.16.d:
किं दानैः किं क्रियाकांडैः किं यज्ञैः किं व्रतैरपि ..
तत्क्षेत्रं सेवयेद्भक्त्या हाटकेश्वरसंभवम् ..2..
5.16.m:
What is the use of gifts? What of ritual codes? What of sacrifices? What even of vows?
One should with devotion resort to that sacred field arisen from Hāṭakeśvara. 2

5.16.s:
agniṣṭomādayo yajñāḥ sarve saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇāḥ ..
tasya kṣetrasya purataḥ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm .. 3 ..
5.16.d:
अग्निष्टोमादयो यज्ञाः सर्वे संपूर्णदक्षिणाः ..
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य पुरतः कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम् .. 3 ..
5.16.m:
The Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices, all with full sacrificial fees,
do not equal a sixteenth part before that sacred field. 3

5.16.s:
cāndrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tathā sāṃtapanāni ca ..
tasya kṣetrasya purataḥ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm..4..
5.16.d:
चान्द्रायणानि कृच्छ्राणि तथा सांतपनानि च ..
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य पुरतः कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम्..4..
5.16.m:
The Cāndrāyaṇa, Kṛcchra, and Sāṃtapana penances
do not equal a sixteenth part before that sacred field. 4

5.16.s:
prabhāsādyāni tīrthāni gaṅgādyāḥ saritastathā ..
tasya kṣetrasya purataḥ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm..5..
5.16.d:
प्रभासाद्यानि तीर्थानि गङ्गाद्याः सरितस्तथा ..
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य पुरतः कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम्..5..
5.16.m:
Prabhāsa and the other sacred fords, and likewise the Gaṅgā and other rivers,
do not equal a sixteenth part before that sacred field. 5

5.16.s:
bhūmidānāni sarvāṇi dharmāḥ sarve dayādikāḥ..
tasya kṣetrasya purataḥ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm..6..
5.16.d:
भूमिदानानि सर्वाणि धर्माः सर्वे दयादिकाः..
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य पुरतः कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम्..6..
5.16.m:
All gifts of land, all virtues such as compassion,
do not equal a sixteenth part before that sacred field. 6

5.16.s:
tatra rājarṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ prabhūtāḥ siddhimāgatāḥ ..
paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarpāḥ siṃhavyāghrā mṛgādayaḥ ..7..
5.16.d:
तत्र राजर्षयः पूर्वं प्रभूताः सिद्धिमागताः ..
पशवः पक्षिणः सर्पाः सिंहव्याघ्रा मृगादयः ..7..
5.16.m:
Many royal seers reached perfection there in former times.
Beasts, birds, serpents, lions, tigers, deer, and others, 7

5.16.s:
tatra kālavaśānnaṣṭāste'pi prāptā divālayam ..
yastatra vratahīno'pi kṛṣikarmarato'pi vā ..9..
nivāsaṃ kurute viprā mṛtastatra divaṃ vrajet ..
kiṃvā ca bahunoktena bhūyobhūyo dvijottamāḥ ..9..
5.16.d:
तत्र कालवशान्नष्टास्तेऽपि प्राप्ता दिवालयम् ..
यस्तत्र व्रतहीनोऽपि कृषिकर्मरतोऽपि वा ..9..
निवासं कुरुते विप्रा मृतस्तत्र दिवं व्रजेत् ..
किंवा च बहुनोक्तेन भूयोभूयो द्विजोत्तमाः ..9..
5.16.m:
perished there by the power of Time, and even they reached the abode of the gods.
Whoever, even though devoid of vows or engaged in the work of farming, 8
dwells there, O brahmins, goes to heaven when dead.
Or what need is there of saying much, again and again, O best of the twice-born? 9

5.16.s:
śrūyatāṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ tasya kṣetrasya saṃbhavam ..
punaṃti kṣetratīrthāni saṃvāsādiha mānavān .. 6.16.10 ..
5.16.d:
श्रूयतां परमं गुह्यं तस्य क्षेत्रस्य संभवम् ..
पुनंति क्षेत्रतीर्थानि संवासादिह मानवान् .. 6.16.10 ..
5.16.m:
Let the supreme secret relating to that sacred field be heard:
Sacred fields and sacred fords purify human beings here by dwelling [there]. 10

5.16.s:
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ punāti smaraṇādapi ..
kiṃ punardarśanādviprāḥ sparśanācca viśeṣataḥ .. 11 ..
5.16.d:
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं पुनाति स्मरणादपि ..
किं पुनर्दर्शनाद्विप्राः स्पर्शनाच्च विशेषतः .. 11 ..
5.16.m:
The sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara purifies even by remembrance,
how much more then by seeing [it], O brahmins, and especially by touching [it]! 11

5.16.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye raktaśṛṅgasāṃnidhyasevanaphalaśraiṣṭhyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣoḍaśo' dhyāyaḥ..16.. ....
5.16.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये रक्तशृङ्गसांनिध्यसेवनफलश्रैष्ठ्यवर्णनंनाम षोडशो' ध्यायः..16.. ....
5.16.m: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named "Description of the Excellence of the Fruit of Resorting to the Presence of Raktaśṛṅga," in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section] in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa in eighty-one thousand verses.

5.17.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
camatkārapurotpattiḥ śrutā tvatto mahāmate ..
tatkṣetrasya pramāṇaṃ yattadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya .....
yāni tatra ca puṇyāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca ..
sahitāni prabhāveṇa tāni sarvāṇi kīrtaya .. 2 ..
5.17.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
चमत्कारपुरोत्पत्तिः श्रुता त्वत्तो महामते ..
तत्क्षेत्रस्य प्रमाणं यत्तदस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .....
यानि तत्र च पुण्यानि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च ..
सहितानि प्रभावेण तानि सर्वाणि कीर्तय .. 2 ..
5.17.m:
The seers said:
The origin of Camatkārapura has been heard from you, O noble-minded one.
Proclaim to us the extent of that sacred field, 1
and whatever auspicious sacred fords and temples are there,
together with their power—proclaim them all! 2

5.17.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
pañcakrośapramāṇena kṣetraṃ brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
āyāmavyāsataścaiva camatkārapurottamam .. 3 ..
5.17.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पञ्चक्रोशप्रमाणेन क्षेत्रं ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
आयामव्यासतश्चैव चमत्कारपुरोत्तमम् .. 3 ..
5.17.m:
Sūta said:
The sacred field, the excellent Camatkārapura, O best of brahmins,
is five krośas in measure, both in length and in breadth. 3

5.17.s:
prācyāṃ tasya gayāśīrṣaṃ paścimena hareḥ padam ..
dakṣiṇottarayoścaiva gokarṇeśvarasaṃjñitau ..4..
5.17.d:
प्राच्यां तस्य गयाशीर्षं पश्चिमेन हरेः पदम् ..
दक्षिणोत्तरयोश्चैव गोकर्णेश्वरसंज्ञितौ ..4..
5.17.m:
To its east is Gayāśīrṣa; to the west is the foot of Hari;
and to the south and north are the two called Gokarṇeśvara. 4

5.17.s:
hāṭakeśvara saṃjñaṃ tu pūrvamāsīddvijottamāḥ ..
tatkṣetraṃ prathitaṃ loke sarvapātakanāśanam .. 5 ..
5.17.d:
हाटकेश्वर संज्ञं तु पूर्वमासीद्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तत्क्षेत्रं प्रथितं लोके सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 5 ..
5.17.m:
In former times, O best of the twice-born, it was called Hāṭakeśvara;
that sacred field, celebrated in the world, destroys all sins. 5

5.17.s:
yataḥ prabhṛti viprebhyo dattaṃ tena mahātmanā ..
camatkāreṇa tatsthānaṃ nāmnā khyātiṃ tato gatam .. 6 ..
5.17.d:
यतः प्रभृति विप्रेभ्यो दत्तं तेन महात्मना ..
चमत्कारेण तत्स्थानं नाम्ना ख्यातिं ततो गतम् .. 6 ..
5.17.m:
From the time it was given to the brahmins by that great soul,
Camatkāra, that place attained renown by his name. 6

5.17.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tasya pūrve gayāśiraḥ ..
māhātmyaṃ tasya no brūhi sūtaputra savistaram .. 7 ..
5.17.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
यदेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं तस्य पूर्वे गयाशिरः ..
माहात्म्यं तस्य नो ब्रूहि सूतपुत्र सविस्तरम् .. 7 ..
5.17.m:
The brahmins said:
That which was spoken of by you as Gayāśiras to the east of it—
tell us its māhātmya in detail, O son of Sūta. 7

5.17.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
āsīdvidūrathonāma haihayādhipatiḥ purā ..
yo vai dānapatirdakṣaḥ śatrupakṣakṣayāvahaḥ .. 8 ..
5.17.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
आसीद्विदूरथोनाम हैहयाधिपतिः पुरा ..
यो वै दानपतिर्दक्षः शत्रुपक्षक्षयावहः .. 8 ..
5.17.m:
Sūta said:
Formerly there was a king of the Haihayas named Vidūratha,
who was indeed a master of giving, skilled, bringing destruction to the faction of his enemies. 8

5.17.s:
sa kadācinmṛgānhaṃtuṃ nṛpaḥ senāvṛto yayau ..
nānāvṛkṣalatākīrṇaṃ vanaṃ śvāpadasaṃkulam .. 9 ..
5.17.d:
स कदाचिन्मृगान्हंतुं नृपः सेनावृतो ययौ ..
नानावृक्षलताकीर्णं वनं श्वापदसंकुलम् .. 9 ..
5.17.m:
Once, surrounded by his army, that king went out to hunt deer
in a forest filled with various trees and creepers, thronged with beasts of prey. 9

5.17.s:
sa jaghāna mṛgāṃstatra śarairāśīviṣopamaiḥ ..
mahiṣāṃścavarāhāṃśca tarakṣūñcchambarānrurūn .. 6.17.10 ..
5.17.d:
स जघान मृगांस्तत्र शरैराशीविषोपमैः ..
महिषांश्चवराहांश्च तरक्षूञ्च्छम्बरान्रुरून् .. 6.17.10 ..
5.17.m:
There he struck deer with arrows resembling venomous serpents,
as well as buffaloes, boars, hyenas, sambar, and ruru deer, 10

5.17.s:
siṃhānvyāghrāngajānmattāñcchataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
atha tena mṛgo viddhaḥ śareṇā''nataparvaṇā .. 11 ..
5.17.d:
सिंहान्व्याघ्रान्गजान्मत्ताञ्च्छतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ..
अथ तेन मृगो विद्धः शरेणा'ऽनतपर्वणा .. 11 ..
5.17.m:
lions, tigers, and rutting elephants by the hundreds and thousands.
Then a deer, pierced by him with a bent-jointed arrow, 11

5.17.s:
na papāta dharāpṛṣṭhe saśaro dudruve drutam..
tataḥ sa kautukāviṣṭastasya pṛṣṭhe hayottamam ..
prerayāmāsa vegena manomārutavegadhṛk .. 12 ..
5.17.d:
न पपात धरापृष्ठे सशरो दुद्रुवे द्रुतम्..
ततः स कौतुकाविष्टस्तस्य पृष्ठे हयोत्तमम् ..
प्रेरयामास वेगेन मनोमारुतवेगधृक् .. 12 ..
5.17.m:
did not fall to the surface of the earth, [but] quickly ran away with the arrow.
Then, seized with wonder, he spurred an excellent horse behind it
with speed, bearing the velocity of the mind and the wind. 12

5.17.s:
tataḥ sainyaṃ samutsajya mṛgaṃ lipsurmahīpatiḥ ..
anyadvanāṃtaraṃ prāpto raudraṃ cittabhayāvaham .. 13 ..
5.17.d:
ततः सैन्यं समुत्सज्य मृगं लिप्सुर्महीपतिः ..
अन्यद्वनांतरं प्राप्तो रौद्रं चित्तभयावहम् .. 13 ..
5.17.m: Then, abandoning his army, the king, eager to catch the deer, / entered another forest, terrible and frightful to the mind,

5.17.s:
kaṇṭakībadarīprāyaṃ śālmalīvanasaṃkulam ..
tathānyaiḥ kaṇṭakākīrṇai rūkṣai rvṛkṣaiḥ samanvitam .. 14 ..
5.17.d:
कण्टकीबदरीप्रायं शाल्मलीवनसंकुलम् ..
तथान्यैः कण्टकाकीर्णै रूक्षै र्वृक्षैः समन्वितम् .. 14 ..
5.17.m: consisting mostly of thorny jujube bushes, crowded with groves of silk-cotton trees, / and filled with other dry trees bristling with thorns.

5.17.s:
tatra rūkṣā'khilā bhūmirnirjalā tamasā vṛtā ..
cīrikolūkagṛdhāḍhyā śīrṣacchāyāvivarjitā .. 15 ..
5.17.d:
तत्र रूक्षाऽखिला भूमिर्निर्जला तमसा वृता ..
चीरिकोलूकगृधाढ्या शीर्षच्छायाविवर्जिता .. 15 ..
5.17.m: There the ground was entirely dry, waterless, covered in darkness, / full of crickets, owls, and vultures, and devoid of shade for one's head.

5.17.s:
grīṣme madhyagate sūrye mṛgākṛṣṭaḥ sa pārthivaḥ ..
dūrādhvānaṃ jagāmā'tha prāsapāṇirvarāśvagaḥ .. 16 ..
5.17.d:
ग्रीष्मे मध्यगते सूर्ये मृगाकृष्टः स पार्थिवः ..
दूराध्वानं जगामाऽथ प्रासपाणिर्वराश्वगः .. 16 ..
5.17.m: In the summer, when the sun was at its zenith, drawn by the deer, the king, / holding a spear in his hand and riding an excellent horse, then travelled a great distance.

5.17.s:
tena tasyānugā bhṛtyāḥ sarve suśrāṃtavāhanāḥ ..
kṣutpipāsākulāḥ śrāṃtāḥ sthāne sthāne samāśritāḥ .. 17 ..
5.17.d:
तेन तस्यानुगा भृत्याः सर्वे सुश्रांतवाहनाः ..
क्षुत्पिपासाकुलाः श्रांताः स्थाने स्थाने समाश्रिताः .. 17 ..
5.17.m: Because of that, all his following servants, their mounts utterly exhausted, / overcome by hunger and thirst, and weary, collapsed at various spots.

5.17.s:
siṃhavyāghraistathā cānyaiḥ patitā naṣṭacetanāḥ ..
bhakṣyaṃte cetayanto'pi tathā'nye calanākṣamāḥ .. 18 ..
5.17.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रैस्तथा चान्यैः पतिता नष्टचेतनाः ..
भक्ष्यंते चेतयन्तोऽपि तथाऽन्ये चलनाक्षमाः .. 18 ..
5.17.m: Having fallen unconscious, they were devoured by lions, tigers, and others; / and others, unable to move, were devoured even while conscious.

5.17.s:
tataḥ so'pi mahīpālaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamākulaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā tadvyasanaṃ prāptamātmanaḥ sevakaiḥ samam .. 19 ..
5.17.d:
ततः सोऽपि महीपालः क्षुत्पिपासासमाकुलः ..
दृष्ट्वा तद्व्यसनं प्राप्तमात्मनः सेवकैः समम् .. 19 ..
5.17.m: Then the king too, overcome by hunger and thirst, / seeing that disaster had befallen him along with his servants,

5.17.s:
kāṃtārasyāṃtamanvicchanprerayāmāsa taṃ hayam..
jātyaṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ kaśāghātaiḥ pratāḍayan .. 6.17.20 ..
5.17.d:
कांतारस्यांतमन्विच्छन्प्रेरयामास तं हयम्..
जात्यं सर्वगुणोपेतं कशाघातैः प्रताडयन् .. 6.17.20 ..
5.17.m: seeking the end of the wilderness, spurred on that horse, / a noble steed endowed with every excellence, striking it with lashes of the whip.

5.17.s:
tataḥ sa nṛpatistena vāyuvegena vājinā ..
nīto dūraṃ durgamārgaṃ sarvajaṃtuvivarjitam .. 21 ..
5.17.d:
ततः स नृपतिस्तेन वायुवेगेन वाजिना ..
नीतो दूरं दुर्गमार्गं सर्वजंतुविवर्जितम् .. 21 ..
5.17.m: Then that king was carried far along a difficult path, / devoid of all living creatures, by that horse swift as the wind.

5.17.s:
evaṃ tasya narendrasya kāṃdiśīke'navasthite ..
so'śvo'pataddharāpṛṣṭhe so'pyadhastātturaṃgamāt .. 22 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye vidūrathamṛgayāvarṇanaṃnāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 17 .. .. cha .. ..
5.17.d:
एवं तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य कांदिशीकेऽनवस्थिते ..
सोऽश्वोऽपतद्धरापृष्ठे सोऽप्यधस्तात्तुरंगमात् .. 22 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये विदूरथमृगयावर्णनंनाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः .. 17 .. .. छ .. ..
5.17.m:
Thus, while that king was panicked and unsteady, / that horse fell to the surface of the earth, and he too fell down from the horse.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, named 'Description of Vidūratha's Hunt', in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.18.s:
sūta uvāca .. ..
tataḥ so'pi mahīpālaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamākulaḥ ..
papāta dharaṇīpṛṣṭhe padbhyāṃ gatvā vanāṃtaram .. 1 ..
5.18.d:
सूत उवाच .. ..
ततः सोऽपि महीपालः क्षुत्पिपासासमाकुलः ..
पपात धरणीपृष्ठे पद्भ्यां गत्वा वनांतरम् .. 1 ..
5.18.m: Sūta said: / Then that king too, overcome by hunger and thirst, / having walked to another forest on foot, fell to the surface of the earth.

5.18.s:
athā'paśyadviyatsthānātsa trīnpretānsu dāruṇān ..
ūrdhvakeśānsuraktākṣānkṛṣṇadantānkṛśodarān .. 2 ..
5.18.d:
अथाऽपश्यद्वियत्स्थानात्स त्रीन्प्रेतान्सु दारुणान् ..
ऊर्ध्वकेशान्सुरक्ताक्षान्कृष्णदन्तान्कृशोदरान् .. 2 ..
5.18.m: Then, from the sky, he saw three very terrible ghosts (pretas), / with upright hair, blood-red eyes, black teeth, and emaciated bellies.

5.18.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā bhayasaṃtrasto viśeṣeṇa sa bhūpatiḥ ..
nirāśo jīvite kṛcchrādidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 3 ..
5.18.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा भयसंत्रस्तो विशेषेण स भूपतिः ..
निराशो जीविते कृच्छ्रादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 3 ..
5.18.m: Seeing them, the king, extremely terrified with fear, / despairing of his life, spoke these words with difficulty:

5.18.s:
ke yūyaṃ vikṛtākārā mayā dṛṣṭā na karhicit ..
evaṃvidhā nṛloke'tra bhramatā prāgvibhīṣaṇāḥ .. 4 ..
5.18.d:
के यूयं विकृताकारा मया दृष्टा न कर्हिचित् ..
एवंविधा नृलोकेऽत्र भ्रमता प्राग्विभीषणाः .. 4 ..
5.18.m: “Who are you of deformed appearance, such terrifying forms as have never been seen / by me wandering in this world of mortals before?

5.18.s:
vidūratho narendro'haṃ kṣutpipāsātipīḍitaḥ ..
mṛgalipsuriha prāpto vane jantuvivarjite .. 5 ..
5.18.d:
विदूरथो नरेन्द्रोऽहं क्षुत्पिपासातिपीडितः ..
मृगलिप्सुरिह प्राप्तो वने जन्तुविवर्जिते .. 5 ..
5.18.m: I am King Vidūratha, extremely afflicted by hunger and thirst; / eager to catch a deer, I have arrived here in a forest devoid of living creatures.”

5.18.s:
tatasteṣāṃ tu yo jyeṣṭho māṃsādaḥ pratyuvāca tam ..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ . 6 ..
5.18.d:
ततस्तेषां तु यो ज्येष्ठो मांसादः प्रत्युवाच तम् ..
कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा विनयावनतः स्थितः . 6 ..
5.18.m: Then the eldest of them, Māṃsāda, replied to him, / standing with folded hands and bowed in modesty:

5.18.s:
vayaṃ pretā mahārāja nivasāmo'tra kānane ..
svakarmajanitāddoṣādduḥkhena mahatā vṛtāḥ .. 7 ..
5.18.d:
वयं प्रेता महाराज निवसामोऽत्र कानने ..
स्वकर्मजनिताद्दोषाद्दुःखेन महता वृताः .. 7 ..
5.18.m: “We are ghosts, O great king, dwelling in this forest, / overwhelmed with great suffering because of the fault born of our own actions.

5.18.s:
ahaṃ māṃsādakonāma dvitīyo'yaṃ vidaivataḥ ..
kṛtaghnaśca tṛtīyastu trayāṇāmeṣa pāpakṛt .. 8 .
5.18.d:
अहं मांसादकोनाम द्वितीयोऽयं विदैवतः ..
कृतघ्नश्च तृतीयस्तु त्रयाणामेष पापकृत् .. 8 .
5.18.m: I am named Māṃsāda; this second one is Vidaivata; / and the third is Kṛtaghna, the evil-doer among the three.”

5.18.s:
..rājovāca .. ..
sarveṣāṃ dehi nāṃ nāma jāyate pitṛmātṛjam ..
kimetatkāraṇaṃ yena sarve yūyaṃ svanāmakāḥ .. 9 ..
5.18.d:
..राजोवाच .. ..
सर्वेषां देहि नां नाम जायते पितृमातृजम् ..
किमेतत्कारणं येन सर्वे यूयं स्वनामकाः .. 9 ..
5.18.m: The king said: / “The name of every embodied being is given by father and mother; / what is the reason that all of you have such self-coined names?”

5.18.s:
tacchrutvā prāha māṃsādaḥ karmanāmāni pārthiva ..
mithaḥ kṛtāni saṃjñārthamasmābhiḥ svayameva hi . 6.18.10 ..
5.18.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह मांसादः कर्मनामानि पार्थिव ..
मिथः कृतानि संज्ञार्थमस्माभिः स्वयमेव हि . 6.18.10 ..
5.18.m: Hearing that, Māṃsāda said: “O king, these are names based on our actions, / made among ourselves by our own accord for the sake of identification.

5.18.s:
śṛṇuṣvā'vahito bhūtvā sarveṣāṃ naḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
karmaṇā yena saṃjātaṃ pretatvamiha bhūmipa .. 11 ..
5.18.d:
शृणुष्वाऽवहितो भूत्वा सर्वेषां नः पृथक्पृथक् ..
