कर्मणा येन संजातं प्रेतत्वमिह भूमिप .. 11 ..
5.18.m: Listen attentively, each of us in turn, / to the action by which the state of a ghost arose here for us, O protector of the earth.

5.18.s:
vayaṃ hi brāhmaṇā jātyā vaidiśākhye pure nṛpa ..
devarātasya viprasya gṛhe jātā mahātmanaḥ .. 12 ..
5.18.d:
वयं हि ब्राह्मणा जात्या वैदिशाख्ये पुरे नृप ..
देवरातस्य विप्रस्य गृहे जाता महात्मनः .. 12 ..
5.18.m: We are indeed brahmins by birth, O king, born in the city named Vaidiśa, / in the house of the high-souled brahmin Devarāta.

5.18.s:
nāstikā bhinnamaryādāḥ paradāraratāḥ sadā ..
pāpa karmaratāstatra śubhakarmavivarjitāḥ .. 13 ..
5.18.d:
नास्तिका भिन्नमर्यादाः परदाररताः सदा ..
पाप कर्मरतास्तत्र शुभकर्मविवर्जिताः .. 13 ..
5.18.m: We were atheists, transgressors of proper conduct, constantly devoted to other men's wives, / there engaged in sinful deeds and devoid of auspicious acts.

5.18.s:
jihvālaulyaprasaṃgena mayā bhuktaṃ sadā''miṣam ..
tena me karmajaṃ nāma māṃsādākhyaṃ vyavasthitam .. 14 ..
5.18.d:
जिह्वालौल्यप्रसंगेन मया भुक्तं सदा'ऽमिषम् ..
तेन मे कर्मजं नाम मांसादाख्यं व्यवस्थितम् .. 14 ..
5.18.m: Due to the indulgence of the craving of my tongue, meat was constantly eaten by me; / therefore, a name born of my action, known as 'Māṃsāda' (Meat-eater), was fixed for me.

5.18.s:
dvitīyo'yaṃ mahārāja yastiṣṭhati tavā'grataḥ ..
anenā'nnaṃ sadā bhuktamakṛtvā devatārcanam .. 15 ..
5.18.d:
द्वितीयोऽयं महाराज यस्तिष्ठति तवाऽग्रतः ..
अनेनाऽन्नं सदा भुक्तमकृत्वा देवतार्चनम् .. 15 ..
5.18.m: This second one, O great king, who stands before you, / by him food was always eaten without performing the worship of deities.

5.18.s:
tena karmavipākena pretayoniṃ samāśritaḥ ..
vidaivata iti khyāto dvitīyo'yaṃ supāpakṛt .. 16 ..
5.18.d:
तेन कर्मविपाकेन प्रेतयोनिं समाश्रितः ..
विदैवत इति ख्यातो द्वितीयोऽयं सुपापकृत् .. 16 ..
5.18.m: By that ripening of karma, he attained the womb of a ghost; / this second one, an extreme evil-doer, is renowned as 'Vidaivata' (Godless).

5.18.s:
sadaivā'nuṣṭhitā'nena supāpena kṛtaghnatā ..
kṛtaghnaḥ procyate tena karmaṇā nṛpasattama .. 17 .. ..
5.18.d:
सदैवाऽनुष्ठिताऽनेन सुपापेन कृतघ्नता ..
कृतघ्नः प्रोच्यते तेन कर्मणा नृपसत्तम .. 17 .. ..
5.18.m: Ungratefulness was constantly practiced by this extremely sinful one; / therefore, by that action he is called 'Kṛtaghna' (Ungrateful), O best of kings.”

5.18.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
āhāreṇa nṛloke'sminsarve jīvanti jantavaḥ ..
yuṣmākaṃ katamo yo'tra procyatāṃ me savistaram .. 18 ..
5.18.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
आहारेण नृलोकेऽस्मिन्सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः ..
युष्माकं कतमो योऽत्र प्रोच्यतां मे सविस्तरम् .. 18 ..
5.18.m: The king said: / “In this world of mortals, all creatures live by food; / which [food] is yours here? Tell me in detail.”

5.18.s:
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
bhojyakāle gṛhe yatra strīṇāṃ yuddhaṃ pravartate .
api mantrauṣadhīprāyaṃ pretā bhuṃjati tatra hi .. 19 ..
5.18.d:
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
भोज्यकाले गृहे यत्र स्त्रीणां युद्धं प्रवर्तते .
अपि मन्त्रौषधीप्रायं प्रेता भुंजति तत्र हि .. 19 ..
5.18.m: Māṃsāda said: / “In a house where a quarrel of women occurs at mealtime, / even if it consists mostly of spells and herbs, ghosts eat there indeed.

5.18.s:
bhujyate yatra bhūpāla veṃśvadevaṃ vinā naraiḥ ..
pākasyāgramadattvā ca pretā bhuṃjati tatra ca .. 6.18.20 ..
5.18.d:
भुज्यते यत्र भूपाल वेंश्वदेवं विना नरैः ..
पाकस्याग्रमदत्त्वा च प्रेता भुंजति तत्र च .. 6.18.20 ..
5.18.m: Where food is eaten by men without the Vaiśvadeva rite, O king, / and without giving the first portion of the cooked food, ghosts eat there too.

5.18.s:
rātrau yatkriyate śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ vā parvavarjitam..
tatsarvaṃ nṛpaśārdūla pretānāṃ bhojanaṃ bhavet.. .. 21 ..
5.18.d:
रात्रौ यत्क्रियते श्राद्धं दानं वा पर्ववर्जितम्..
तत्सर्वं नृपशार्दूल प्रेतानां भोजनं भवेत्.. .. 21 ..
5.18.m: A śrāddha that is performed at night, or a gift [given] outside of auspicious occasions— / all that, O tiger among kings, becomes food for ghosts.

5.18.s:
yasminno mārjanaṃ harmye kriyate nopalepanam ..
na māṃgalyaṃ ca satkāraḥ pretā bhuṃjati tatra hi .. 22 ..
5.18.d:
यस्मिन्नो मार्जनं हर्म्ये क्रियते नोपलेपनम् ..
न मांगल्यं च सत्कारः प्रेता भुंजति तत्र हि .. 22 ..
5.18.m: In a mansion where no sweeping is done nor plastering with cow dung, / and where there is no auspiciousness and no hospitality, ghosts eat there indeed.

5.18.s:
bhinnabhāṇḍaparityāgo yatra na kriyate gṛhe ..
na ca vedadhvaniryatra pretā bhuñjaṃti tatra hi ..23..
5.18.d:
भिन्नभाण्डपरित्यागो यत्र न क्रियते गृहे ..
न च वेदध्वनिर्यत्र प्रेता भुञ्जंति तत्र हि ..23..
5.18.m: In a house where the discarding of broken vessels is not done, / and where there is no sound of the Veda, ghosts eat there indeed.

5.18.s:
yacchrāddhaṃ dakṣiṇāhīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ ca vā nṛpa ..
tathā rajasvalādṛṣṭaṃ tadasmākaṃ prajāyate..24..
5.18.d:
यच्छ्राद्धं दक्षिणाहीनं क्रियाहीनं च वा नृप ..
तथा रजस्वलादृष्टं तदस्माकं प्रजायते..24..
5.18.m: A śrāddha that is devoid of sacrificial gifts, O king, or devoid of rites, / and likewise one seen by a menstruating woman, that falls to us.

5.18.s:
hīnāṃgā hyadhikāṃgā vā yasmiñcchrāddhe dvijātayaḥ ..
bhuṃjate vṛṣalīnāthāstadasmākaṃ prajāyate .. 25 ..
5.18.d:
हीनांगा ह्यधिकांगा वा यस्मिञ्च्छ्राद्धे द्विजातयः ..
भुंजते वृषलीनाथास्तदस्माकं प्रजायते .. 25 ..
5.18.m: At a śrāddha where brahmins with missing limbs or extra limbs, / or those who are husbands of Śūdra women, eat, that falls to us.

5.18.s:
atithiryatra saṃprāptaḥ śrāddhakāla upasthite ..
apūjito gṛhādyāti tacchrāddhaṃ pretatṛptidam ..26..
5.18.d:
अतिथिर्यत्र संप्राप्तः श्राद्धकाल उपस्थिते ..
अपूजितो गृहाद्याति तच्छ्राद्धं प्रेततृप्तिदम् ..26..
5.18.m: When a guest arrives as the time of the śrāddha is at hand / and departs from the house unhonored, that śrāddha gives satisfaction to ghosts.

5.18.s:
kiṃ vā te bahunoktena śṛṇu saṃkṣepato nṛpa ..
asmākaṃ bhojanaṃ nityaṃ yattvaṃ śrutvā vigarhasi ..27..
5.18.d:
किं वा ते बहुनोक्तेन शृणु संक्षेपतो नृप ..
अस्माकं भोजनं नित्यं यत्त्वं श्रुत्वा विगर्हसि ..27..
5.18.m: Or what is the use of speaking much to you? Hear in brief, O king, / our constant food, which you will despise upon hearing:

5.18.s:
yadannaṃ keśasūtrāsthiśleṣmādibhirupaplutam ..
hīnajātyaiśca saṃspṛṣṭaṃ tadasmākaṃ prajāyate .. 28 ..
5.18.d:
यदन्नं केशसूत्रास्थिश्लेष्मादिभिरुपप्लुतम् ..
हीनजात्यैश्च संस्पृष्टं तदस्माकं प्रजायते .. 28 ..
5.18.m: Food that is contaminated with hair, thread, bones, mucus, and the like, / and touched by outcasts, that falls to us.”

5.18.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
kena karmavipākena pretatvaṃ jāyate nṛṇām..
etanme sarvamācakṣva māṃsāda mama pṛcchataḥ ..29..
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
yo bhavenmānavaḥ kṣudrastathā paiśunyasūcakaḥ ..
mṛṣṭamāṃsāśane saktaḥ sa preto jāyate naraḥ ..6.18.3...
akṛtvā devakāryaṃ ca tathā ca pitṛtarpaṇam..
yo'śnātyadattvā bhṛtyebhyaḥ sa preto jāyate naraḥ ..3...
5.18.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
केन कर्मविपाकेन प्रेतत्वं जायते नृणाम्..
एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व मांसाद मम पृच्छतः ..29..
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
यो भवेन्मानवः क्षुद्रस्तथा पैशुन्यसूचकः ..
मृष्टमांसाशने सक्तः स प्रेतो जायते नरः ..6.18.3...
अकृत्वा देवकार्यं च तथा च पितृतर्पणम्..
योऽश्नात्यदत्त्वा भृत्येभ्यः स प्रेतो जायते नरः ..3...
5.18.m:
The king said: / “By what ripening of karma does the state of a ghost arise for men? / Tell me all of this, Māṃsāda, as I ask you.”
Māṃsāda said: / “A man who is vile and given to slander, / attached to eating sweet meats—that man is born as a ghost.
And he who eats without performing rites for the gods and libations to ancestors, / and without giving to his servants—that man is born as a ghost.

5.18.s:
paradārarataścaiva paravittāpahārakaḥ ..
parāpavādasaṃtuṣṭaḥ sa preto jāyate naraḥ ..32..
5.18.d:
परदाररतश्चैव परवित्तापहारकः ..
परापवादसंतुष्टः स प्रेतो जायते नरः ..32..
5.18.m: A man devoted to another's wife, a thief of another's wealth, / and one who delights in slandering others is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
kanyāṃ yacchati vṛddhāya nīcāya dhanalipsayā ..
kurūpāya kuśīlāya sa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 33 ..
5.18.d:
कन्यां यच्छति वृद्धाय नीचाय धनलिप्सया ..
कुरूपाय कुशीलाय स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 33 ..
5.18.m: A man who gives his daughter to an old man or a base man out of greed for wealth, / or to an ugly or ill-behaved man, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
kule jātāṃ vinītāṃ ca dharmapatnīṃ sukhocchritām ..
yastyajeddoṣanirmuktāṃ sa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 34 ..
5.18.d:
कुले जातां विनीतां च धर्मपत्नीं सुखोच्छ्रिताम् ..
यस्त्यजेद्दोषनिर्मुक्तां स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 34 ..
5.18.m: A man who abandons his lawful wife born of good family, humble, / thriving in happiness, and free from fault, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
devastrīguruvittāni yo gṛhītvā na yacchati ..
viśeṣādbrāhmaṇasvaṃ ca sa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 35 ..
5.18.d:
देवस्त्रीगुरुवित्तानि यो गृहीत्वा न यच्छति ..
विशेषाद्ब्राह्मणस्वं च स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 35 ..
5.18.m: A man who takes the property of gods, women, or his guru and does not return it, / especially the property of a brahmin, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
paravyasanasaṃtuṣṭaḥ kṛtaghno gurutalpagaḥ ..
dūṣako devaviprāṇāṃ sa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 36 ..
5.18.d:
परव्यसनसंतुष्टः कृतघ्नो गुरुतल्पगः ..
दूषको देवविप्राणां स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 36 ..
5.18.m: A man pleased by another's distress, ungrateful, a violator of the guru's bed, / and a reviler of gods and brahmins, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
dīyamānasya vittasya brāhmaṇebhyaḥ supāpakṛt ..
vighnamārabhate yastu sa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 37 ..
5.18.d:
दीयमानस्य वित्तस्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सुपापकृत् ..
विघ्नमारभते यस्तु स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 37 ..
5.18.m: A man who, committing grave sin, causes an obstacle / to wealth being given to brahmins, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
śūdrānnenodarasthena brāhmaṇo mriyate yadi ..
sa preto jāyate rājanyadyapi syātṣaḍaṃgavit .. 38 ..
5.18.d:
शूद्रान्नेनोदरस्थेन ब्राह्मणो म्रियते यदि ..
स प्रेतो जायते राजन्यद्यपि स्यात्षडंगवित् .. 38 ..
5.18.m: If a brahmin dies with the food of a śūdra in his stomach, / he is born as a preta, O king, even if he knows the six Vedāṅgas.

5.18.s:
kuladeśocitaṃ dharmaṃ yastyaktvā'nyatsamācaret ..
kāmādvā yadi vā lobhātsa preto jāyate naraḥ .. 39 ..
5.18.d:
कुलदेशोचितं धर्मं यस्त्यक्त्वाऽन्यत्समाचरेत् ..
कामाद्वा यदि वा लोभात्स प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 39 ..
5.18.m: A man who abandons the duty proper to his family and region and practices another, / whether out of desire or greed, is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ mayā pārthivasattama ..
yena karmavipākena pretaḥ saṃjāyate naraḥ .. 6.18.40 ..
5.18.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया पार्थिवसत्तम ..
येन कर्मविपाकेन प्रेतः संजायते नरः .. 6.18.40 ..
5.18.m: All this has been related to you by me, O best of kings: / by what ripening of karma a man is born as a preta.

5.18.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
kṛtena karmaṇā yena na preto jāyate naraḥ ..
tanme kīrtaya māṃsāda vistareṇa viśeṣataḥ .. 41 ..
5.18.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
कृतेन कर्मणा येन न प्रेतो जायते नरः ..
तन्मे कीर्तय मांसाद विस्तरेण विशेषतः .. 41 ..
5.18.m:
The king said:
By doing what deed is a man not born as a preta? / Proclaim that to me in detail and particularly, O flesh-eater.

5.18.s:
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
mātṛvatparadārānyaḥ paradravyāṇi loṣṭavat ..
yaḥ paśyatyātmavajjaṃtūnna preto jāyate naraḥ .. 42 ..
5.18.d:
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
मातृवत्परदारान्यः परद्रव्याणि लोष्टवत् ..
यः पश्यत्यात्मवज्जंतून्न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 42 ..
5.18.m:
The flesh-eater said:
A man who regards the wives of others like his mother, the property of others like a clod of earth, / and living beings like himself is not born as a preta.

5.18.s:
annadānaparo nityaṃ viśeṣeṇātithipriyaḥ ..
svādhyāyavrataśīlo yo na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 43 ..
5.18.d:
अन्नदानपरो नित्यं विशेषेणातिथिप्रियः ..
स्वाध्यायव्रतशीलो यो न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 43 ..
5.18.m: A man who is always dedicated to the gift of food, especially fond of guests, / and devoted to the practice of Vedic recitation is not born as a preta.

5.18.s:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samaloṣṭāśmakāṃcanaḥ ..
samo mānāpamāneṣu na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 44 ..
5.18.d:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च समलोष्टाश्मकांचनः ..
समो मानापमानेषु न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 44 ..
5.18.m: A man who is equal toward enemy and friend, to whom a clod, a stone, and gold are equal, / and who is equal in honor and dishonor is not born as a preta.

5.18.s:
dānadharmapravṛttānāṃ dharmamārgā nuyāyinām ..
protsāhaṃ vardhayedyastu na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 49 ..
yūkāmatkuṇadaṃśādīnsarvasattvāni yo naraḥ ..
putravatpālayennityaṃ na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 46 ..
sadā yajñakriyopetaḥ sadā tīrthaparāyaṇaḥ ..
śāstraśravaṇasaṃyukto na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 47 ..
vāpīkūpataḍāgānāmārāmāṇāṃ viśe ṣataḥ ..
āropakaḥ prapāṇāṃ ca na preto jāyate naraḥ .. 48 ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ svaguhyaṃ vasudhādhipa ..
nirviṇṇāḥ pretabhāvena tasmāttvaṃ no gatirbhava .. 49 ..
5.18.d:
दानधर्मप्रवृत्तानां धर्ममार्गा नुयायिनाम् ..
प्रोत्साहं वर्धयेद्यस्तु न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 49 ..
यूकामत्कुणदंशादीन्सर्वसत्त्वानि यो नरः ..
पुत्रवत्पालयेन्नित्यं न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 46 ..
सदा यज्ञक्रियोपेतः सदा तीर्थपरायणः ..
शास्त्रश्रवणसंयुक्तो न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 47 ..
वापीकूपतडागानामारामाणां विशे षतः ..
आरोपकः प्रपाणां च न प्रेतो जायते नरः .. 48 ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं स्वगुह्यं वसुधाधिप ..
निर्विण्णाः प्रेतभावेन तस्मात्त्वं नो गतिर्भव .. 49 ..
5.18.m:
A man who increases the encouragement of those engaged in the duty of giving / and following the path of dharma is not born as a preta.
A man who constantly protects all creatures—lice, bedbugs, / biting gnats, and others—like sons is not born as a preta.
A man always engaged in the performance of sacrifices, always dedicated to sacred fords, / and intent on hearing sacred teachings is not born as a preta.
A man who constructs oblong tanks, wells, and pools, / especially groves, and water-huts is not born as a preta.
All this, our own secret, has been related to you, O lord of the earth; / we are disgusted with our state as pretas, so you must become our refuge.

5.18.s:
gatvā gayāśiraḥ puṇyamekaikasya pṛthakpṛthak ..
śrāddhaṃ dehi mahīpāla trayāṇāmapi sādaram .. 6.18.50 ..
5.18.d:
गत्वा गयाशिरः पुण्यमेकैकस्य पृथक्पृथक् ..
श्राद्धं देहि महीपाल त्रयाणामपि सादरम् .. 6.18.50 ..
5.18.m: Having gone to the holy Gayāśiras, O protector of the earth, / respectfully offer a śrāddha separately for each of the three of us.

5.18.s:
pretatvaṃ yāti yenedaṃ tvatpra sādātsudāruṇam ..
nā'nyathā muktirasmākaṃ bhaviṣyati kathaṃcana .. 51 ..
5.18.d:
प्रेतत्वं याति येनेदं त्वत्प्र सादात्सुदारुणम् ..
नाऽन्यथा मुक्तिरस्माकं भविष्यति कथंचन .. 51 ..
5.18.m: So that this dreadful condition of being pretas departs by your grace; / otherwise our liberation will in no way come to pass.

5.18.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
īdṛgjātismṛtiryasyāṃ pretayonau ca khe gatiḥ ..
dharmādharmaparijñānaṃ tacca kasmātpraniṃdasi .. 52 ..
5.18.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
ईदृग्जातिस्मृतिर्यस्यां प्रेतयोनौ च खे गतिः ..
धर्माधर्मपरिज्ञानं तच्च कस्मात्प्रनिंदसि .. 52 ..
5.18.m:
The king said:
Why do you censure this womb of a preta, in which there is such memory of previous births, / movement in the sky, and thorough knowledge of dharma and adharma?

5.18.s:
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
pretayoniriyaṃ rājannavamī devasaṃjñitā ..
guṇatrayasamāyuktā śeṣairdoṣaiḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 53 ..
5.18.d:
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
प्रेतयोनिरियं राजन्नवमी देवसंज्ञिता ..
गुणत्रयसमायुक्ता शेषैर्दोषैः समंततः .. 53 ..
5.18.m:
The flesh-eater said:
This womb of a preta, O king, the ninth, is called divine; / it is endowed with three qualities, but with defects on all other sides.

5.18.s:
ekā jātismṛtiḥ samyagasyāmevaprajāyate ..
khecaratvaṃ tathaivānyaddharmādharmaviniścayaḥ .. 54 ..
5.18.d:
एका जातिस्मृतिः सम्यगस्यामेवप्रजायते ..
खेचरत्वं तथैवान्यद्धर्माधर्मविनिश्चयः .. 54 ..
5.18.m: One is complete memory of previous births, which arises in this very state; / another is flying in the sky, and likewise discernment of dharma and adharma.

5.18.s:
etadguṇatrayaṃ proktaṃ pretayonau nṛpottama ..
doṣānapi ca te vacmi tāñcchṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ .. 55 ..
5.18.d:
एतद्गुणत्रयं प्रोक्तं प्रेतयोनौ नृपोत्तम ..
दोषानपि च ते वच्मि ताञ्च्छृणुष्व समाहितः .. 55 ..
5.18.m: These three qualities are declared in the womb of a preta, O best of kings; / I shall also tell you the defects: hear them attentively.

5.18.s:
yadi tāvadvanādasmādyāmonyatra vayaṃ nṛpa ..
adṛṣṭamudgarāghātairnūnaṃ hanyāmahe tataḥ .. .. 56 ..
5.18.d:
यदि तावद्वनादस्माद्यामोन्यत्र वयं नृप ..
अदृष्टमुद्गराघातैर्नूनं हन्यामहे ततः .. .. 56 ..
5.18.m: If we were to go anywhere else from this forest, O king, / then we would surely be struck by blows of invisible clubs.

5.18.s:
tathā dharmakriyāḥ sarvā mānuṣāṇāmudāhṛtāḥ ..
na pretānāṃ na devānāṃ nānyeṣāṃ mānuṣaṃ vinā .. 57 ..
5.18.d:
तथा धर्मक्रियाः सर्वा मानुषाणामुदाहृताः ..
न प्रेतानां न देवानां नान्येषां मानुषं विना .. 57 ..
5.18.m: Likewise, all religious acts are ordained for human beings, / not for pretas, not for gods, and not for any others without human form.

5.18.s:
paśyāmo dūrato rājañjalapūrṇāñjalā śayān ..
pipāsākulitāḥ śrāṃtā bhāskare vṛṣasaṃsthite .. 58 ..
5.18.d:
पश्यामो दूरतो राजञ्जलपूर्णाञ्जला शयान् ..
पिपासाकुलिताः श्रांता भास्करे वृषसंस्थिते .. 58 ..
5.18.m: From afar, O king, we see reservoirs full of water, / afflicted by thirst and exhausted when the sun resides in Taurus.

5.18.s:
gacchāmaḥ saṃnidhau teṣāṃ yadi pārthivasatama ..
adṛṣṭamudgarāghātairvayaṃ hanyāmahe tataḥ .. 59 ..
5.18.d:
गच्छामः संनिधौ तेषां यदि पार्थिवसतम ..
अदृष्टमुद्गराघातैर्वयं हन्यामहे ततः .. 59 ..
5.18.m: If we go near them, O best of kings, / then we are struck by blows of invisible clubs.

5.18.s:
tathā rasavatī siddhāḥ paśyāmo dūrasaṃsthitāḥ ..
kṣudhāviṣṭā gṛhasthānāṃ gṛheṣu vividhā nṛpa .. 6.18.60 ..
5.18.d:
तथा रसवती सिद्धाः पश्यामो दूरसंस्थिताः ..
क्षुधाविष्टा गृहस्थानां गृहेषु विविधा नृप .. 6.18.60 ..
5.18.m: Likewise, overwhelmed by hunger, from far away we see various cooked dishes / ready in the houses of householders, O king.

5.18.s:
tathā suphalino vṛkṣānkalapakṣibhirāvṛtān ..
snigdhānsacchāyayopetānsevituṃ na labhāmahe .. 61 ..
5.18.d:
तथा सुफलिनो वृक्षान्कलपक्षिभिरावृतान् ..
स्निग्धान्सच्छाययोपेतान्सेवितुं न लभामहे .. 61 ..
5.18.m: Likewise, fruitful trees filled with sweet-voiced birds, / lush and endowed with good shade, we are not allowed to enjoy.

5.18.s:
kiṃvā te bahunoktena yadyatkarma vigarhitam ..
kleśadaṃ ca tadasmākaṃ svayamevopatiṣṭhate .. 62 ..
5.18.d:
किंवा ते बहुनोक्तेन यद्यत्कर्म विगर्हितम् ..
क्लेशदं च तदस्माकं स्वयमेवोपतिष्ठते .. 62 ..
5.18.m: Or what need is there to tell you much? Whatever act is blameworthy / and brings torment approaches us of its own accord.

5.18.s:
na cchidreṇa vinā'smākaṃ prāṇayātrā prajāyate ..
na jalāni na ca cchāyā na yānaṃ na ca vāhanam .. 63 ..
5.18.d:
न च्छिद्रेण विनाऽस्माकं प्राणयात्रा प्रजायते ..
न जलानि न च च्छाया न यानं न च वाहनम् .. 63 ..
5.18.m: Without a vulnerability, the maintenance of our life does not occur; / there are no waters, no shade, no vehicle, and no mount for us.

5.18.s:
etasmātkāraṇānnityaṃ bhramāmaśchidrahetave ..
prāpte rātrimukhe rājanna prātarna ca vāsare .. 64 ..
5.18.d:
एतस्मात्कारणान्नित्यं भ्रमामश्छिद्रहेतवे ..
प्राप्ते रात्रिमुखे राजन्न प्रातर्न च वासरे .. 64 ..
5.18.m: For this reason, we wander constantly in search of a vulnerability / at the onset of night, O king, and neither in the morning nor during the day.

5.18.s:
yattvaṃ śaṃsasi cā'smākaṃ khecaratvaṃ mahīpate ..
vyarthaṃ tadapi na śreyaḥ śṛṇu tatrāpi kāraṇam .. 65 ..
5.18.d:
यत्त्वं शंससि चाऽस्माकं खेचरत्वं महीपते ..
व्यर्थं तदपि न श्रेयः शृणु तत्रापि कारणम् .. 65 ..
5.18.m: As for your praise of our flying in the sky, O lord of the earth, / that too is useless and not beneficial; hear the reason for that as well.

5.18.s:
kriyate khecaratvena kiṃkiṃ dharmaṃ viniścayaiḥ ..
yato na sidhyate mokṣo jāti smṛtyādikaṃ tathā .. 66 ..
5.18.d:
क्रियते खेचरत्वेन किंकिं धर्मं विनिश्चयैः ..
यतो न सिध्यते मोक्षो जाति स्मृत्यादिकं तथा .. 66 ..
5.18.m: What is accomplished by flying in the sky, or by decisions on dharma, / or by memory of previous births and the like, since liberation is not attained?

5.18.s:
tasmāddoṣādime rājanguṇā yadyapi kīrtitāḥ ..
pretānāṃ yānsamāśritya kācitsiddhirna jāyate .. 67 ..
5.18.d:
तस्माद्दोषादिमे राजन्गुणा यद्यपि कीर्तिताः ..
प्रेतानां यान्समाश्रित्य काचित्सिद्धिर्न जायते .. 67 ..
5.18.m: Therefore, because of this defect, O king, although these are spoken of as qualities / of pretas, by relying on them no attainment whatsoever arises.

5.18.s:
viṣādo jāyate bhūyo guṇairetairnarādhipa ..
aśaktāḥ pretayogādvai sarvasya śubhakarmaṇaḥ .. 68 ..
5.18.d:
विषादो जायते भूयो गुणैरेतैर्नराधिप ..
अशक्ताः प्रेतयोगाद्वै सर्वस्य शुभकर्मणः .. 68 ..
5.18.m: Greater dejection arises because of these qualities, O lord of men; / by joining the state of pretas, we are unable to perform any auspicious action.

5.18.s:
.. rājovāca . ..
yadi yāsyāmi bhūyo'haṃ gṛhamasmānmahāvanāt ..
tatkariṣyāmi sarveṣāṃ gayāśrāddhamasaṃśayam .. 69 ..
5.18.d:
.. राजोवाच . ..
यदि यास्यामि भूयोऽहं गृहमस्मान्महावनात् ..
तत्करिष्यामि सर्वेषां गयाश्राद्धमसंशयम् .. 69 ..
5.18.m:
The king said:
If I return to my home from this great forest, / then without a doubt I will perform the Gayā-śrāddha for all of you.

5.18.s:
tārayiṣyāmi sarvāṃśca sarvapāpaiḥ prayatnataḥ ..
apyātmadehadānena satyenātmānamālabhe .. .. 6.18.70 ..
5.18.d:
तारयिष्यामि सर्वांश्च सर्वपापैः प्रयत्नतः ..
अप्यात्मदेहदानेन सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. .. 6.18.70 ..
5.18.m: And I will diligently deliver you all from all sins, / even by giving my own body: by truth I swear to myself.

5.18.s:
yasmāddhṛdgataśaṃkā me hṛtā yuṣmābhiradya vai ..
yena tatprāpya yuṣmākamupakāraṃ karomyaham .. 71 ..
5.18.d:
यस्माद्धृद्गतशंका मे हृता युष्माभिरद्य वै ..
येन तत्प्राप्य युष्माकमुपकारं करोम्यहम् .. 71 ..
5.18.m: Since the doubt dwelling in my heart has been removed by you today, / having reached [my home], I shall render this service to you.

5.18.s:
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
itaḥ sthānānmahārāja nātidūre jalāśayaḥ .
asti nānādrumopetaścittāhlādakaraḥ paraḥ .. 72 ..
5.18.d:
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
इतः स्थानान्महाराज नातिदूरे जलाशयः .
अस्ति नानाद्रुमोपेतश्चित्ताह्लादकरः परः .. 72 ..
5.18.m:
The flesh-eater said:
Not very far from this place, O great king, is a reservoir of water / surrounded by various trees, supremely delighting the heart.

5.18.s:
tasmādudaṅmukho gaccha yatra te jalapakṣiṇaḥ ..
dṛśyaṃte vyomamārgeṇa pragacchataḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 73 ..
5.18.d:
तस्मादुदङ्मुखो गच्छ यत्र ते जलपक्षिणः ..
दृश्यंते व्योममार्गेण प्रगच्छतः समंततः .. 73 ..
5.18.m: Therefore, go facing north, where waterbirds are seen / flying all around along the path of the sky.

5.18.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
athāsau nṛpaśārdūlaḥ samutthāya śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
saumyāṃ diśaṃ samuddiśya pratasthe sa tu duḥkhitaḥ .. 74 ..
5.18.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथासौ नृपशार्दूलः समुत्थाय शनैःशनैः ..
सौम्यां दिशं समुद्दिश्य प्रतस्थे स तु दुःखितः .. 74 ..
5.18.m:
Sūta said:
Then, having slowly stood up, that tiger among kings / set out toward the northern direction, sorrowful indeed.

5.18.s:
evaṃ pragacchatā tena kṣutpipāsākulena ca .
adūrādeva saṃdṛṣṭaṃ nīlaṃ drumakadaṃbakam ..
bhramamāṇairbakairhaṃsaiḥ sārasairmadgubhistathā ..76..
sa gatvā salilaṃ tatra tadvātena mahīpatiḥ ..
āhūta iva śītena prayayau tvarayānvitaḥ .. 76 ..
5.18.d:
एवं प्रगच्छता तेन क्षुत्पिपासाकुलेन च .
अदूरादेव संदृष्टं नीलं द्रुमकदंबकम् ..
भ्रममाणैर्बकैर्हंसैः सारसैर्मद्गुभिस्तथा ..76..
स गत्वा सलिलं तत्र तद्वातेन महीपतिः ..
आहूत इव शीतेन प्रययौ त्वरयान्वितः .. 76 ..
5.18.m:
As he proceeded thus, distressed by hunger and thirst, / he saw not far away a dark grove of trees, / with herons, swans, cranes, and cormorants wheeling about.
Approaching the water there, the king, / as if summoned by its cool breeze, went on in haste.

5.18.s:
athā'paśyanmanohāri saumyasattvaniṣevitam ..
āśramaṃ hradatīrasthaṃ tāpasaiḥ sarvato vṛtam .. 77 ..
5.18.d:
अथाऽपश्यन्मनोहारि सौम्यसत्त्वनिषेवितम् ..
आश्रमं ह्रदतीरस्थं तापसैः सर्वतो वृतम् .. 77 ..
5.18.m: Then he beheld a charming hermitage situated on the bank of a pool, / frequented by gentle creatures and surrounded on all sides by ascetics,

5.18.s:
puṣpitaiḥ phalitairvṛkṣaiḥ samaṃtātpariveṣṭitam ..
vicitrairmadhurārāvairnāditaṃ vihagottamaiḥ .. 78 ..
5.18.d:
पुष्पितैः फलितैर्वृक्षैः समंतात्परिवेष्टितम् ..
विचित्रैर्मधुरारावैर्नादितं विहगोत्तमैः .. 78 ..
5.18.m: encircled everywhere by trees laden with flowers and fruits, / and made resonant with varied, sweet calls by excellent birds.

5.18.s:
tatrāpaśyannagādhastāttapasvigaṇasevitam ..
śivadharmaparaṃ śāṃtaṃ jaiminiṃ munisattamam.. 79 .
5.18.d:
तत्रापश्यन्नगाधस्तात्तपस्विगणसेवितम् ..
शिवधर्मपरं शांतं जैमिनिं मुनिसत्तमम्.. 79 .
5.18.m: There, beneath a tree, he saw the best of sages, Jaimini, / attended by a host of ascetics, devoted to the path of Śiva, and serene.

5.18.s:
atha gatvā sa rājeṃdraḥ praṇipatya munīśvaram ..
tathānyānapi tacchiṣyānnipapāta dharātale .. 6.18.80 ..
5.18.d:
अथ गत्वा स राजेंद्रः प्रणिपत्य मुनीश्वरम् ..
तथान्यानपि तच्छिष्यान्निपपात धरातले .. 6.18.80 ..
5.18.m: Then, having approached, the king of kings bowed down to the lord of sages, / and likewise to his other disciples, and fell to the ground.

5.18.s:
te dṛṣṭvā'dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ taṃ rājalakṣaṇalakṣitam..
dhūlidhūsaritāṃgaṃ ca bhasmāvṛtamivācalam .. 81 ..
5.18.d:
ते दृष्ट्वाऽदृष्टपूर्वं तं राजलक्षणलक्षितम्..
धूलिधूसरितांगं च भस्मावृतमिवाचलम् .. 81 ..
5.18.m: Seeing him, whom they had never seen before, endowed with the marks of a king, / his limbs greyed with dust like a mountain covered with ash,

5.18.s:
manyamānā mahīpālaṃ vismayotphullalocanāḥ ..
procuśca madhurairvākyairāśīrvādapuraḥsaraiḥ .. 82 ..
5.18.d:
मन्यमाना महीपालं विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनाः ..
प्रोचुश्च मधुरैर्वाक्यैराशीर्वादपुरःसरैः .. 82 ..
5.18.m: considering him to be an earthly ruler, their eyes wide with wonder, / they addressed him with sweet words preceded by blessings:

5.18.s:
kutastvamanusaṃprāpto vane'smiñjanavarjite ..
ekākī sukumārāṃgaḥ padātiḥ śramavihvalaḥ .. 93 ..
pārthivasyeva liṃgāni dṛśyaṃte tava bhūriśaḥ ..
na vidmo niścayaṃ tasmādvadāgamanakāraṇam .. 84 ..
athovāca nṛpaḥ kṛcchrātpipāsā māṃ prabādhate ..
tasmādvadata pānīyaṃ yatpītvā kīrtayāmyaham .. 85 ..
tatastairdarśitaṃ toyaṃ samīpe yanmahīpateḥ ..
so'pi pītvā'vagāhyātha vitṛṣṇaḥ samapadyata .. 86 ..
tataḥ phalāni pakvāni tarūṇāṃ patitānyadhaḥ ..
sumṛṣṭāni samādāya bhakṣayāmāsa vāṃchayā .. 87 ..
tatastṛptiṃ parāṃ prāpya gatvā jaiminisaṃnidhau ..
upaviṣṭaḥ praṇamyoccaistathānyāṃśca munīnkramāt .. 88 ..
uvāca ca nijāṃ vārtāṃ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ ..
sa pṛṣṭastāpasaiḥ sarvaiḥ suvismayasamanvitaiḥ .. 89 ..
5.18.d:
कुतस्त्वमनुसंप्राप्तो वनेऽस्मिञ्जनवर्जिते ..
एकाकी सुकुमारांगः पदातिः श्रमविह्वलः .. 93 ..
पार्थिवस्येव लिंगानि दृश्यंते तव भूरिशः ..
न विद्मो निश्चयं तस्माद्वदागमनकारणम् .. 84 ..
अथोवाच नृपः कृच्छ्रात्पिपासा मां प्रबाधते ..
तस्माद्वदत पानीयं यत्पीत्वा कीर्तयाम्यहम् .. 85 ..
ततस्तैर्दर्शितं तोयं समीपे यन्महीपतेः ..
सोऽपि पीत्वाऽवगाह्याथ वितृष्णः समपद्यत .. 86 ..
ततः फलानि पक्वानि तरूणां पतितान्यधः ..
सुमृष्टानि समादाय भक्षयामास वांछया .. 87 ..
ततस्तृप्तिं परां प्राप्य गत्वा जैमिनिसंनिधौ ..
उपविष्टः प्रणम्योच्चैस्तथान्यांश्च मुनीन्क्रमात् .. 88 ..
उवाच च निजां वार्तां कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः ..
स पृष्टस्तापसैः सर्वैः सुविस्मयसमन्वितैः .. 89 ..
5.18.m:
"From where have you arrived in this uninhabited forest, / alone, of delicate limbs, on foot, overcome with exhaustion?
Many marks of a king are seen on you. / Therefore we do not know with certainty; tell us the reason for your coming."
Then the king said with difficulty: "Thirst torments me. / Therefore, tell me where there is water, having drunk which I will narrate [everything]."
Then the water that was nearby was pointed out to the king by them. / He too, having drunk and bathed, became free from thirst.
Then, taking up ripe, very pure fruits of the trees / that had fallen below, he ate with appetite.
Then, having attained supreme satisfaction, he approached Jaimini's presence; / having bowed deeply, he sat down, and likewise [did reverence] to the other sages in order.
Standing with joined palms, he recounted his own story, / when questioned by all the ascetics filled with great astonishment:

5.18.s:
vidūratho mahīpo'haṃ māhiṣmatyāṃ kṛtāspadaḥ ..
mṛgalipsurvane ghore praviṣṭaḥ sainikaiḥ saha .. 6.18.90 ..
tato me bhramamāṇasya praṇaṣṭāḥ sarvasainikāḥ ..
gulmairaṃtaritāścā'nye na jāne'haṃ kathaṃ sthitāḥ .. 91 ..
āsīddhayo mamā'dhastājjātyaḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ ..
so'pi karmavipākena pañcatvaṃ samupasthitaḥ .ā 92 ..
bhramamāṇastvahaṃ prāpta āyuḥśeṣatayātra ca ..
tadbrūta kaḥ pradeśo'yaṃ kiyaddūre ca me purī .. 93 ..
5.18.d:
विदूरथो महीपोऽहं माहिष्मत्यां कृतास्पदः ..
मृगलिप्सुर्वने घोरे प्रविष्टः सैनिकैः सह .. 6.18.90 ..
ततो मे भ्रममाणस्य प्रणष्टाः सर्वसैनिकाः ..
गुल्मैरंतरिताश्चाऽन्ये न जानेऽहं कथं स्थिताः .. 91 ..
आसीद्धयो ममाऽधस्ताज्जात्यः सर्वगुणान्वितः ..
सोऽपि कर्मविपाकेन पञ्चत्वं समुपस्थितः .आ 92 ..
भ्रममाणस्त्वहं प्राप्त आयुःशेषतयात्र च ..
तद्ब्रूत कः प्रदेशोऽयं कियद्दूरे च मे पुरी .. 93 ..
5.18.m:
"I am King Vidūratha, whose seat is in Māhiṣmatī. / Wishing to hunt deer, I entered the terrible forest along with my soldiers.
Then, as I wandered about, all my soldiers were lost; / and others were hidden by the thickets—I do not know how they fared.
I had a thoroughbred steed under me, endowed with all fine qualities; / he too, through the ripening of past deeds, met his death.
Wandering about, I have arrived here because a remnant of my lifespan remained. / So tell me: what region is this, and how far away is my city?"

5.18.s:
tataste tāpasāḥ procurvidmahe na vayaṃ purīm ..
tvāṃ ca deśaṃ ca te rājanko'yaṃ deśaśca kīrtyate .. 94 ..
5.18.d:
ततस्ते तापसाः प्रोचुर्विद्महे न वयं पुरीम् ..
त्वां च देशं च ते राजन्कोऽयं देशश्च कीर्त्यते .. 94 ..
5.18.m: Then those ascetics said: "We do not know your city, / nor do we know you or your land, O king, nor what this region is called.

5.18.s:
narendrairnaiva naḥ kāryaṃ na diśairna purairnṛpa ..
vanecarā vayaṃ nityaṃ śivārādhanatatparāḥ .. 95 ..
5.18.d:
नरेन्द्रैर्नैव नः कार्यं न दिशैर्न पुरैर्नृप ..
वनेचरा वयं नित्यं शिवाराधनतत्पराः .. 95 ..
5.18.m: We have no concern with rulers of men, nor with quarters, nor with cities, O king. / We are forest-dwellers, always devoted to the worship of Śiva.

5.18.s:
sarve śīrṇāni vṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca ..
bhakṣayāmo'tha patrāṇi śarī rasthitihetunā .. 96 ..
5.18.d:
सर्वे शीर्णानि वृक्षाणां पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ..
भक्षयामोऽथ पत्राणि शरी रस्थितिहेतुना .. 96 ..
5.18.m: All of us eat only fallen flowers and fruits of the trees, / or leaves, for the sake of maintaining the body.

5.18.s:
mānuṣaiḥ saha saṃsargaṃ saṃbhāṣaṃ ca narādhipa ..
na kurmo na ca paśyāmo gacchāmo'nyatra dūrataḥ .. 97 ..
5.18.d:
मानुषैः सह संसर्गं संभाषं च नराधिप ..
न कुर्मो न च पश्यामो गच्छामोऽन्यत्र दूरतः .. 97 ..
5.18.m: We do not associate or converse with human beings, O ruler of men; / we do not look at them, but go elsewhere, far away.

5.18.s:
ekaikasya tarormūle divasaṃ vā dinadvayam..
tiṣṭhāmo na bhavedyena mamatvaṃ tatsamudbhavam ..98..
5.18.d:
एकैकस्य तरोर्मूले दिवसं वा दिनद्वयम्..
तिष्ठामो न भवेद्येन ममत्वं तत्समुद्भवम् ..98..
5.18.m: We stay at the foot of each single tree for one day or two, / so that no sense of possessiveness arising therefrom may develop.

5.18.s:
kāraṇāttava rājeṃdra niśāmetāṃ vanaspatau ..
neṣyāmo'nyatra yāsyāmaḥ prabhā te'nyatra kānane .. 99 ..
5.18.d:
कारणात्तव राजेंद्र निशामेतां वनस्पतौ ..
नेष्यामोऽन्यत्र यास्यामः प्रभा तेऽन्यत्र कानने .. 99 ..
5.18.m: For your sake, O king of kings, we shall spend this night / at [the foot of] this tree; at dawn we shall depart elsewhere, to another forest.

5.18.s:
ekākinaṃ padātiṃ ca viśastraṃ śramavihvalam ..
tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūpate'smākaṃ dayā jātā tato'dhikā ..6.18......
ekākī pārthivendro'yaṃ neṣyati ca kathaṃ niśām ..
vane'sminmaṃtrayitvaivaṃ tato'traiva vyavasthitāḥ .. 101 ..
5.18.d:
एकाकिनं पदातिं च विशस्त्रं श्रमविह्वलम् ..
त्वां दृष्ट्वा भूपतेऽस्माकं दया जाता ततोऽधिका ..6.18......
एकाकी पार्थिवेन्द्रोऽयं नेष्यति च कथं निशाम् ..
वनेऽस्मिन्मंत्रयित्वैवं ततोऽत्रैव व्यवस्थिताः .. 101 ..
5.18.m: Seeing you alone, on foot, weaponless, and overcome with exhaustion, / O king, greater compassion arose within us. / 'How will this lone foremost of kings pass the night / in this forest?' Having deliberated thus, we remained right here.

5.18.s:
tasmādatraiva neṣyāmaḥ sametāḥ śarvarīmimām..
gaṃtavyaṃ prātarutthāya tataḥ sarvairyadṛcchayā 102 ..
5.18.d:
तस्मादत्रैव नेष्यामः समेताः शर्वरीमिमाम्..
गंतव्यं प्रातरुत्थाय ततः सर्वैर्यदृच्छया 102 ..
5.18.m: Therefore, gathered together, we will pass this night right here. / Rising in the morning, everyone must then proceed according to their will."

5.18.s:
evaṃ saṃvadatāṃ teṣāṃ bhagavāṃstīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
astācalamanuprāptaḥ kuṃkumakṣodasaṃnibhaḥ .. 103 ..
5.18.d:
एवं संवदतां तेषां भगवांस्तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
अस्ताचलमनुप्राप्तः कुंकुमक्षोदसंनिभः .. 103 ..
5.18.m: As they were conversing in this manner, the venerable sun of sharp rays, / resembling saffron powder, reached the setting mountain.

5.18.s:
atha tāstāpasānrājā provāca praṇataḥ sthitaḥ ..
saṃdhyākālaḥ samāyātaḥ sāṃprataṃ munisattamāḥ ..
tasmātsaṃdhyāvidhiḥ kāryaḥ sarvaireva yathocitaḥ .. 104 ..
5.18.d:
अथ तास्तापसान्राजा प्रोवाच प्रणतः स्थितः ..
संध्याकालः समायातः सांप्रतं मुनिसत्तमाः ..
तस्मात्संध्याविधिः कार्यः सर्वैरेव यथोचितः .. 104 ..
5.18.m: Then the king, standing with head bowed, said to those ascetics: / "The twilight hour has now arrived, O best of sages; / therefore, the evening rite ought to be performed by everyone properly."

5.18.s:
atha te munayaḥ sarve sa ca rājā tathā dvijāḥ ..
cakruḥ sāyaṃtanaṃ karma yathoddiṣṭaṃ purātanaiḥ .. 105 ..
5.18.d:
अथ ते मुनयः सर्वे स च राजा तथा द्विजाः ..
चक्रुः सायंतनं कर्म यथोद्दिष्टं पुरातनैः .. 105 ..
5.18.m: Then all those sages and that king, as well as the twice-born, / performed the evening ritual as enjoined by the ancients.

5.18.s:
kāmibhiḥ kāminīlokaiḥ priyoktairabhivāṃ chitā ..
asatstrībhirviśeṣeṇa saṃprāptā rajanī tataḥ .. 106 ..
5.18.d:
कामिभिः कामिनीलोकैः प्रियोक्तैरभिवां छिता ..
असत्स्त्रीभिर्विशेषेण संप्राप्ता रजनी ततः .. 106 ..
5.18.m: Then arrived the night, longed for by lovers, by women, / and with sweet words by those who are cherished, and especially by unchaste wives—

5.18.s:
pīyūṣārṇavaveleva viṣavṛkṣalateva ca ..
ulūkaiścakravākaiśca yugapadyā vilokyate .. 107..
5.18.d:
पीयूषार्णववेलेव विषवृक्षलतेव च ..
उलूकैश्चक्रवाकैश्च युगपद्या विलोक्यते .. 107..
5.18.m: which is viewed simultaneously like a shore of the nectar ocean / and like a creeper of the poison tree by owls and by cakravāka birds;

5.18.s:
ulūkā rākṣasāścaurāḥ kāminaḥ kulaṭāṃ'ganāḥ ..
yāṃ vāṃchaṃti sadā sotkāḥ suvṛṣṭimiva karṣukāḥ .. 108 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye māṃsādavacanādṛṣyāśramapadaṃ prāptasya vidūrathasya munibhiḥ saha saṃvādapūrvakasāṃyatanakarmādividhānavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 18 .. .. ..
5.18.d:
उलूका राक्षसाश्चौराः कामिनः कुलटांऽगनाः ..
यां वांछंति सदा सोत्काः सुवृष्टिमिव कर्षुकाः .. 108 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मांसादवचनादृष्याश्रमपदं प्राप्तस्य विदूरथस्य मुनिभिः सह संवादपूर्वकसांयतनकर्मादिविधानवर्णनंनामाष्टादशोऽध्यायः .. 18 .. .. ..
5.18.m:
which owls, rākṣasas, thieves, lovers, and unchaste women / always desire eagerly, just as farmers desire abundant rain.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Performance of Evening Rites and Other Observances Preceded by the Dialogue with the Sages of Vidūratha, Who Reached the Abode of the Seers' Hermitage on the Word of the Carnivore,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.

5.19.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etasminnaṃtare prāptāstasya bhūpasya sevakāḥ ..
kecicca daivayo gena śvāpadairardhabhakṣitāḥ .. 1 ..
5.19.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तास्तस्य भूपस्य सेवकाः ..
केचिच्च दैवयो गेन श्वापदैरर्धभक्षिताः .. 1 ..
5.19.m: Sūta said: / In the meantime, the servants of that king arrived, / some of whom, by turn of fate, had been half-eaten by beasts of prey,

5.19.s:
kṣutpipāsāturā dīnā duḥkhena mahatā'nvitāḥ ..
padapaddhatimārgeṇa yena yātaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ .. 2 ..
5.19.d:
क्षुत्पिपासातुरा दीना दुःखेन महताऽन्विताः ..
पदपद्धतिमार्गेण येन यातः स भूपतिः .. 2 ..
5.19.m: tormented by hunger and thirst, wretched, and afflicted with great sorrow, / [following] along the path of footprints by which the king had gone.

5.19.s:
te dṛṣṭvā pārthivaṃ tatra diṣṭyādiṣṭyeti sādaram ..
bruvaṃtaḥ pādayostasya patitā harṣasaṃyutāḥ .. 3 ..
5.19.d:
ते दृष्ट्वा पार्थिवं तत्र दिष्ट्यादिष्ट्येति सादरम् ..
ब्रुवंतः पादयोस्तस्य पतिता हर्षसंयुताः .. 3 ..
5.19.m: Seeing the king there, respectfully crying, "By good fortune! By good fortune!" / they fell at his feet, filled with joy.

5.19.s:
tatastasya narendrasya vyasanaṃ sainyasaṃbhavam ..
procuścaiva yathādṛṣṭama nubhūtaṃ yathāśrutam ..4..
5.19.d:
ततस्तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य व्यसनं सैन्यसंभवम् ..
प्रोचुश्चैव यथादृष्टम नुभूतं यथाश्रुतम् ..4..
5.19.m: Then they recounted to that ruler of men the calamity that befell the army, / just as it was seen, experienced, and heard.

5.19.s:
atha te tāpasāḥ sarve sa ca rājā sasevakaḥ ..
prasuptāḥ pādapasyādhaḥ parṇānyāstīryabhūtale ..5..
5.19.d:
अथ ते तापसाः सर्वे स च राजा ससेवकः ..
प्रसुप्ताः पादपस्याधः पर्णान्यास्तीर्यभूतले ..5..
5.19.m: Then all those ascetics and that king along with his servants / fell asleep beneath the tree, having spread leaves on the ground.

5.19.s:
tatasteṣāṃ prasuptānāṃ sarveṣāṃ tatra kānane ..
atikrāṃtā sukhenaiva rajanī sā mahātmanām .. 6 ..
5.19.d:
ततस्तेषां प्रसुप्तानां सर्वेषां तत्र कानने ..
अतिक्रांता सुखेनैव रजनी सा महात्मनाम् .. 6 ..
5.19.m: Then, as all of them slept there in the forest, / that night passed very pleasantly for those noble souls.

5.19.s:
tataḥ sa prātarutthāya kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyaḥ ..
taṃ muniṃ praṇipatyoccairanujñāpya muhu rmuhuḥ .. 7 ..
5.19.d:
ततः स प्रातरुत्थाय कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः ..
तं मुनिं प्रणिपत्योच्चैरनुज्ञाप्य मुहु र्मुहुः .. 7 ..
5.19.m: Then, having risen in the morning and performed his morning rituals, / he bowed deeply to that sage and repeatedly took his leave.

5.19.s:
nijaistaiḥ sevakaiḥ sārdhaṃ prasthitaḥ svapurīṃ prati ..
māhiṣmatīṃ samuddiśya dṛṣṭvā mārge śanaiḥśanaiḥ .. 8 ..
5.19.d:
निजैस्तैः सेवकैः सार्धं प्रस्थितः स्वपुरीं प्रति ..
माहिष्मतीं समुद्दिश्य दृष्ट्वा मार्गे शनैःशनैः .. 8 ..
5.19.m: Along with those attendants of his, he set out towards his own city, / aiming for Māhiṣmatī, watching [the path] step by step along the way.

5.19.s:
tato nijagṛhaṃ prāpya kañci tkālaṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
viśramya prayayau paścāttūrṇaṃ puṇyaṃ gayāśiraḥ .. 9 ..
5.19.d:
ततो निजगृहं प्राप्य कञ्चि त्कालं महीपतिः ..
विश्रम्य प्रययौ पश्चात्तूर्णं पुण्यं गयाशिरः .. 9 ..
5.19.m: Then, having reached his own home and having rested for some time, / the king afterwards went swiftly to the holy Gayāśiras.

5.19.s:
tacca kālena saṃprāpya snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ ..
māṃsādāya dadau śrāddhaṃ śraddhāpūtena cetasā .. 6.19.10 ..
5.19.d:
तच्च कालेन संप्राप्य स्नात्वा धौतांबरः शुचिः ..
मांसादाय ददौ श्राद्धं श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा .. 6.19.10 ..
5.19.m: Having arrived there in due time, having bathed, wearing washed garments, and purified, / he offered a śrāddha for the meat-eater with a heart purified by faith.

5.19.s:
athā'sau pṛthivīpālaḥ svapnāṃte ca dadarśa tam ..
divyamālyāṃbaradharaṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanam ..
vimānavaramārūḍhaṃ stūyamānaṃ ca kiṃnaraiḥ .. 11 ..
5.19.d:
अथाऽसौ पृथिवीपालः स्वप्नांते च ददर्श तम् ..
दिव्यमाल्यांबरधरं दिव्यगंधानुलेपनम् ..
विमानवरमारूढं स्तूयमानं च किंनरैः .. 11 ..
5.19.m: Then that king saw him at the end of a dream, / wearing heavenly garlands and garments, anointed with heavenly fragrant cosmetics, / mounted upon an excellent aerial chariot, and being praised by kinnaras.

5.19.s:
.. māṃsāda uvāca .. ..
prasādāttava bhūpāla mukto'haṃ pretayonitaḥ ..
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tridivā layam.. 12 ..
5.19.d:
.. मांसाद उवाच .. ..
प्रसादात्तव भूपाल मुक्तोऽहं प्रेतयोनितः ..
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सांप्रतं त्रिदिवा लयम्.. 12 ..
5.19.m: The meat-eater said: / 'By your favor, O king, I am released from the state of a ghost. / May it be well with you; I shall now go to the abode of the thirty gods.'

5.19.s:
tataḥ sa prātarutthāya harṣāviṣṭo mahīpatiḥ ..
vidaivataṃ samuddiśya cakre śrāddhaṃ yathocitam .. 13
5.19.d:
ततः स प्रातरुत्थाय हर्षाविष्टो महीपतिः ..
विदैवतं समुद्दिश्य चक्रे श्राद्धं यथोचितम् .. 13
5.19.m: Then, having arisen in the morning, the king, filled with joy, / performed the śrāddha as prescribed, dedicating it to Vidaivata.

5.19.s:
so'pi tenaiva rūpeṇa tasya saṃdarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
svapnāṃ'te bhūmipālasya tadvaccoktvā divaṃ gataḥ .. 14 ..
5.19.d:
सोऽपि तेनैव रूपेण तस्य संदर्शनं गतः ..
स्वप्नांऽते भूमिपालस्य तद्वच्चोक्त्वा दिवं गतः .. 14 ..
5.19.m: He too came into his sight in that very same form / at the end of the king's dream, spoke likewise, and went to heaven.

5.19.s:
tataḥ prātastṛtīye'hni kṛtaghnasya mahīpatiḥ ..
cakre śrāddhaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ śraddhāpūtena cetasā .. 15 ..
5.19.d:
ततः प्रातस्तृतीयेऽह्नि कृतघ्नस्य महीपतिः ..
चक्रे श्राद्धं यथापूर्वं श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा .. 15 ..
5.19.m: Then, in the morning on the third day, the king performed a śrāddha / for the ungrateful one as before, with a heart purified by faith.

5.19.s:
tataḥ so'pi samāyātastasya svapne mahīpateḥ ..
tenaiva pretarūpeṇa duḥkhena mahatā vṛtaḥ .. 16 ..
5.19.d:
ततः सोऽपि समायातस्तस्य स्वप्ने महीपतेः ..
तेनैव प्रेतरूपेण दुःखेन महता वृतः .. 16 ..
5.19.m: Then he also came into that king's dream / in the very same form of a ghost, overwhelmed with great sorrow.

5.19.s:
.. kṛtaghna uvāca ..
na me gatirmahārāja saṃjātā pāpakarmiṇaḥ ..
taḍāgavittacaurasya kṛtaghnasya tathaiva ca .. 17 ..
5.19.d:
.. कृतघ्न उवाच ..
न मे गतिर्महाराज संजाता पापकर्मिणः ..
तडागवित्तचौरस्य कृतघ्नस्य तथैव च .. 17 ..
5.19.m: The ungrateful one said: / 'No higher state has come to me, an evildoer, O great king, / a thief of money meant for a reservoir, and likewise ungrateful.

5.19.s:
tasmātsaṃjāyate muktiryathā me pārthivottama ..
tathaiva tvaṃ kuruṣyā'dya satyavākyaparo bhava .. 18 ..
5.19.d:
तस्मात्संजायते मुक्तिर्यथा मे पार्थिवोत्तम ..
तथैव त्वं कुरुष्याऽद्य सत्यवाक्यपरो भव .. 18 ..
5.19.m: Therefore, O best of kings, so that liberation may arise for me, / do thus today, and be intent on truthful speech.

5.19.s:
satyameva paraṃ brahma satyameva paraṃ tapaḥ ..
satyameva paraṃ jñānaṃ satyameva paraṃ śrutam .. 19 ..
5.19.d:
सत्यमेव परं ब्रह्म सत्यमेव परं तपः ..
सत्यमेव परं ज्ञानं सत्यमेव परं श्रुतम् .. 19 ..
5.19.m: Truth alone is the supreme Brahman; truth alone is the supreme austerity; / truth alone is the supreme knowledge; truth alone is the supreme sacred learning.

5.19.s:
satyena vāyu rvahati satyena tapate raviḥ ..
sāgaraḥ satyavākyena maryādāṃ na vilaṃghayet .. 6.19.20 ..
5.19.d:
सत्येन वायु र्वहति सत्येन तपते रविः ..
सागरः सत्यवाक्येन मर्यादां न विलंघयेत् .. 6.19.20 ..
5.19.m: By truth the wind blows; by truth the sun burns; / by the word of truth the ocean does not transgress its shore.

5.19.s:
tīrthasevā tapo dānaṃ svādhyāyo gurusevanam ..
sarvaṃ satyavihīnasya vyarthaṃ saṃjāyate yataḥ .. 21 ..
5.19.d:
तीर्थसेवा तपो दानं स्वाध्यायो गुरुसेवनम् ..
सर्वं सत्यविहीनस्य व्यर्थं संजायते यतः .. 21 ..
5.19.m: Visiting sacred fords, austerity, giving gifts, personal study of the Veda, serving a guru— / because of this, everything becomes useless for one who lacks truth.

5.19.s:
sarve dharmā dhṛtāḥ pūrvamekatrā'nyatra cāpyṛtam ..
tulāyāṃ kautukāddevairjātaṃ tatra ṛtaṃ guru .. 22 ..
5.19.d:
सर्वे धर्मा धृताः पूर्वमेकत्राऽन्यत्र चाप्यृतम् ..
तुलायां कौतुकाद्देवैर्जातं तत्र ऋतं गुरु .. 22 ..
5.19.m: Formerly, all religious duties were placed on one side and truth on the other / upon a scale by the gods out of curiosity; there truth proved heavier.

5.19.s:
tasmātsatyaṃ puraskṛtya māṃ tāraya mahāmate ..
etatte paramaṃ śreyastapaso'pi bhaviṣyati .. 23 ..
5.19.d:
तस्मात्सत्यं पुरस्कृत्य मां तारय महामते ..
एतत्ते परमं श्रेयस्तपसोऽपि भविष्यति .. 23 ..
5.19.m: Therefore, placing truth foremost, deliver me, O noble-minded one! / This will be the highest benefit for you, surpassing even austerity.'

5.19.s:
.. vidūratha uvāca .. ..
kathaṃ te jāyate muktirvada me preta satvaram ..
karomi yena tatkarma yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram ḥ. 24 ..
5.19.d:
.. विदूरथ उवाच .. ..
कथं ते जायते मुक्तिर्वद मे प्रेत सत्वरम् ..
करोमि येन तत्कर्म यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुष्करम् ः. 24 ..
5.19.m: Vidūratha said: / 'Tell me quickly, O ghost, how does your liberation come about, / so that I may perform that act, even if it should be very difficult to do?'

5.19.s:
.. preta uvāca .. ..
camatkārapure bhūpa śrīkṣetre hāṭakeśvare ..
āste pāṃsubhirācchannaṃ kalerbhītaṃ gayāśiraḥ .. 25 ..
5.19.d:
.. प्रेत उवाच .. ..
चमत्कारपुरे भूप श्रीक्षेत्रे हाटकेश्वरे ..
आस्ते पांसुभिराच्छन्नं कलेर्भीतं गयाशिरः .. 25 ..
5.19.m: The ghost said: / 'In Camatkārapura, O king, in the holy sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, / lies Gayāśiras, covered with dust out of fear of the Kali [age],

5.19.s:
adhastātplakṣavṛkṣasya darbhasthānaiḥ samaṃtataḥ ..
kālaśākaistathānekaistilaiścāraṇyasaṃbhavaiḥ .. .. 26 ..
5.19.d:
अधस्तात्प्लक्षवृक्षस्य दर्भस्थानैः समंततः ..
कालशाकैस्तथानेकैस्तिलैश्चारण्यसंभवैः .. .. 26 ..
5.19.m: beneath a plakṣa tree, surrounded on all sides by places of darbha grass, / by abundant kālaśāka greens, and by sesame seeds grown in the forest.

5.19.s:
tatra gatvā tilaistaistvaṃ taiḥ śākaistaiḥ kuśaistathā ..
śrāddhaṃ dehi drutaṃ yena muktiḥ saṃjāyate mama .. 27 ..
5.19.d:
तत्र गत्वा तिलैस्तैस्त्वं तैः शाकैस्तैः कुशैस्तथा ..
श्राद्धं देहि द्रुतं येन मुक्तिः संजायते मम .. 27 ..
5.19.m: Having gone there, quickly offer a śrāddha with those sesame seeds, / with those greens, and with those kuśa blades, so that my liberation may occur.'

5.19.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa dīnasya dayānvitaḥ..
jagāma tatra yatrā''ste sa vṛkṣaḥ plakṣasaṃjñakaḥ.. 28 ..
5.19.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स दीनस्य दयान्वितः..
जगाम तत्र यत्रा'ऽस्ते स वृक्षः प्लक्षसंज्ञकः.. 28 ..
5.19.m: Having heard those words of that wretched one, filled with compassion, / he went there where that tree called plakṣa stood.

5.19.s:
dṛṣṭvā śākāṃstilāṃstāṃstu darbhāṃstena yathoditān..
akhanattatra deśe ca jalārthe laghu kūpikām .. 29 ..
5.19.d:
दृष्ट्वा शाकांस्तिलांस्तांस्तु दर्भांस्तेन यथोदितान्..
अखनत्तत्र देशे च जलार्थे लघु कूपिकाम् .. 29 ..
5.19.m: Having seen the greens, the sesame seeds, and the darbha grass as described by him, / he dug a small well in that spot for water.

5.19.s:
tataḥ kṛtaghnamuddiśya śrāddhaṃ cakre yathoditam ..
ānīya brāhmaṇāñchreṣṭhānvedavedāṃgapāragān .. 6.19.3. ..
kṛtamātre tataḥ śrāddhe divya rūpadharaḥ pumān..
vimānavaramārūḍho vidūrathamathā'bravīt .. 31 ..
5.19.d:
ततः कृतघ्नमुद्दिश्य श्राद्धं चक्रे यथोदितम् ..
आनीय ब्राह्मणाञ्छ्रेष्ठान्वेदवेदांगपारगान् .. 6.19.3. ..
कृतमात्रे ततः श्राद्धे दिव्य रूपधरः पुमान्..
विमानवरमारूढो विदूरथमथाऽब्रवीत् .. 31 ..
5.19.m: Then, having fetched excellent brahmins who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / he performed the śrāddha as prescribed for the sake of the ungrateful one. / As soon as the śrāddha was performed, a man possessing a divine form, / mounted upon an excellent aerial chariot, then spoke to Vidūratha:

5.19.s:
mukto'haṃ tvatprasādācca pretatvāddāruṇādvibho ..
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tridaśālayam .. 32 ..
5.19.d:
मुक्तोऽहं त्वत्प्रसादाच्च प्रेतत्वाद्दारुणाद्विभो ..
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सांप्रतं त्रिदशालयम् .. 32 ..
5.19.m: 'I am released from the dreadful condition of a ghost through your favor, O lord. / May it be well with you; I shall now go to the abode of the gods.'

5.19.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tataḥ prabhṛti sā tatra kūpikā khyātimāgatā ..
pitṝṇāṃ puṣṭidā nityaṃ gayāśīrṣasamudbhavā.. 33 ..
5.19.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततः प्रभृति सा तत्र कूपिका ख्यातिमागता ..
पितॄणां पुष्टिदा नित्यं गयाशीर्षसमुद्भवा.. 33 ..
5.19.m: Sūta said: / From then on, that small well there became famous / as Gayāśīrṣasamudbhavā, constantly granting nourishment to the ancestors.

5.19.s:
pretapakṣasya darśāyāṃ yastasyāṃ śrāddhamācaret ..
kālaśākena vipreṃdrāstathāraṇyodbhavaistilaiḥ .. 34 ..
5.19.d:
प्रेतपक्षस्य दर्शायां यस्तस्यां श्राद्धमाचरेत् ..
कालशाकेन विप्रेंद्रास्तथारण्योद्भवैस्तिलैः .. 34 ..
5.19.m: Whosoever should perform a śrāddha at it on the new moon of the fortnight of the departed spirits, / O best of brahmins, with kālaśāka and with sesame seeds produced in the forest,

5.19.s:
kṛṃtitaiśca tathā darbhaiḥ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
sa prāpnoti phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kṛtaghnapretatīrthataḥ .. 35 ..
5.19.d:
कृंतितैश्च तथा दर्भैः सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः .
स प्राप्नोति फलं कृत्स्नं कृतघ्नप्रेततीर्थतः .. 35 ..
5.19.m: and with trimmed darbha grass, properly endowed with faith, / he obtains the complete fruit from the sacred ford of the ungrateful ghost.

5.19.s:
agniṣvāttāḥ pitṛgaṇāstathā barhiṣadaśca ye ..
tatra saṃnihitā nityamājyapāḥ somapāstathā .. 36 ..
5.19.d:
अग्निष्वात्ताः पितृगणास्तथा बर्हिषदश्च ये ..
तत्र संनिहिता नित्यमाज्यपाः सोमपास्तथा .. 36 ..
5.19.m: The classes of ancestors—the Agniṣvāttas and the Barhiṣads, / as well as the Ājyapas and the Somapas—are always present there.

5.19.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena śrāddhaṃ tatra samācaret ..
kāle vā
yadi vā'kāle pitṝṇāṃ tuṣṭaye sadā .. 37 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye māṃsādādipretatrayasya vidūrathakṛtaśrāddhadvārā muktidāne pitṛkūpikātīrthamā hātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 19 .. .. cha .. ..
5.19.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन श्राद्धं तत्र समाचरेत् ..
काले वा
यदि वाऽकाले पितॄणां तुष्टये सदा .. 37 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मांसादादिप्रेतत्रयस्य विदूरथकृतश्राद्धद्वारा मुक्तिदाने पितृकूपिकातीर्थमा हात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनविंशोऽध्यायः .. 19 .. .. छ .. ..
5.19.m:
Therefore, one should perform a śrāddha there with every effort, / whether at the prescribed time or outside the prescribed time, always for the satisfaction of the ancestors.
Thus, in the holy Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorification of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, the nineteenth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the māhātmya of the Sacred Ford of Pitṛkūpikā in the Bestowal of Liberation upon the Three Ghosts, Beginning with the Meat-eater, by Means of the Śrāddha Performed by Vidūratha.'

5.20.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatra dāśarathī rāmo vanavāsāya dīkṣitaḥ ..
bhramamāṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe sītālakṣmaṇasaṃyutaḥ .. 1 ..
5.20.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्र दाशरथी रामो वनवासाय दीक्षितः ..
भ्रममाणो धरापृष्ठे सीतालक्ष्मणसंयुतः .. 1 ..
5.20.m: Sūta said: / There, Rāma, son of Daśaratha, consecrated for dwelling in the forest, / wandering over the surface of the earth accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa,

5.20.s:
samā''yāto dvijaśreṣṭhā yatra sā pitṛkūpikā ..
tṛṣārtaśca śramārtaśca niṣasāda dharātale .. 2 ..
5.20.d:
समा'ऽयातो द्विजश्रेष्ठा यत्र सा पितृकूपिका ..
तृषार्तश्च श्रमार्तश्च निषसाद धरातले .. 2 ..
5.20.m: arrived, O best of the twice-born, where that Pitṛkūpikā is. / Afflicted with thirst and exhausted with fatigue, he sat down upon the ground.

5.20.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāpto bhagavāndinanāyakaḥ ..
astācalaṃ japāpuṣpasannibho dvijasattamāḥ .. 3 ..
5.20.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तो भगवान्दिननायकः ..
अस्ताचलं जपापुष्पसन्निभो द्विजसत्तमाः .. 3 ..
5.20.m: In the meantime, the lord sun, / resembling a hibiscus flower, reached the mountain of setting, O best of the twice-born.

5.20.s:
tataḥ plakṣanagādhastātparṇānyāstīrya bhūtale ..
sāyaṃtanaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā suṣvāpa raghunandanaḥ .. 4 ..
5.20.d:
ततः प्लक्षनगाधस्तात्पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले ..
सायंतनं विधिं कृत्वा सुष्वाप रघुनन्दनः .. 4 ..
5.20.m: Then, having spread leaves on the ground beneath the plakṣa tree / and having performed the evening rites, the delight of the Raghu race fell asleep.

5.20.s:
athā'valokayāmāsa svapne daśarathaṃ nṛpam ..
yadvatpūrvaṃ priyā''lāpasaṃsaktaṃ hṛṣṭamānasam .. 5 ..
5.20.d:
अथाऽवलोकयामास स्वप्ने दशरथं नृपम् ..
यद्वत्पूर्वं प्रिया'ऽलापसंसक्तं हृष्टमानसम् .. 5 ..
5.20.m: Then he saw King Daśaratha in a dream, / engaged in pleasant conversation and delighted in mind, just as before.

5.20.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṇḍale ..
viprānāhūya tatsarvaṃ kathayāmāsa rāghavaḥ .. 6 ..
5.20.d:
ततः प्रभाते विमले प्रोद्गते रविमण्डले ..
विप्रानाहूय तत्सर्वं कथयामास राघवः .. 6 ..
5.20.m: Then, at pure dawn, when the orb of the sun had arisen, / Rāghava summoned the brahmins and recounted all of that:

5.20.s:
adya svapne mayā viprāḥ priyālāpaparaḥ pitā ..
atihṛṣṭamanā dṛṣṭaḥ śvetamālyānulepanaḥ .. 7 ..
5.20.d:
अद्य स्वप्ने मया विप्राः प्रियालापपरः पिता ..
अतिहृष्टमना दृष्टः श्वेतमाल्यानुलेपनः .. 7 ..
5.20.m: 'Today in a dream, O brahmins, my father was seen by me, / intent on pleasant conversation, with a very cheerful mind, wearing white garlands and ointments.

5.20.s:
tatkīdṛkpariṇāmo'sya svapnasya dvijasattamāḥ ..
bhaviṣyati prajalpadhvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ yataḥ .. 8 .. ..
5.20.d:
तत्कीदृक्परिणामोऽस्य स्वप्नस्य द्विजसत्तमाः ..
भविष्यति प्रजल्पध्वं परं कौतूहलं यतः .. 8 .. ..
5.20.m: What will be the outcome of this dream, O best of the twice-born? / Tell me, since I have supreme curiosity.'

5.20.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
pitaraḥ śrāddhakāmā ye vṛddhiṃ paśyaṃti vā nṛpa ..
te svapne darśanaṃ yāṃti putrāṇāmiti naḥ śrutam .. 9 ..
5.20.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
पितरः श्राद्धकामा ये वृद्धिं पश्यंति वा नृप ..
ते स्वप्ने दर्शनं यांति पुत्राणामिति नः श्रुतम् .. 9 ..
5.20.m: The brahmins said: / 'The ancestors who desire a śrāddha, or who see prosperity, O king, / appear in the dreams of their sons: so it has been heard by us.'

5.20.s:
tadasyāṃ kūpikāyāṃ ca svayameva gayā sthitā ..
tena tvayā pitā dṛṣṭaḥ svapne śrāddhasya vāṃchakaḥ .. 6.20.10 ..
5.20.d:
तदस्यां कूपिकायां च स्वयमेव गया स्थिता ..
तेन त्वया पिता दृष्टः स्वप्ने श्राद्धस्य वांछकः .. 6.20.10 ..
5.20.m: Therefore, Gayā herself resides in this small well; / because of that, you saw your father in a dream desiring a śrāddha.

5.20.s:
tasmātkuru raghuśreṣṭha śrāddhamatra yathoditam ..
nīvāraiḥ śāka mūlaiśca tathā'raṇyodbhavaistilaiḥ .. 11 ..
5.20.d:
तस्मात्कुरु रघुश्रेष्ठ श्राद्धमत्र यथोदितम् ..
नीवारैः शाक मूलैश्च तथाऽरण्योद्भवैस्तिलैः .. 11 ..
5.20.m: Therefore, best of the Raghus, perform the śrāddha here as prescribed, / with wild rice, vegetables, roots, and wild sesame seeds.

5.20.s:
athaivāmantrayāmāsa tānviprānraghusattamaḥ ..
śrāddheṣu śraddhayā yuktaḥ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti .. 12 ..
5.20.d:
अथैवामन्त्रयामास तान्विप्रान्रघुसत्तमः ..
श्राद्धेषु श्रद्धया युक्तः प्रसादः क्रियतामिति .. 12 ..
5.20.m: Then the best of the Raghus invited those brahmins / for the śrāddha rites, endowed with faith, saying, “Please grant your favor.”

5.20.s:
bāḍhamityeva te coktvā snānārthaṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
gatāḥ sarve susaṃhṛṣṭā svakīyānāśramānprati va 13 ..
5.20.d:
बाढमित्येव ते चोक्त्वा स्नानार्थं द्विजसत्तमाः ..
गताः सर्वे सुसंहृष्टा स्वकीयानाश्रमान्प्रति व 13 ..
5.20.m: Saying, “Very well,” all those best among brahmins, / exceedingly delighted, went to their own hermitages for their ritual ablution.

5.20.s:
atha teṣu prayāteṣu brāhmaṇeṣu raghūttamaḥ ..
provāca lakṣmaṇaṃ pārśve vinayāvanataṃ sthitam .. 14 ..
5.20.d:
अथ तेषु प्रयातेषु ब्राह्मणेषु रघूत्तमः ..
प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणं पार्श्वे विनयावनतं स्थितम् .. 14 ..
5.20.m: Then, when those brahmins had departed, the best of the Raghus / spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who was standing beside him bowed down in humility:

5.20.s:
śākamūlaphalānyāśu śrāddhārthaṃ samupānaya ..
saumitrānaya vaidehī svayaṃ pacati bhāminī .. 15 ..
5.20.d:
शाकमूलफलान्याशु श्राद्धार्थं समुपानय ..
सौमित्रानय वैदेही स्वयं पचति भामिनी .. 15 ..
5.20.m: “Quickly bring vegetables, roots, and fruits for the śrāddha; / bring them, son of Sumitrā; the noble Vaidehī will cook them herself.”

5.20.s:
tacchrutvā lakṣmaṇastūrṇaṃ jagāmā'raṇyameva hi ..
śrāddhārthamānināyā''śu phalāni vividhāni ca .. 16 ..
5.20.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्तूर्णं जगामाऽरण्यमेव हि ..
श्राद्धार्थमानिनाया'ऽशु फलानि विविधानि च .. 16 ..
5.20.m: Hearing that, Lakṣmaṇa went quickly to the forest; / he swiftly brought various fruits for the sake of the śrāddha:

5.20.s:
dhātrīphalāni cā''mrāṇi cirbhaṭānīṃ gudāni ca ..
karīrāṇi kapitthāni tathaivā'nyāni bhūriśaḥ .. 17 ..
5.20.d:
धात्रीफलानि चा'ऽम्राणि चिर्भटानीं गुदानि च ..
करीराणि कपित्थानि तथैवाऽन्यानि भूरिशः .. 17 ..
5.20.m: āmalakī fruits, mangoes, cirbhaṭa fruits, and iṅgudas, / karīra fruits, wood-apples, and many others as well.

5.20.s:
tataśca pācayāmāsa tadarthe janakodbhavā ..
rāmādeśātsvayaṃ sādhvī vinayena samanvitā .. 18 ..
5.20.d:
ततश्च पाचयामास तदर्थे जनकोद्भवा ..
रामादेशात्स्वयं साध्वी विनयेन समन्विता .. 18 ..
5.20.m: Then, for that purpose, Janaka's daughter, / by Rāma's command, the virtuous woman, full of humility, cooked [them] herself.

5.20.s:
tataśca kutape prāpte kāle te dvijasattamāḥ ..
kṛtāhnikāḥ samāyātā rāmabhaktisamanvitāḥ .. 19 ..
5.20.d:
ततश्च कुतपे प्राप्ते काले ते द्विजसत्तमाः ..
कृताह्निकाः समायाता रामभक्तिसमन्विताः .. 19 ..
5.20.m: And then, when the kutapa hour had arrived, those best among brahmins, / having performed their daily rites, arrived, endowed with devotion to Rāma.

5.20.s:
etasminnaṃtare sītā plakṣavṛkṣāṃtare sthitā..
ātmānaṃ gopayāmāsa yathā vetti na rāghavaḥ..6.20.20
sa tāṃ sīteti sīteti vyāhṛtyātha muhurmuhuḥ..
strīdharmiṇīti matvā tu lakṣmaṇaṃ cedamabravīt .. 21 ..
5.20.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सीता प्लक्षवृक्षांतरे स्थिता..
आत्मानं गोपयामास यथा वेत्ति न राघवः..6.20.20
स तां सीतेति सीतेति व्याहृत्याथ मुहुर्मुहुः..
स्त्रीधर्मिणीति मत्वा तु लक्ष्मणं चेदमब्रवीत् .. 21 ..
5.20.m: Meanwhile, Sītā stood behind a plakṣa tree / and concealed herself so that the descendant of Raghu would not know. / Calling out to her again and again, “Sītā! Sītā!”, / and thinking she had her monthly period, he said this to Lakṣmaṇa:

5.20.s:
vatsa lakṣmaṇa śuśrūṣāṃ viprāṇāṃ śrāddhasaṃbhavām..
pādaprakṣālanādyāṃ tvaṃ yathāvatkartumarhasi .. 22 ..
5.20.d:
वत्स लक्ष्मण शुश्रूषां विप्राणां श्राद्धसंभवाम्..
पादप्रक्षालनाद्यां त्वं यथावत्कर्तुमर्हसि .. 22 ..
5.20.m: “Dear Lakṣmaṇa, you should duly perform / the service for the brahmins required for the śrāddha, beginning with washing their feet.”

5.20.s:
bāḍhamityeva saṃprokto lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ ..
cakre sarvaṃ tathā karma yathā nārī vicakṣaṇā .. 23 ..
5.20.d:
बाढमित्येव संप्रोक्तो लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः ..
चक्रे सर्वं तथा कर्म यथा नारी विचक्षणा .. 23 ..
5.20.m: Addressed with “Very well,” Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with auspicious marks, / performed all that duty just as an experienced woman would.

5.20.s:
tato nirvartite śrāddhe brāhmaṇeṣu gateṣvatha ..
janakasya sutā sādhvī tatkṣaṇātsamupasthitā .. 24 ..
5.20.d:
ततो निर्वर्तिते श्राद्धे ब्राह्मणेषु गतेष्वथ ..
जनकस्य सुता साध्वी तत्क्षणात्समुपस्थिता .. 24 ..
5.20.m: Then, when the śrāddha was concluded and the brahmins had left, / Janaka's virtuous daughter appeared that very instant.

5.20.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītāṃ kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ ..
provāca paruṣairvākyairbhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ.. 25 ..
5.20.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा राघवः सीतां कोपसंरक्तलोचनः ..
प्रोवाच परुषैर्वाक्यैर्भर्त्समानो मुहुर्मुहुः.. 25 ..
5.20.m: Seeing Sītā, the descendant of Raghu, his eyes red with anger, / spoke with harsh words, rebuking her repeatedly:

5.20.s:
āyāteṣu dvijāteṣu śrāddhakāla upasthite ..
kva gatā vada pāpe tvaṃ māṃ parityajya dūrataḥ .. 26 ..
5.20.d:
आयातेषु द्विजातेषु श्राद्धकाल उपस्थिते ..
क्व गता वद पापे त्वं मां परित्यज्य दूरतः .. 26 ..
5.20.m: “When the twice-born arrived and the time for śrāddha was at hand, / where did you go, tell me, wicked woman, abandoning me from afar?

5.20.s:
naitadyuktaṃ kulastrīṇāṃ viśeṣādatra kānane ..
vihartuṃ dūrataḥ śūnye tasmāttyājyā'si maithili .. 27 ..
5.20.d:
नैतद्युक्तं कुलस्त्रीणां विशेषादत्र कानने ..
विहर्तुं दूरतः शून्ये तस्मात्त्याज्याऽसि मैथिलि .. 27 ..
5.20.m: It is not proper for women of noble family, especially here in the forest, / to roam far away in an empty place; therefore, you deserve to be abandoned, Maithilī!”

5.20.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhītā sā janakodbhavā ..
uvāca vepamānāṃgī praskhalaṃtyā girā tataḥ .. 28 ..
5.20.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भीता सा जनकोद्भवा ..
उवाच वेपमानांगी प्रस्खलंत्या गिरा ततः .. 28 ..
5.20.m: Hearing that speech of his, the frightened daughter of Janaka, / her limbs trembling, then spoke with a faltering voice:

5.20.s:
na māmarhasi kārye'smingarhituṃ raghusattama ..
yasmādahamatikrāntā sthānādasmācchraṇuṣva tat .. 29 ..
5.20.d:
न मामर्हसि कार्येऽस्मिन्गर्हितुं रघुसत्तम ..
यस्मादहमतिक्रान्ता स्थानादस्माच्छ्रणुष्व तत् .. 29 ..
5.20.m: “You ought not to reproach me in this matter, best of the Raghus. / Hear the reason why I went away from this place:

5.20.s:
pitā tava mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sākṣāddaśarathaḥ svayam ..
brāhmaṇasya śarīrastho dvitīyaśca pitāmahaḥ .. 6.20.30 ..
5.20.d:
पिता तव मया दृष्टः साक्षाद्दशरथः स्वयम् ..
ब्राह्मणस्य शरीरस्थो द्वितीयश्च पितामहः .. 6.20.30 ..
5.20.m: I saw your father, Daśaratha himself in person, / residing in the body of a brahmin, and your grandfather in the second;

5.20.s:
pituḥ pitāmaho'nyasya tṛtīyasya raghūttama ..
trayāṇāṃ ca tathānyeṣāṃ trayo'nye nṛpasaṃnibhāḥ .. 31 ..
5.20.d:
पितुः पितामहोऽन्यस्य तृतीयस्य रघूत्तम ..
त्रयाणां च तथान्येषां त्रयोऽन्ये नृपसंनिभाः .. 31 ..
5.20.m: in another, the third, [I saw] the father’s grandfather, best of the Raghus; / and in three other [brahmins I saw] three others resembling kings;

5.20.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ mayā dṛṣṭāḥ śarīrasthāḥ suharṣitāḥ ..
mātāmahānahaṃ manye tānapi trīnahaṃ sphuṭam .. 32 ..
5.20.d:
ब्राह्मणानां मया दृष्टाः शरीरस्थाः सुहर्षिताः ..
मातामहानहं मन्ये तानपि त्रीनहं स्फुटम् .. 32 ..
5.20.m: I saw them residing in the bodies of the brahmins, greatly delighted; / I distinctly recognized them also as the three maternal grandfathers.

5.20.s:
tato 'haṃ lajjayā naṣṭā dṛṣṭvā śvaśurasaṃgamān ..
yena bhuktāni bhojyāni purā mṛṣṭānyanekaśaḥ .. 33 ..
5.20.d:
ततो ऽहं लज्जया नष्टा दृष्ट्वा श्वशुरसंगमान् ..
येन भुक्तानि भोज्यानि पुरा मृष्टान्यनेकशः .. 33 ..
5.20.m: Then I fled out of shame upon seeing the presence of my father-in-law. / By him sweet delicacies were formerly eaten manifold;

5.20.s:
tathā khādyāni lehyāni coṣyāṇi ca viśeṣataḥ ..
pitā tava kathaṃ so'dya kaṣāyāṇi kaṭūni ca ..
bhakṣayiṣyati dattāni svahastena mayā vibho .. 34 ..
5.20.d:
तथा खाद्यानि लेह्यानि चोष्याणि च विशेषतः ..
पिता तव कथं सोऽद्य कषायाणि कटूनि च ..
भक्षयिष्यति दत्तानि स्वहस्तेन मया विभो .. 34 ..
5.20.m: so too solid foods, lickable foods, and suckable foods especially. / How could he, your father, today eat the bitter and astringent [foods] / offered with my own hand, O Lord?

5.20.s:
etasmātkāraṇānnaṣṭā tvatsamīpādahaṃ vibho ..
śrāddhakāle'pi saṃprāpte satyenātmānamālabhe .. 358 ..
tacchrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭātmā rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ ..
sādhusādhviti tāṃ prāha pariṣvajya muhurmuhuḥ .. 36 ..
tato bhuktvā svayaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇena samanvitaḥ ..
sāyāhne samanuprāpte saṃdhyākāryaṃ vidhāya ca .. 37 ..
provāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vatsa parṇānyāstīrya bhūtale ..
śayyāṃ kuru samānīya pādaśaucāya sajjalam .. 38 ..
tataḥ kopaparītātmā saumitriḥ prāha rāghavam ..
nāhaṃ śayyāṃ kariṣyāmi pādaprakṣālanaṃ na ca .. 39 ..
tathā'nyadapi yatkiṃcitkarma svalpamapi prabho ..
tvāṃ vā tyaktvā gamiṣyāmi kutracitpīḍito bhṛśam.. .. 6.20.40 ..
preṣyatvena raghuśreṣṭha satyametanmayoditam ..
sītāyāḥ kiṃ samādeśyaṃ na kiṃcitsaṃprayacchasi ..
api svalpataraṃ rāma mayā tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi .. 41 ..
5.20.d:
एतस्मात्कारणान्नष्टा त्वत्समीपादहं विभो ..
श्राद्धकालेऽपि संप्राप्ते सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. 358 ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा संप्रहृष्टात्मा रामो राजीवलोचनः ..
साधुसाध्विति तां प्राह परिष्वज्य मुहुर्मुहुः .. 36 ..
ततो भुक्त्वा स्वयं रामो लक्ष्मणेन समन्वितः ..
सायाह्ने समनुप्राप्ते संध्याकार्यं विधाय च .. 37 ..
प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणं वत्स पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले ..
शय्यां कुरु समानीय पादशौचाय सज्जलम् .. 38 ..
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा सौमित्रिः प्राह राघवम् ..
नाहं शय्यां करिष्यामि पादप्रक्षालनं न च .. 39 ..
तथाऽन्यदपि यत्किंचित्कर्म स्वल्पमपि प्रभो ..
त्वां वा त्यक्त्वा गमिष्यामि कुत्रचित्पीडितो भृशम्.. .. 6.20.40 ..
प्रेष्यत्वेन रघुश्रेष्ठ सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ..
सीतायाः किं समादेश्यं न किंचित्संप्रयच्छसि ..
अपि स्वल्पतरं राम मया त्वं किं करिष्यसि .. 41 ..
5.20.m:
For this reason I fled from your presence, O Lord, / even when the time of the śrāddha arrived. I swear by the truth.”
Hearing that, Rāma, lotus-eyed, his heart delighted, / embraced her again and again, saying to her, “Well done! Well done!”
Then, having eaten himself along with Lakṣmaṇa, / when evening arrived and having performed the evening twilight rites,
he spoke to Lakṣmaṇa: “Dear boy, spread leaves upon the ground, / make a bed, and bring water for washing the feet.”
Then, overcome with anger, the son of Sumitrā said to the descendant of Raghu: / “I will not make a bed, nor will I wash your feet,
nor any other task, even the slightest, O Lord! / Or else, abandoning you, I will go somewhere, exceedingly distressed,
as a servant, best of the Raghus; this is the truth spoken by me. / Why do you not give even a single order to Sītā, / even the smallest, Rāma? What will you do with me?”

5.20.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vikṛtaṃ cāpi rāghavaḥ ..
tūṣṇīṃ babhūva medhāvī hāsyaṃ kṛtvā manāktataḥ .. 42 ..
tataḥ svayaṃ samutthāya kṛtvā svā starakaṃ śubham ..
sītayā kṣālitāṃghristu suṣvāpa tadanaṃtaram .. 43 ..
lakṣmaṇo'pi vidūrasthaḥ kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ ..
vṛkṣamūlaṃ samāśritya suptaścitte vyaciṃtayat .. 44 ..
hatvainaṃ rāghavaṃ suptaṃ sītāṃ patnīṃ vidhāya ca..
kiṃ gacchāmi nijaṃ sthānaṃ videśaṃ vā'pidūrataḥ .. 45 ..
evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya bahudhā lakṣmaṇasya sā ..
vyatikrāṃtā niśā viprāḥ kṛcchreṇa mahatā tataḥ .. 46 ..
na tasya niścayo jajñe tasminkṛtye kathaṃcana ..
kopātpraṇaṣṭanidrasya soṣṇaṃ niḥśvasato muhuḥ .. 47 ..
tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyaḥ ..
rāmaḥ sītāṃ samādāya prasthito dakṣiṇāṃ diśam.. 48 ..
5.20.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विकृतं चापि राघवः ..
तूष्णीं बभूव मेधावी हास्यं कृत्वा मनाक्ततः .. 42 ..
ततः स्वयं समुत्थाय कृत्वा स्वा स्तरकं शुभम् ..
सीतया क्षालितांघ्रिस्तु सुष्वाप तदनंतरम् .. 43 ..
लक्ष्मणोऽपि विदूरस्थः कोपसंरक्तलोचनः ..
वृक्षमूलं समाश्रित्य सुप्तश्चित्ते व्यचिंतयत् .. 44 ..
हत्वैनं राघवं सुप्तं सीतां पत्नीं विधाय च..
किं गच्छामि निजं स्थानं विदेशं वाऽपिदूरतः .. 45 ..
एवं चिंतयतस्तस्य बहुधा लक्ष्मणस्य सा ..
व्यतिक्रांता निशा विप्राः कृच्छ्रेण महता ततः .. 46 ..
न तस्य निश्चयो जज्ञे तस्मिन्कृत्ये कथंचन ..
कोपात्प्रणष्टनिद्रस्य सोष्णं निःश्वसतो मुहुः .. 47 ..
ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः ..
रामः सीतां समादाय प्रस्थितो दक्षिणां दिशम्.. 48 ..
5.20.m:
Hearing that distorted speech of his, the wise descendant of Raghu / smiled slightly and then fell silent.
Then, having risen himself and made a lovely bed of his own, / his feet were washed by Sītā, and thereafter he slept.
Lakṣmaṇa too, staying far away, his eyes red with anger, / slept resting at the foot of a tree, and thought in his mind:
“Having killed this sleeping descendant of Raghu and making Sītā my wife, / shall I go to my own place or far away to a foreign land?”
While he was reflecting thus in many ways, O brahmins, / that night passed for Lakṣmaṇa with great difficulty.
No resolve was born in him concerning that deed in any way, / as his sleep was destroyed by rage and he sighed warmly again and again.
Then at clear dawn, having performed his morning rites, / Rāma took Sītā and set out toward the southern direction.

5.20.s:
lakṣmaṇo'pi dhanuḥ sajyaṃ kṛtvā saṃdhāya sāyakam ..
anuvrajati pṛṣṭhasthastasya cchidraṃ vilokayan .. 49 ..
tato gokarṇamāsādya praṇamya ca maheśvaram ..
pratasthe rāghavo yāvatsaumitristāvadāgataḥ .. 6.20.50 ..
bāṣpaparyākulākṣaśca vrīḍayā'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ ..
praṇamya śirasā rāmaṃ tataḥ prāha suduḥ khitaḥ .. 51 ..
kuru me nigrahaṃ nātha svāmidrohasamudbhavam ..
atipāpasya duṣṭasya kṛtaghnasya raghūttama .. 52..
uttarāṇi viruddhāni tava dattāni bhūriśaḥ ..
mayā vinā'parādhena vadhopāyaśca ciṃtitaḥ .. 53 ..
tataśca taṃ pariṣvajya rāmo'pi nijabāṃdhavam ..
bāṣpaklinnamukhaḥ prāha kṣāṃtaṃ vatsa mayā tava .. 54 ..
na te tvanyaḥ priyaḥ kaścinmāṃ muktvā vedmyahaṃ sphuṭam..
tasmādāgaccha gacchāmo mārgaṃ velādhikā bhavet ..55..
5.20.d:
लक्ष्मणोऽपि धनुः सज्यं कृत्वा संधाय सायकम् ..
अनुव्रजति पृष्ठस्थस्तस्य च्छिद्रं विलोकयन् .. 49 ..
ततो गोकर्णमासाद्य प्रणम्य च महेश्वरम् ..
प्रतस्थे राघवो यावत्सौमित्रिस्तावदागतः .. 6.20.50 ..
बाष्पपर्याकुलाक्षश्च व्रीडयाऽधोमुखः स्थितः ..
प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं ततः प्राह सुदुः खितः .. 51 ..
कुरु मे निग्रहं नाथ स्वामिद्रोहसमुद्भवम् ..
अतिपापस्य दुष्टस्य कृतघ्नस्य रघूत्तम .. 52..
उत्तराणि विरुद्धानि तव दत्तानि भूरिशः ..
मया विनाऽपराधेन वधोपायश्च चिंतितः .. 53 ..
ततश्च तं परिष्वज्य रामोऽपि निजबांधवम् ..
बाष्पक्लिन्नमुखः प्राह क्षांतं वत्स मया तव .. 54 ..
न ते त्वन्यः प्रियः कश्चिन्मां मुक्त्वा वेद्म्यहं स्फुटम्..
तस्मादागच्छ गच्छामो मार्गं वेलाधिका भवेत् ..55..
5.20.m:
Lakṣmaṇa too, stringing his bow and fixing an arrow, / followed behind him, looking for an opportunity [to strike] him.
Then, having reached Gokarṇa and bowed down to the Great Lord, / as the descendant of Raghu set out, the son of Sumitrā approached.
His eyes bewildered with tears, standing with his face cast down in shame, / he bowed down with his head to Rāma and then spoke, deeply sorrowful:
“Inflict punishment upon me, O Lord, arising from betrayal of my master, / for I am a great sinner, wicked and ungrateful, O best of the Raghus!”
I gave you countless hostile replies, / and without any fault on your part, I devised a means to kill you. (53)
Then Rāma embraced his own brother, / and with his face wet with tears said: “Dear boy, I have forgiven you. (54)
For I know clearly that no one is dearer to you than me. / Therefore come, let us go on our way, lest the hour grow late.” (55)

5.20.s:
.. lakṣmaṇa uvāca .. ..
yadi me nigrahaṃ nātha na kariṣyasi sāṃpratam ..
prāṇatyāgaṃ kariṣyāmi vahnāvātmaviśuddhaye.. 56 ..
rāmalakṣmaṇayorevaṃ vadatostatra kānane ..
ājagāma muniśreṣṭho mārkaṃḍa iti yaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 57 ..
tataḥ praṇamya taṃ rāmaḥ sītālakṣmaṇasaṃyutaḥ ..
provāca svāgataṃ testu kutaḥ prāpto'si sanmune .. 58 .. ..
.. mārkaṃḍeya uvāca .. ..
prabhāsādahamāyātaḥ sāṃprataṃ raghunaṃdana ..
svamāśramaṃ gamiṣyāmi kṣetre'traiva vyavasthitam .. 59..
mayā rāghava tatrā'sti sthāpitaḥ prapitāmahaḥ ..
tasyā'dya divase yātrā bahuśreyaḥpradā smṛtā .. 6.20.60 ..
tasmāttvamapi tatraiva tūrṇameva mayā saha ..
mamāśramapade sthitvā paśya devaṃ pitāmaham .. 61 ..
yena syāḥ sarvaśatrūṇāmagamyastvaṃ raghūdvaha ..
jyeṣṭhapañcadaśīyoge jyeṣṭhaputraḥ samāhitaḥ .. 62 ..
5.20.d:
.. लक्ष्मण उवाच .. ..
यदि मे निग्रहं नाथ न करिष्यसि सांप्रतम् ..
प्राणत्यागं करिष्यामि वह्नावात्मविशुद्धये.. 56 ..
रामलक्ष्मणयोरेवं वदतोस्तत्र कानने ..
आजगाम मुनिश्रेष्ठो मार्कंड इति यः स्मृतः .. 57 ..
ततः प्रणम्य तं रामः सीतालक्ष्मणसंयुतः ..
प्रोवाच स्वागतं तेस्तु कुतः प्राप्तोऽसि सन्मुने .. 58 .. ..
.. मार्कंडेय उवाच .. ..
प्रभासादहमायातः सांप्रतं रघुनंदन ..
स्वमाश्रमं गमिष्यामि क्षेत्रेऽत्रैव व्यवस्थितम् .. 59..
मया राघव तत्राऽस्ति स्थापितः प्रपितामहः ..
तस्याऽद्य दिवसे यात्रा बहुश्रेयःप्रदा स्मृता .. 6.20.60 ..
तस्मात्त्वमपि तत्रैव तूर्णमेव मया सह ..
ममाश्रमपदे स्थित्वा पश्य देवं पितामहम् .. 61 ..
येन स्याः सर्वशत्रूणामगम्यस्त्वं रघूद्वह ..
ज्येष्ठपञ्चदशीयोगे ज्येष्ठपुत्रः समाहितः .. 62 ..
5.20.m:
Lakṣmaṇa said: / “Lord, if you do not punish me now, / I will abandon my life in fire for the purification of my soul.” (56)
While Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa were speaking thus in that forest, / there arrived the foremost sage known as Mārkaṇḍa. (57)
Then Rāma, bowing to him together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, / said: “Welcome to you! Whence have you come, good sage?” (58)
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “I have come now from Prabhāsa, O son of Raghu; / I am going to my own hermitage situated right here in this sacred field. (59)
By me, O scion of Raghu, the Great-Grandfather was established there; / a pilgrimage to him on this day is remembered as bestowing great welfare. (60)
Therefore you too, quickly along with me, / having halted at the precinct of my hermitage, behold the god, the Grandfather, (61)
so that you may become unassailable to all your enemies, O upholder of Raghu’s line! / An eldest son who is collected in mind during the conjunction of the fifteenth day of Jyeṣṭha, (62)

5.20.s:
yastatra kurute snānaṃ tasya mṛtyubhayaṃ kutaḥ ..
sā'dya paṃcadaśī rāma jyeṣṭhamāsasamudbhavā ..
jyeṣṭhānakṣatrasaṃyuktā tasmātsnātuṃ tvamarhasi .. 63 ..
tataḥ saṃprasthitaṃ rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca lakṣmaṇaḥ ..
kuru me nigrahaṃ tāvadgaccha tīrthaṃ tataḥ prabho .. 64 ..
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
sthite'sminmuniśārdūle samīpe vatsa lakṣmaṇa ..
anarhā niṣkṛtiḥ kartuṃ tasmādenaṃ prayācaya .. 65 ..
.. lakṣmaṇa uvāca .. ..
svāmidrohe kṛte brahmanprāyaścittaṃ yadīkṣyate ..
tanme dehi sphuṭaṃ yena kāyaśuddhiḥ prajāyate .. 66 ..
.. mārkaṃḍeya uvāca .. ..
mamā''śramasamīpe'sti sutīrthaṃ bālamaṃḍanam ..
svāmidroharatāḥ snātā mucyaṃte tatra pātakaiḥ .. 67 ...
tatra śakro vipāpmābhūddhatvā garbhaṃ diteḥ purā ..
viśvastāyā viśeṣeṇa mātuḥ kākutsthasattama ..
tasmāttatra drutaṃ gatvā snānaṃ kuru mahāmate .. 68 ..
5.20.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते स्नानं तस्य मृत्युभयं कुतः ..
साऽद्य पंचदशी राम ज्येष्ठमाससमुद्भवा ..
ज्येष्ठानक्षत्रसंयुक्ता तस्मात्स्नातुं त्वमर्हसि .. 63 ..
ततः संप्रस्थितं रामं दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणः ..

who performs ritual ablution there—whence could he have fear of death? / Today is that fifteenth day belonging to the month of Jyeṣṭha, / conjoined with the Jyeṣṭhā lunar mansion; therefore it is fitting that you bathe.” (63)
Then, seeing Rāma set out, Lakṣmaṇa said: / “Inflict punishment on me first, O Lord, and only then proceed to the sacred ford.” (64)
Rāma said: / “Dear Lakṣmaṇa, while this tiger among sages stands near, / it is inappropriate to perform expiation [without him]; therefore petition him.” (65)
Lakṣmaṇa said: / “O brahmin, if any expiation is seen for treachery committed against one's master, / grant it to me clearly, so that bodily purification may arise.” (66)
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “Near my hermitage is an excellent sacred ford called Bālamaṇḍana; / those who have engaged in treachery to their master, having bathed there, are freed from their sins. (67)
There Indra became free of sin after killing the fetus of Diti of old, / the mother who had placed special trust [in him], O best of the Kakutsthas. / Therefore, go there quickly and perform ritual ablution, O highly intelligent one. (68)

5.20.m:
Then you will be freed from the sin born of treachery against your master. / Furthermore, you have no fault, for the sin was committed only in the mind. (69)
It is purified by remorse of mind; this is the view of the wise. / Since the treachery was committed by you only mentally on account of Rāma, (70)
and on account of such mental remorse, therefore you are pure, Lakṣmaṇa! / Furthermore, hear my word: there is no fault in you, sinless one. (71)
Such is the power of this sacred field: it is devoid of fraternal love. / Those who dwell here in this sacred field of five krośas, O Lakṣmaṇa, (72)
not even the slightest fraternal affection ever arises among them. (73)
A mortal is devoted to affection and speaks gently only so long / as he does not touch with his feet the sacred field born of Camatkāra. (74)
The other cattle, birds, and wild beasts that dwell here / are also devoid of goodwill and harbor rivalry toward one another. (75)
No one has affection toward anyone else at all. / Therefore you have no fault; such is the state of this sacred field. (76)

5.20.m:
Even so, if any doubt remains in your mind, / go and perform ritual ablution in that very auspicious sacred ford (77)
where Indra became free of sin after committing dreadful treachery / born of causing the miscarriage of the trusting Diti of old.” (78)
Addressed thus, the son of Sumitrā went there, O best of brahmins, / and from ritual ablution in that sacred ford frequented by Śakra, he became purified. / Rāma too went swiftly to Mārkaṇḍeya's excellent hermitage; (79)
having performed ritual ablution according to rule, he then beheld the Grandfather. / Then, accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, he set out in the southern direction. (80)
Through its power, he then slew the best of rākṣasas beginning with Khara, / and likewise the fierce Rāvaṇa together with Meghanāda. (83)
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, named “Description of the Māhātmya of the Bālamaṇḍana Sacred Ford on the Occasion of Rāma's Departure for the Southern Direction,” in the māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the sixth section of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.
